FWP 1 anthropicpbc-fwpjapanamend.htm FWP Anthropic, PBC- FWP (Japan Amendment)
Issuer Free Writing Prospectus dated November 11, 2026
Filed Pursuant to Rule 433
Relating to Preliminary Prospectus dated November 10, 2026
Registration File No. 333-299633
This free writing prospectus relates to the initial public offering of Class A common stock of Anthropic, PBC (“Anthropic”). On November 10, 2026, Anthropic filed Amendment No. 2 to its Registration Statement on Form S-1 (File No. 333-299633) (“Amendment No. 2”) with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”). Amendment No. 2 and a copy of the preliminary prospectus dated November 10, 2026 relating to this offering may be accessed through the following link:
https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026072484/anthropicpbc-sx1ax2.htm
On November 11, 2026, Anthropic filed a Japanese amended securities registration statement relating to the initial public offering of shares of Class A common stock in Japan with the Kanto Regional Finance Bureau, including a prospectus, a copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit A. This document is an English translation of the Japanese-language prospectus of Anthropic filed in Japan on November 11, 2026 in connection with a public offering in Japan of the Class A common stock of Anthropic.
Anthropic has filed a registration statement (including a prospectus) with the SEC for the offering to which this communication relates. Before you invest, you should read the prospectus in that registration statement and other documents Anthropic has filed with the SEC for more complete information about Anthropic and this offering. You may get these documents for free by visiting EDGAR on the SEC Web site at www.sec.gov. Alternatively, copies of the preliminary prospectus may be obtained from: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 200 West Street, New York, NY 10282, by telephone at (866) 471-2526, or by email at prospectus-ny@ny.email.gs.com; or Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 180 Varick Street, 2nd Floor, New York, NY 10014.

The price range will be from US$70.00 (11,057.90 yen) to US$78.00 (12,321.66 yen) (the “Initial Preliminary Price Range”). The offering price is scheduled to be determined on the Pricing Date, taking into comprehensive consideration factors such as investor demand during the book-building process, as well as stock price fluctuation risks up to the listing date. However, depending on factors such as investor demand in the book-building process for this Offering, the results of the roadshow, or changes in the macroeconomic environment, in accordance with current U.S. market practices, the Initial Preliminary Price Range may be revised prior to the Pricing Date, without limitation as to the upper or lower end of the range (the terms presented upon such a revision shall be referred to as the “Revised Preliminary Price Range”). The Initial Preliminary Price Range, the Revised Preliminary Price Range and the offering price for the Japanese Primary Offering will be identical to the Initial Preliminary Price Range, the Revised Preliminary Price Range and the offering price for the Shares in this Offering. Please also note that the method for determining the offering price in this Offering differs from the typical method used in Japan for IPOs. First, (i) unlike typical IPOs in Japan, in this Offering, the Initial Preliminary Price Range may be revised prior to the Pricing Date, as described above. Second, (ii) in determining the offering price in this Offering, in accordance with current market practice in the United States, the offering price may be set at a price higher than the upper end or lower than the lower end of the Initial Preliminary Price Range or any Revised Preliminary Price Range. Accordingly, the offering price may be determined outside the range of the Initial Preliminary Price Range or any Revised Preliminary Price Range without prior notice or amendment to this document. However, even in the case described in (ii) above, the offering price will be set such that, at a minimum, the product of (x) the offering price so determined multiplied by (y) the Total Number of Shares does not fall below an amount equal to (a) the product of the lower end of the Initial Preliminary Price Range (or, if subsequently revised, the Revised Preliminary Price Range) multiplied by the Total Number of Shares indicated together with such Price Range, minus (b) 20% of an amount equal to the product of the upper end of the Initial Preliminary Price Range (or, if subsequently revised, the Revised Preliminary Price Range) multiplied by the Total Number of Shares indicated together with such Price Range. Based on the Initial Preliminary Price Range and the Total Number of Shares set forth in this document, the aggregate offering price will be at least US$51,612,000,000 (8,153,147,640,000 yen). In addition, with respect to any increase in the offering price at the time of pricing, so long as the Total Number of Shares for this Offering so determined does not exceed the Total Number of Shares indicated together with the Initial Preliminary Price Range (or, if subsequently revised, the Revised Preliminary Price Range), the offering price will not exceed the upper limit of the Initial Preliminary Price Range (or, if subsequently revised, the Revised Preliminary Price Range) plus an amount up to twice the lower limit of the range. Based on the Initial Preliminary Price Range and the Total Number of Shares set forth in this document, the aggregate offering price in such case will be capped at US$206,827,500,000 (32,672,540,175,000 yen). However, if the Total Number of Shares for this Offering so determined exceeds the Total Number of Shares indicated together with the Initial Preliminary Price Range (or, if subsequently revised, the Revised Preliminary Price Range), the offering price will be set such that, at a maximum, the product of (x) the offering price so determined multiplied by (y) the increased Total Number of Shares

 
5 does not exceed 120% of the product of the upper end of the Initial Preliminary Price Range (or, if subsequently revised, the Revised Preliminary Price Range) multiplied by the Total Number of Shares indicated together with such Price Range. The method of selling the Shares by Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd. through face-to-face sales is as follows. During the period from November 11, 2026 (Japan time) until the Pricing Date, investors may submit indications of interest to Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd., with reference to the Initial Preliminary Price Range or the Revised Preliminary Price Range. Such indications of interest may be changed or withdrawn. Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd. will endeavor to conduct sales in a fair manner and intends to conduct distribution in accordance with its basic policy and internal rules regarding allocations. Investors will place applications with Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd. accompanied by the application deposit during the application period. The method of selling the Shares by Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd. through the internet is as follows. From November 11, 2026 (Japan time) until 10:00 a.m. on November 18, 2026 (Japan time) (expected), investors may, during the acceptance period designated by Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd., apply to Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd. to participate in the lottery through Mizuho Securities Net Club, with reference to the Initial Preliminary Price Range or the Revised Preliminary Price Range. By applying to participate in the lottery, an investor shall be deemed to have expressed its intention to purchase the Shares. Such application to participate in the lottery may be cancelled during the acceptance period designated by Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd. In applying to participate in the lottery for the Shares, investors acknowledge that the offering price may be determined outside the Initial Preliminary Price Range or the Revised Preliminary Price Range presented at the time of such application, and agree that, even if the offering price is determined outside such range, unless the application to participate in the lottery is cancelled by the deadline determined by Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd., the investor shall be bound to purchase, up to the number of Shares specified in such investor’s application to participate in the lottery, the number of Shares for which such investor is selected or placed on the waiting list as a result of the lottery. Investors are required to prepare, by the business day immediately preceding the Pricing Date, the estimated amount necessary for the purchase of the Shares, calculated using the foreign exchange rate designated by Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd. On the Pricing Date, Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd. shall notify investors who have applied to participate in the lottery of the determined offering terms and, based on the results of the lottery, the amount and number of Shares for which such investors have been selected or placed on the waiting list; provided, however, that investors who have been selected or placed on the waiting list may decline their applications to purchase through the link provided in such notification until 12:59 p.m. (Japan time) (planned) on the same date. Waiting-list applicants will, on and after 1:00 p.m. (Japan time) (planned) on the same date, be 6 advanced sequentially to selected status with respect to the Shares for which selected applicants have declined their applications to purchase. With respect to investors selected through the lottery and waiting-list investors who have been advanced to selected status, in each case who have not declined their applications to purchase by 12:59 p.m. (Japan time) (planned) on the same date, Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd. shall finalize the amount and number of Shares for which such investors have been selected or advanced to selected status, and shall notify such investors of the execution of the purchase of the Shares so finalized by 4:30 p.m. (Japan time) (planned) on the same date. For details regarding the lottery process and purchase procedures, please refer to the information provided through Mizuho Securities Co., Ltd.’s website. Such indications of interest may be changed or withdrawn. 11 (2) 【Use of Proceeds】 We intend to use the net proceeds we receive from this Offering and the concurrent private placement for general corporate purposes, including working capital, operating expenses, and capital expenditures, including investments in compute and infrastructure, as well as hiring and retention of highly skilled personnel. Additionally, we may use a portion of the net proceeds we receive from this Offering and the concurrent private placement to acquire or invest in businesses, products, services, or technologies. However, we do not have agreements or commitments for any material acquisitions or investments at this time. We also intend to use a portion of the net proceeds we receive from this Offering and the concurrent private placement to satisfy our anticipated tax withholding and remittance obligations of US$3.8 billion related to the RSU Settlement (as defined below). This amount is based upon the assumed offering price of US$74.00 per share, which is the midpoint of the Initial Preliminary Price Range (or, if subsequently revised, the Revised Preliminary Price Range), and an assumed 50.90% tax withholding rate. Each $1.00 increase or decrease in the assumed offering price of US$74.00 per share would increase or decrease, as applicable, the amount we would be required to pay to satisfy our tax withholding and remittance obligations related to the RSU Settlement by US$52 million. Pending the use of proceeds from this Offering and the concurrent private placement as described above, we may invest the net proceeds that we receive in this Offering and the concurrent private placement in short-term, investment-grade, interest-bearing instruments. The “RSU Settlement” is the net issuance of 49,754,965 shares of Class A common stock subject to restricted stock units (“RSUs”) outstanding as of September 30, 2026, for which the service-based vesting condition will be satisfied as of November 19, 2026 (U.S. time) and the performance-based vesting condition will be satisfied upon the effectiveness of the registration statement in the United States relating to this Offering, after giving effect to the withholding of 51,578,975 shares of Class A common stock subject to such RSUs to satisfy the associated estimated tax withholding and remittance obligations (based upon the assumed initial public offering price of US$74.00 per share, which is the midpoint of the Initial Preliminary Price Range (or, if subsequently revised, the Revised Preliminary Price Range), and an assumed 50.90% tax withholding rate). In certain circumstances, the release of lock-up securities from the lock-up restrictions described above will trigger a pro rata release of lock-up securities held by certain other holders. 5 Stabilization Transactions In order to facilitate the offering of Shares, Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, acting as stabilization agent on behalf of the Overseas Underwriters, may engage in transactions that stabilize, maintain, or otherwise affect the price of Shares. Specifically, the underwriter may sell more Shares than the Overseas Underwriters are obligated to purchase under the underwriting agreement, creating a short position. A short sale is covered if the short position is no greater than the number of shares available for purchase under the underwriter’s option to purchase additional shares. The underwriter can close out a covered short sale by exercising the underwriter’s option to purchase additional shares or purchasing shares in the open market. In determining the source of shares to close out a covered short sale, the underwriter will consider, among other things, the open market price of Shares compared to the price available under the underwriter’s option to purchase additional shares. The underwriter may also sell Shares in excess of the underwriter’s option to purchase additional shares, creating a naked short position. The underwriter must close out any naked short position by purchasing Shares in the open market. A naked short position is more likely to be created if the underwriter is concerned that there may be downward pressure on the price of Shares in the open market after pricing that could adversely affect investors who purchase Shares in this Offering. As an additional means of facilitating this Offering, the underwriter may bid for, and purchase, Shares in the open market to stabilize the price of Shares. These activities may raise or maintain the market price of Shares above independent market levels or prevent or slow a decline in the market price of Shares. The underwriter is not required to engage in these activities and may end any of these activities at any time. 6 Electronic Delivery of Prospectus The Applications Handling Financial Instruments Business Operators will provide the prospectus in the Japanese Primary Offering not in paper form but entirely by electronic delivery. A provider of a prospectus will be deemed to have delivered the prospectus if, with the consent of the person to whom the prospectus is to be provided, the matters stated in the prospectus are provided by electromagnetic means (Article 27- 30-9, Paragraph 1 of the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act and Article 23-2, Paragraph 1 of the Cabinet Office Ordinance on Disclosure of Corporate Information, etc.). Accordingly, if such consent is not obtained, or if such consent is revoked (Article 23-2, Paragraph 6 of the Cabinet Office Ordinance on Disclosure of Corporate Information, etc.), electronic delivery of the prospectus cannot be made; however, in the Japanese Primary Offering, Applications Handling Financial Instruments Business Operators will sell Shares only to investors from whom such consent has been obtained and not revoked. 22 7 Timing of Delivery of Prospectus Delivery of the prospectus relating to the Japanese Primary Offering will take place on or after November 11, 2026. 23 Part II 【Corporate Information】 SELECT DEFINED TERMS The following are abbreviations, acronyms, and definitions of certain terms used in this document: “accelerators” refer to processors purpose-built or adapted for the large-scale computations required to pre-train, post-train, refine, and run super intelligence models. These processors are significantly more efficient and faster than general-purpose processors for these workloads. “agent loop” refers to the iterative cycle in which an SI agent receives a task, takes an action, such as planning a project, running code, or calling a tool, observes the result, and decides its next step, with this cycle repeating until the task is complete. The agent loop is the core execution pattern underlying agentic SI behavior. “agentic AI” or “agentic SI” refers to systems that, with varying degrees of autonomy, can plan, determine, and sequence actions and execute them to accomplish defined objectives, including through interaction with external tools, services, datasets, and environments on behalf of a user. “API” refers to application programming interface, a standardized interface that allows external software to access a system’s capabilities programmatically. SI model providers may offer APIs that allow software developers to send inputs to a model and receive outputs, enabling integration into the software developers’ products and workflows. “Applied AI” refers to a discipline and organizational function focused on embedding SI capabilities directly into production business environments to address specific customer requirements. Applied AI teams, which include forward-deployed engineers, work with enterprises to design and deploy custom solutions, specialized workflows, and domain-specific implementations tailored to a customer’s own systems and processes. “artificial intelligence” or “AI” refers to a machine-based system that learns or is trained from data and, for explicit or implicit objectives and with varying levels of autonomy, processes that data to infer patterns, generate outputs—such as predictions, content, recommendations, and decisions—and act upon physical or virtual environments. For purposes of this document, we use the terms “artificial intelligence,” “AI,” “super intelligence,” and “SI” interchangeably. “closing the loop” refers to a development cycle in which successive versions of an SI model assist in building the next, with the goal of compounding capability gains over time. “compute” refers to the computational processing resources used to train and run SI models, including, without limitation, specialized accelerators, memory, networking, storage, and power systems that are deployed in data centers or other physical computing environments. “compute multipliers” refer to algorithmic and methodological improvements in training and inference that increase the effective output of a given amount of compute. “computer use” refers to an SI capability that allows a model to observe and interact with a graphical user interface, such as clicking, typing, and navigating applications, similar to how a human operator would. 24 “Constitutional AI” refers to an approach to training AI models using a set of written principles, which we refer to as Claude’s constitution, currently organized around four priorities: being broadly safe, broadly ethical, compliant with our guidelines, and genuinely helpful. Under Constitutional AI, our models evaluate, critique, and revise their own responses against these principles, enabling us to define and control model behavior through auditable principles, rather than relying solely on fixed rule-based instructions or human reviewers. “context window” refers to the maximum amount of text, code, or other content, measured in tokens, that an SI model can process in a given request, encompassing instructions, prior conversation history, user input, and the model’s output. “CSP” refers to a cloud service provider, a technology company that owns and operates large-scale cloud computing infrastructure and provides on-demand compute, storage, and networking. CSPs may also serve as distribution channels through which SI products and services are made available to customers. The largest CSPs, sometimes referred to as hyperscalers, operate at global scale with significant infrastructure and market concentration. “customer” refers to a prosumer or an organization that uses our models, platform, or applications. “customers with $100,000 or more of revenue on a TTM basis,” “customers with $1 million or more of revenue on a TTM basis,” and “customers with $10 million or more of revenue on a TTM basis” each refer to customers contributing revenue equal to or greater than the applicable dollar amount during the trailing twelve-month (“TTM”) period ending on the measurement date. For purposes of this metric, we define a customer as a distinct organization, identified by aggregating the accounts that we determine belong to the same organization based on internal records and available data. We do not separately define or internally track a category of “enterprise” customers, and our customers are not segmented or measured internally by reference to whether a given customer is an “enterprise.” Because spending $100,000 or more on our products is generally characteristic of organizational rather than individual usage, we use the number of and revenue from customers with $100,000 or more of revenue on a TTM basis as our measure of enterprise adoption and engagement with Claude throughout this document, including in references to “enterprise customers” and “enterprise adoption.” “frontier intelligence” refers to SI systems at the current leading edge of capability and safety, performing at or near the highest levels of any existing system across a broad range of tasks. “hallucinations” refer to outputs in which an SI model generates factually incorrect or fabricated information with apparent confidence. “inference” refers to the process by which a trained SI model processes an input and generates an output. Inference occurs each time a user or agent interacts with an SI system. “interleaved thinking” refers to a capability whereby an SI model interposes discrete reasoning steps between successive tool calls within a single response, rather than confining its reasoning to a single planning phase at the outset. “interpretability” refers to research into how and why SI models produce specific outputs, with the goal of making model behavior more transparent and verifiable, especially in high-stakes applications.

 
25 “knowledge work” refers to complex cognitive work and related professional activities, including obtaining, producing, analyzing, and communicating information through tasks such as coding, drafting analyses, synthesizing research, building financial models, and managing and automating documents and workflows. “LLMs” refer to large language models, or SI models trained primarily on large datasets to understand and generate natural language and computer code. “mechanistic interpretability” refers to a subfield of interpretability research focused on reverse- engineering the internal computations of neural networks. Rather than inferring model behavior from inputs and outputs alone, mechanistic interpretability seeks to identify the specific features and circuits within a model that give rise to its behavior with the goal of making model reasoning auditable at the mechanism level and detecting failure modes, including deceptive or unsafe behavior, that may not surface in standard testing. “model weights” refer to the numerical parameters encoding a trained SI model’s behavior, which are the primary intellectual asset of a frontier intelligence developer, representing the accumulated investment in compute, data, and research. “multi-agent orchestration” refers to an architecture in which multiple SI agents collaborate on a shared task, with one coordinating while others execute subtasks in parallel, enabling more complex, long-horizon work than a single agent can complete alone. “Net Revenue Retention” reflects customer expansion, contraction, and churn as of a measurement date. We calculate Net Revenue Retention by dividing the Qualified Customers’ Current Period revenue by their Base Period revenue. A Qualified Customer is a customer with at least $1 of revenue during the Base Period, excluding subscribers to our Claude Pro, Max, and Ultra plans, whose fixed-price subscriptions do not reflect the expansion and contraction behavior this metric is intended to capture. The Base Period is the three months ending a year prior to the measurement date. The Current Period is the three months ending as of the measurement date. “open-weight” refers to an SI model whose trained model weights are publicly released, allowing third parties to download, run, and modify the model, subject to the terms of the model’s license, without necessarily providing access to the underlying training data or code. “pay-for-intelligence” or “consumption” refers to our revenue model under which customers pay for their usage of our intelligence service, which is metered in tokens and priced according to the model selected. “persistent,” in the context of SI applications, refers to denoting data, state, or context that is continuously retained beyond the boundary of a single operation, session, or interaction, remaining accessible for reuse across subsequent steps, sessions, or workflows without requiring reinitialization. “post-training” refers to the collection of techniques applied to a pre-trained model to refine its behavior, including reinforcement learning, supervised refinement methods, and other alignment methods. Post- training is the stage in which much of the work to make a frontier model helpful, accurate, and safe is performed, including the application of safety and alignment techniques. “pre-training” refers to the initial stage of training an SI model, in which the model learns general patterns and representations from large-scale datasets of text, code, and other data, typically by predicting the next token in a sequence. The output of pre-training is a base model with broad capabilities that has not yet been adapted for any specific deployment context. 26 “primitives” refer to the foundational, modular building blocks of a software system from which more complex applications and workflows are constructed. “prompt injection” refers to an adversarial technique in which malicious instructions are embedded in content an SI model is asked to process, such as websites, documents, or tool outputs, with the aim of overriding or manipulating the model’s intended behavior, typically without the user’s knowledge. “prosumers” refer to individual users who subscribe to SI tools to perform knowledge work. “reinforcement learning” refers to a machine learning approach in which a model learns to perform a task by taking actions, receiving feedback signals called rewards, and adjusting its behavior to maximize the rewards it accrues over time. In contemporary SI development, reinforcement learning is widely used to refine model behavior after pre-training, including to improve helpfulness, accuracy, and adherence to safety guidelines. “RLHF” refers to reinforcement learning from human feedback, a specific form of reinforcement learning in which human evaluators rate the model’s responses, and those ratings are used as the reward signal to guide training. “Run-Rate Revenue” is an operating metric that refers to the estimated annualized value of our revenue- generating activity as of a measurement date, calculated as the sum of (i) our consumption-based fees during the trailing 28-day period ended on the measurement date, multiplied by 13, and (ii) our aggregate monthly subscription fees as of the measurement date, multiplied by 12. For purposes of calculating Run- Rate Revenue, consumption-based fees and subscription-based fees are derived from customer usage and active subscriptions. “super intelligence” or “SI” refers to a machine-based system that learns or is trained from data and, for explicit or implicit objectives and with varying levels of autonomy, processes that data to infer patterns, generate outputs—such as predictions, content, recommendations, and decisions—and act upon physical or virtual environments. For purposes of this document, to avoid confusion, we use the terms “super intelligence,” “SI,” “artificial intelligence,” and “AI” interchangeably. On September 29, 2026, the President of the United States issued Executive Order 14434, which directs federal executive departments and agencies to use the terms “Super Intelligence” and “SI” in place of “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI.” “systems integrators” refer to third-party technology and professional services firms that design, build, and deploy integrated solutions for customers by combining products and services from multiple technology vendors into unified systems tailored to customer needs. “tokens” refer to numeric units into which an SI model converts the data it processes, including text, images, audio, and video, the number of which varies by the model and tokenizer applied. Tokens are the smallest individual units of data a language model processes and can correspond to words, subwords, characters, or bytes. A tokenizer is the component of a model that converts customer inputs into the sequence of tokens the model processes and then converts the processed tokens into the outputs provided to customers.

Based on wage data for U.S. workers by occupation classification from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics in 2025, we calculate the total salary for the subset of workers that we believe to represent knowledge workers. Based on International Labor Organization data for global labor income as a percentage of global GDP, and based on 2025 global GDP, we estimate a 2025 global wages figure. We calculate the ratio of total U.S. wages in 2025 to the 2025 global wages figure, and apply that ratio to the total U.S. knowledge workers’ wages figure to arrive at an estimate of global knowledge workers’ wages.

 
31 Section 1 【Overview of the Legal System in the Home Country】 1 【Overview of Corporate Structure and Related Matters】 (1) 【Corporate Structure in the Country, State or Other Jurisdiction Where the Filing Company Is Organized】 The legal systems that govern the Company are those of the federal laws of the United States of America and the laws of the State of Delaware, including the Delaware General Corporation Law (“DGCL”). U.S. federal law exerts influence over all areas of corporate business; its extent is broad, including, but not limited to, antitrust, bankruptcy, labor relations, employee benefits, securities, and taxation. The SEC administers enforcement of U.S. federal laws relating to securities. These laws, among other things, prohibit use of fraudulent means to sell securities and seek to ensure the maintenance of fair and honest markets in securities, and the SEC requires all public companies such as the Company to make periodic financial and other disclosures to the SEC and to stockholders. In the United States, companies are established under state law. The Company is incorporated under Delaware law, which has extensive laws relating to corporations, including the DGCL (“Delaware Law”). The following is a summary of Delaware Law. Certificate of Incorporation and Bylaws A Delaware corporation is incorporated by filing a certificate of incorporation with the Delaware Secretary of State. At a minimum, the certificate of incorporation must state basic facts about the corporation, including the following: the corporate name, the address of its registered office in the State of Delaware and the name of its registered agent at such address, the nature of the business or purposes to be conducted or promoted (including, in the case of a public benefit corporation, one or more specific public benefits to be promoted by the corporation), the number of shares of authorized capital stock, the classes of shares and the number of authorized shares of each such class, the par value of the shares of each such class, and additional information including designations and powers, preferences and rights, and the qualifications, limitations or restrictions of shares of each such class and any series thereof. In addition to the certificate of incorporation, the corporation must adopt bylaws which may provide for the regulation of corporate operations as well as the rights or powers of the corporation and the rights or powers of stockholders, directors, officers or employees, which provisions are not inconsistent with the certificate of incorporation or applicable state and federal law. Types of Shares Under Delaware Law, a corporation may, in accordance with its certificate of incorporation, issue one or more classes of shares; issue par value and no par value shares; issue voting or non-voting stock; and issue stock with such designations, preferences, and relative, participating, optional or other special rights, qualifications, limitations or restrictions as set forth in the certificate of incorporation. Unless otherwise provided in the certificate of incorporation, each share of stock is entitled to one vote. A corporation may issue shares to the extent authorized in its certificate of incorporation. The consideration to be received upon the issuance of shares is generally determined by the board of directors, with the exception that consideration received upon the issuance of shares with par value shall have a value not less than the par value of the shares issued. Meetings of Stockholders 32 Annual stockholders’ meetings are held in accordance with the bylaws for the purpose of electing directors and transacting other proper business. Special stockholders’ meetings may be called by the board of directors or in such other manner as may be authorized by the certificate of incorporation, bylaws, or Delaware Law. A corporation may, by resolution of the board of directors, set a record date, on a date no more than 60 and no less than 10 days before a stockholders’ meeting, in order to determine stockholders entitled to notice of the stockholders’ meeting. If the board of directors fixes a record date for determining stockholders entitled to notice of the meeting, such date shall also be the record date for determining the stockholders entitled to vote at such meeting unless the board of directors determines, at the time it fixes such record date, that a later date on or before the date of the meeting shall be the date for making such determination. Only stockholders of record as of the record date can vote. Unless otherwise specified in the certificate of incorporation or bylaws, a quorum for a stockholders’ meeting is stockholders holding a majority of the voting power of the capital stock entitled to vote, present in person or by proxy. However, in no case may a quorum consist of stockholders holding shares accounting for less than one-third of the total voting power of the capital stock entitled to vote at the meeting. Meetings of the Board of Directors Unless otherwise specified in the certificate of incorporation, the business and affairs of a Delaware corporation are managed by or under the direction of its board of directors. Within the limits set by the DGCL, the certificate of incorporation and the bylaws, the board of directors has wide rights with respect to management of a corporation. The board of directors is typically elected at annual stockholders’ meetings or at a special meeting of stockholders called for such purpose. Unless otherwise provided in the certificate of incorporation or bylaws, (i) vacancies on the board of directors and newly created directorships resulting from an increase in the authorized number of directors elected by all of the stockholders having the right to vote as a single class may be filled by a majority of the directors then in office, although less than a quorum, or by a sole remaining director and (ii) whenever the holders of any class or classes of stock or series thereof are entitled to elect one or more directors by the certificate of incorporation, vacancies and newly created directorships of such class or classes or series may be filled by a majority of the directors elected by such class or classes or series thereof then in office, or by a sole remaining director so elected. If specified in the certificate of incorporation or the corporation’s initial bylaws, the board of directors can be divided into one, two or three classes and, if there are two or more such classes, the terms of each class can be staggered. Generally, directors can be removed, with or without cause, by a majority vote of stockholders unless the board of directors is classified, in which case stockholders can remove directors only for cause unless otherwise specified in the certificate of incorporation. Additionally, whenever the holders of any class or series are entitled to elect one or more directors by the certificate of incorporation, such directors so elected may be removed, without cause, by the vote of the holders of the outstanding shares of that class or series and not the vote of the outstanding shares as a whole. Meetings of the board of directors are called in accordance with the certificate of incorporation and bylaws. Unless limited by the certificate of incorporation or bylaws, any action required or permitted to be taken at any meeting of the board of directors can be taken without a meeting with the unanimous written consent of the directors. Committees Under Delaware Law, the board of directors may generally designate one or more committees, each committee to consist of one or more directors of the corporation. The board of directors can delegate to committees all powers and authority of the board of directors except for approving, adopting or recommending to stockholders any matter (other than the election or removal of directors) expressly

 
33 required by Delaware Law to be approved by the stockholders, such as amendments to the certificate of incorporation or approval of certain merger agreements, or adopting, amending or repealing any bylaw of the corporation. Officers Generally, the board of directors appoints, by resolution, officers responsible for day-to-day operations of the corporation. The corporation will have such officers as required by the bylaws or by resolution of the board of directors. The authority of each officer is as set forth in the bylaws or as established by the board of directors. Public Benefit Corporations Public benefit corporations (“PBC”) are a class of corporations that are intended to produce a public benefit and operate in a responsible and sustainable manner. Under Delaware Law, a PBC is required to identify in its certificate of incorporation the public benefit or benefits it will promote. While directors of traditional corporations typically have a fiduciary duty to focus on maximizing stockholder value, directors of a PBC must manage the affairs of the PBC in a manner that balances the pecuniary interests of the corporation’s stockholders, the best interests of those materially affected by the corporation’s conduct, and the corporation’s specific public benefit purpose identified in its certificate of incorporation. Thus, directors are not merely permitted, but obligated, to consider the corporation’s specific public benefit purpose and the interests of other stakeholders. Under Delaware Law, directors are shielded from liability for breach of these obligations if they make informed and disinterested decisions that serve a rational purpose. 34 (2) 【Corporate Arrangements under the Articles of Incorporation and Other Governing Documents of the Filing Company】 In addition to provisions mandated by U.S. federal or Delaware state law, the Company’s corporate system is prescribed by the Company’s certificate of incorporation and bylaws. (a) Summary of Information Regarding Shares Incorporation and Organization The Company was incorporated as a PBC under Delaware Law, a structure consistent with the Company’s commitment to artificial intelligence (“AI”) safety and responsibility. As a PBC, the Company is required to balance the pecuniary interests of its stockholders, the best interests of those materially affected by its conduct, and the specific public benefit purpose identified in the Company’s amended and restated certificate of incorporation: the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity (“Company Purpose”). The Company also created the LTBT to help ensure that the Company is managed in a manner that responsibly balances its goals as a PBC. The LTBT is intended to operate as an independent body of five financially disinterested trustees (“Trustees”) with expertise in AI safety, national security, public policy, and social enterprise. Through a special class of common stock, Class T common stock, the LTBT generally has the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who together will constitute a majority of the authorized members of the Company’s board of directors. Class T common stock will not vote on the election or removal of directors elected by the holders of our Class A common stock and Class F common stock, who will be elected or removed solely by the holders of Class A common stock and Class F common stock, voting together. The Class T common stock has no economic rights. Furthermore, the Company believes that its seven co-founders, Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, and Christopher Olah, as a group, are distinctly equipped to be stewards of the Company’s mission. In addition, Dr. Amodei serves as our Chief Executive Officer and a member of our board of directors and Ms. Amodei serves as our President and Chairperson of our board of directors. Immediately prior to the completion of the offering, the Company will issue a single share of Class F common stock, a special class of common stock, to a limited liability company of which the seven co-founders will initially be the sole members (“Founder LLC”). The Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of the Company’s outstanding shares with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally, including the election of the Company’s directors other than the Class T directors. The Class F common stock has no economic rights. Under this governance structure, the Company expects that the LTBT and the Founder LLC will collectively have the ability to elect all members of the Company’s board of directors, and the Founder LLC will have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of the Company’s stockholders generally for the foreseeable future. 37 Common Stock We have four classes of authorized common stock: • the class designated as Participating Common Stock, which is divided into two series: Class A common stock and Class N common stock; • Class T common stock, which is a special class of common stock that is issued to the LTBT; • Class F common stock, which is a special class of common stock that will be issued to the Founder LLC; and • Class E common stock, which is a special class of common stock that will be issued to our employees, excluding our co-founders. Voting Rights • Class A common stock. Holders of our Class A common stock are entitled to one vote for each share held on all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of the directors other than the Class T directors. • Class N common stock. Holders of our Class N common stock are not entitled to vote on any matter that is submitted to a vote of stockholders, except as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of our Class N common stock without so adversely affecting our Class A common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holders to vote separately as a series. • Class T common stock. The holder of our Class T common stock has no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with respect to the election of a majority of our board of directors, the redemption of our Class E common stock, certain amendments to the rights of our Class F common stock, or as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of our Class T common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holder to vote separately as a class. • Class F common stock. The holder of our Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date on matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of the directors other than the Class T directors. Our Class F common stock will be voted in the manner provided by the Founder LLC Agreement. See the section titled “— Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics” below. • Class E common stock. The holders of our Class E common stock have no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with respect to the proposed nomination, removal, or change in designation of the Specified Class T Director (Please refer to “Section 5: Status of the Filing Company—3: Status of Corporate Governance, etc.—(1) Overview of Corporate Governance— Our Governance Structure and Its Goals—Long-Term Benefit Trust—Election and Removal of Directors”) (in circumstances where our NGC does not concur with the LTBT’s proposed action), certain changes to the terms of the LTBT or the rights of our Class T common stock, the redemption 38 of our Class T common stock, or as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of our Class E common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holders to vote separately as a class. Conversion and Transferability • Class A common stock. Our Class A common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock. Subject to compliance with applicable law and the restrictions described in “Part I: Securities Information—Special Notes Regarding the Offering or Sale—4 Lock-up and Market Standoff Agreements,” our Class A common stock can be transferred. • Class N common stock. The holders of our Class N common stock are primarily strategic business partners. Subject to compliance with applicable law and the restrictions described in the “Part I: Securities Information—Special Notes Regarding the Offering or Sale—4 Lock-up and Market Standoff Agreements,” our Class N common stock can be transferred. The shares of Class N common stock will automatically convert into an equal number of shares of Class A common stock upon a transfer effected through: (i) a registered offering or an open market sale of such shares or (ii) a transfer to a third party (A) that is not a holder of Class N common stock (or an affiliate of a holder of Class N common stock) and (B) that will not beneficially own or control more than 9.99% of the shares of any class or series of our equity securities after giving effect to the transfer. • Class T common stock. Sunset Provisions Class T Sunset Time Class F Sunset Time Trigger The Class T Sunset Time occurs when no Class T common stock remains outstanding, including due to the redemption of our Class T common stock or an amendment to the rights of our Class T common stock that eliminates our Class T common stock, which in each case requires the approval of persons comprising the Trust Amendment Threshold. The Trust Amendment Threshold may be satisfied as follows: • if the Trustees are voting in favor of the action, upon approval of 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors and 80% of the Trustees then in office (in each case, rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)); • if our Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of the action: ◦ until the third anniversary of the completion of this Offering, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting pursuant to the unanimous approval of the Continuing Founders, (ii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of 40% of our outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by outstanding Class A common The Class F Sunset Time occurs on the earlier of (i) the time when no Class F common stock remains outstanding, including due to the redemption of our Class F common stock agreed to by a Supermajority of the Continuing Founders or upon the dissolution of the Founder LLC, and (ii) the completion of the Class F Transition Period. The Class F Transition Period commences when there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a “Non-Qualifying Member” as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days. A Continuing Founder will be removed from the Founder LLC upon the earliest to occur of (i) such Continuing Founder’s resignation as a member of the Founder LLC; (ii) such Continuing Founder’s death or incapacity; (iii) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, such original co-founder’s ceasing to hold (together with such original co-founder’s related holders) on any record date for a vote of our stockholders a number of shares of Class A common stock (including shares subject to options, RSUs, and other convertible securities) equal to at least 2% of the shares of Class A common stock held by such original co-founder and their related holders as of the completion of

The Class T Sunset Time does not occur automatically upon the lapse of time or the occurrence of specific events. Any action resulting in the occurrence of the Class T Sunset Time requires approval of persons comprising the Trust Amendment Threshold. The Class T Sunset Time, once triggered, is not subject to extension, delay, or waiver. Removals due to resignation, death, or the occurrence of the tenth anniversary of the completion of this Offering occur automatically without any determination by any other person. Removals due to incapacity require determination by a qualified physician jointly selected by the affected Continuing Founder and a majority of the other Continuing Founders (in the case of physical or mental impairment) or determination by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders (in the case of wrongful imprisonment, unlawful detention, or captivity or restraint), subject to the affected Continuing Founder’s right to contest such determination. Removals due to cause require an affirmative determination by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders, subject to the affected Continuing Founder’s right to contest such determination or, in the case of specified categories of cause, to cure the basis for such removal. Removals due to incapacity, cause, or the failure to maintain the minimum ownership threshold require prior written notice from the Founder LLC by action of a majority of the other Continuing Founders. If a Continuing Founder is removed due to death or incapacity during the first ten years following the completion of this Offering, a successor member may be admitted to the Founder LLC and will count toward the three Continuing Founders required to avoid triggering the Class F Transition Period until the tenth anniversary of the completion of this Offering. The Class F Sunset Time, once triggered, is not subject to extension, delay, or waiver. 42 Class T Sunset Time Class F Sunset Time Changes in Voting Power and Director Election and Removal Rights Prior to the Class T Sunset Time, the LTBT, as the sole holder of Class T common stock, will generally have the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who constitute a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. The share of our Class T common stock has no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, including with respect to the election of a majority of our board of directors or as required by law. Following the Class T Sunset Time, if our Class F common stock remains outstanding, our Class A common stock and Class F common stock, voting together as a single class, will elect all of our directors. Because our Class F common stock is entitled to an aggregate number of votes equal to 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock, the Founder LLC would have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of all directors. If neither our Class T common stock nor Class F common stock remains outstanding, our Class A common stock would have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of all directors. Prior to the Class F Sunset Time, our Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date and, together with our Class A common stock, voting together as a single class, will elect the directors other than the Class T directors and decide all other matters put to a vote of stockholders generally. Immediately after the Class F Sunset Time, if our Class T common stock remains outstanding, the LTBT would continue to have the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who would constitute a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. However, the LTBT would no longer need to comply with the procedures for nomination, removal, or change in the Class T director designated as the Specified Class T Director. In such a case, our Class A common stock would elect and remove the remaining directors and decide all other matters put to a vote of stockholders generally. If neither our Class T common stock nor Class F common stock remains outstanding, our Class A common stock would have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of all directors. Anti-Takeover Provisions Certain provisions of Delaware law, our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this Offering that are summarized below, may have the effect of delaying, deferring, or discouraging another person from acquiring control of us. They are also designed, in part, to encourage persons seeking to acquire control of us to negotiate first with our board of directors. We believe that the benefits of increased protection of our potential ability to negotiate with an unsolicited acquirer outweigh the disadvantages of discouraging a proposal to acquire us because negotiation of these proposals could result in an improvement of their terms. Delaware Law We have elected not to be governed by the provisions of Section 203 of the DGCL prior to the later to occur of the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, but our amended and restated certificate of

 
47 incorporation will provide that the restrictions contained in Section 203 will apply to us immediately following the later to occur of either the Class F Sunset Time or the Class T Sunset Time. Following the later to occur of the Class F Sunset Time or the Class T Sunset Time, we will thereafter be governed by Section 203, which generally prohibits a public Delaware corporation from engaging in a “business combination” with an “interested stockholder” for a period of three years after the date of the transaction in which the person became an interested stockholder, unless: • the business combination or transaction which resulted in the stockholder becoming an interested stockholder was approved by the board of directors prior to the time that the stockholder became an interested stockholder; • upon consummation of the transaction which resulted in the stockholder becoming an interested stockholder, the interested stockholder owned at least 85% in voting power of the voting stock of the corporation outstanding at the time the transaction commenced, excluding shares owned by directors who are also officers of the corporation and shares owned by employee stock plans in which employee participants do not have the right to determine confidentially whether shares held subject to the plan will be tendered in a tender or exchange offer; or • at or subsequent to the time the stockholder became an interested stockholder, the business combination was approved by the board of directors and authorized at an annual or special meeting of the stockholders, and not by written consent, by the affirmative vote of at least two-thirds of the outstanding voting stock which is not owned by the interested stockholder. In general, Section 203 defines a “business combination” to include mergers, asset sales, and other transactions resulting in financial benefit to a stockholder and an “interested stockholder” as a person who, together with affiliates and associates, owns, or is an affiliate or associate of the corporation and within three years did own, 15% or more in voting power of the corporation’s outstanding voting stock. Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation and Amended and Restated Bylaws Provisions Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this Offering, will include a number of provisions that could deter hostile takeovers or delay or prevent changes in control of our board of directors or management team, including but not limited to the following: Multi-Class Common Stock As described above in the section titled “—Common Stock—Voting Rights” above, our amended and restated certificate of incorporation provides for a multi-class common stock structure. Under this governance structure, we expect that the LTBT and the Founder LLC will collectively have the ability to elect all members of our board of directors, and the Founder LLC will have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally for the foreseeable future, including the approval by our stockholders of significant corporate transactions such as a merger or other sale of our company or its assets. Such transactions also require approval of our board of directors, a majority of whom are elected by the LTBT. Holders of our Class A common stock generally will not be able to affect the outcome of any matter submitted to a vote of our stockholders or the election of our directors, regardless of how they vote, unless a majority of the Continuing Founders cannot agree on how our Class F common stock will be voted (in which case our Class F common stock will generally be voted proportionately with the votes of our Class A common stock cast on the matter). 48 Classified Board Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this Offering will provide that prior to the Class F Sunset Time, we will not have a classified board of directors, and all directors will be elected for annual terms. Each director’s term will continue until the next annual meeting and until the election and qualification of their successor, or their earlier death, resignation, or removal. Following the Class F Sunset Time, our board of directors will shift to having a classified board of directors consisting of three classes of approximately equal size, each serving staggered three-year terms. At such time, our directors would be assigned by the then-current board of directors to a class. If our Class T common stock remains outstanding, the Class T directors and the remaining directors shall be allocated among the classes so that each class includes a proportionate number of Class T directors and other directors. Upon expiration of the term of a class of directors, directors for that class would each be elected for a three-year term at the annual meeting of stockholders in the year in which that term expires. As a result, only one class of directors would be elected at each annual meeting of our stockholders, with the other classes continuing for the remainder of their respective three-year terms. Each director’s term would continue until the third annual meeting of stockholders following their election and until their successor has been elected and qualified, or until their earlier death, resignation, or removal. Any increase or decrease in the number of directors would be distributed among the three classes so that, as nearly as practicable, each class would consist of one-third of our directors. Board Vacancies Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws will provide that (i) prior to the Class T Sunset Time, only the holder of our Class T common stock can fill vacant directorships of any Class T director, subject to the nomination procedures for the Specified Class T Director; and (ii) prior to the Class F Sunset Time, vacant or newly created directorships for any directors other than our Class T directors can be filled by (A) our board of directors, in accordance with, and following receipt of written notice from, the Founder LLC recommending the person proposed to fill such director seat or (B) the holders of our Class A common stock and Class F common stock, voting together or acting by written consent. Following the Class F Sunset Time, only our board of directors will be permitted to fill vacant or newly created directorships for any directors other than our Class T directors. Prior to the Class T Sunset Time, the number of directors constituting our board of directors will be permitted to be set only with the approval of 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)); provided that until the earlier to occur of the Class F Sunset Time or the Class T Sunset Time, such total number of authorized directors must be an odd number. Following the Class T Sunset Time, the number of directors constituting our board of directors will be permitted to be set with the approval of a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. These provisions would prevent a stockholder from increasing the size of our board of directors and then gaining control of our board of directors by filling the resulting vacancies with its own nominees. This will make it more difficult to change the composition of our board of directors. Advance Notice Requirements for Stockholder Proposals and Director Nominations Our amended and restated bylaws will provide advance notice procedures for stockholders, other than holders of Class T common stock or Class F common stock nominating directors in accordance with nomination procedures in our certificate of incorporation or the Stockholders’ Agreement, seeking to bring business before our annual meeting of stockholders or to nominate candidates for election as directors at

 
49 a meeting of stockholders. Our amended and restated bylaws will also specify certain requirements regarding the form and content of a stockholder’s notice. These provisions might preclude our stockholders from bringing matters before our annual meeting of stockholders or from making nominations for directors at a meeting of stockholders if the proper procedures are not followed. In addition, our NGC (Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. Please refer to “Section 5: Status of the Filing Company—3: Status of Corporate Governance, etc.—(1) Overview of Corporate Governance—Management—Committees of the Board of Directors—Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee”) will have the right to receive 30 days’ prior written notice of any nomination of persons to serve as a director by the LTBT or the Founder LLC or the proposed removal of such directors, as well as appointments and removals of the Trustees. Our NGC may waive such notice periods in its discretion. We expect that these provisions may also discourage or deter a potential acquirer from conducting a solicitation of proxies to elect the acquirer’s own slate of directors or otherwise attempting to obtain control of our company. Special Meetings of Stockholders Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws will provide that special meetings of stockholders may be called only by (i) our board of directors acting pursuant to a resolution adopted by a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors; (ii) the chairperson of our board of directors; (iii) our Chief Executive Officer; (iv) our President; (v) following the Class F Sunset Time, a majority of the directors who are not Class T directors; (vi) prior to the Class F Sunset Time and only with respect to a special meeting at which holders of our Class E common stock will be asked to vote on a proposal, the secretary of the company; or (vii) prior to the Class F Sunset Time, the Founder LLC as the holder of our Class F common stock. No Cumulative Voting The DGCL provides that stockholders are not entitled to cumulate votes in the election of directors unless a corporation’s certificate of incorporation provides otherwise. Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation does not provide for cumulative voting. Action by Written Consent Prior to the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, stockholders may act by written consent only with respect to (i) any action to nominate, elect, or remove directors or appoint a director to fill any vacancy or newly created directorship; (ii) any action to satisfy certain redemption and protective provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation related to our Class F common stock, Class T common stock, and Class E common stock; and (iii) any matter on which stockholders vote together as a single class if such matter is first approved or requested by our board of directors. From and after the Class T Sunset Time, only the holder of the share of Class F common stock may act by written consent, and from and after the Class F Sunset Time, only the holder of the share of Class T common stock may act by written consent, in each case, only with respect to the actions described above. From and after the occurrence of both the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, any action required or permitted to be taken by the stockholders must be effected at a duly called annual or special meeting of stockholders and may not be effected by any consent in writing by such stockholders. Notwithstanding the foregoing, any action required or permitted to be taken by the holders of Class E common stock must be effected at a duly called annual or special meeting of stockholders and may not be effected by any consent in writing by such stockholders. 50 Amendment of Certificate of Incorporation and Bylaws Provisions Prior to the Class F Sunset Time, a majority of the voting power of our Class A common stock and Class F common stock, voting together as a single class, can amend certain provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws. Following the Class F Sunset Time, 66 2/3% of the voting power of our Class A common stock can amend certain provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws. Issuance of Undesignated Preferred Stock Subject to limitations in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this Offering, or prescribed by Delaware law, our board of directors will have the authority, if 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)) approve, and without further action by our stockholders, to issue up to 30,000,000,000 shares of undesignated preferred stock with rights and preferences, including voting rights, designated from time to time by our board of directors, provided that, prior to the Class F Sunset Time, our board of directors shall not designate or issue any series of preferred stock without the affirmative vote or consent of the Founder LLC. The existence of authorized but unissued shares of preferred stock would enable our board of directors to render more difficult or to discourage an attempt to obtain control of us by means of a merger, tender offer, proxy contest, or other means. Exclusive Forum Our amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this Offering, will provide that, unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware does not have jurisdiction, another State court in Delaware or the federal district court for the District of Delaware) will, to the fullest extent permitted by law, be the sole and exclusive forum for (i) any derivative action or proceeding brought on our behalf, (ii) any action asserting a claim of breach of a fiduciary duty owed by any of our current or former directors, stockholders, or officers or other employees to us or our stockholders, (iii) any action arising pursuant to any provision of the DGCL or as to which the DGCL confers jurisdiction upon the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware, (iv) any action arising pursuant to or to interpret, apply, enforce, or determine the validity of our amended and restated certificate of incorporation or our amended and restated bylaws, or (v) any action asserting a claim governed by the internal affairs doctrine, except for, in all cases, any claim as to which such court determines that there is an indispensable party not subject to the jurisdiction of such court (and the indispensable party does not consent to the personal jurisdiction of such court within 10 days following such determination). Section 22 of the Securities Act establishes concurrent jurisdiction for federal and state courts over Securities Act claims. Accordingly, both state and federal courts have jurisdiction to hear such claims. To prevent having to litigate claims in multiple jurisdictions and the threat of inconsistent or contrary rulings by different courts, among other considerations, our amended and restated bylaws will also provide that, unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the federal district courts of the United States will, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, be the sole and exclusive forum for resolving any complaint asserting a cause or causes of action arising under the Securities Act against any person in connection with any offering of our securities, including, without limitation, any auditor, underwriter, expert, control person, or other defendant. Unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the United States District Court for the District of Delaware will, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, be the sole and exclusive forum for the resolution of any derivative action or proceeding brought to

 
51 enforce any duty or liability created by the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”) or the rules or regulations thereunder. All other claims arising under the Exchange Act may be brought in any federal court of competent jurisdiction. Any person or entity purchasing, holding, or otherwise acquiring any interest in our securities shall be deemed to have notice of and consented to these provisions. We note that stockholders cannot waive compliance (or consent to non-compliance) with the federal securities laws and the rules and regulations thereunder. Founder LLC Agreement Our co-founders intend to enter into the Founder LLC limited liability company agreement (the “Founder LLC Agreement”). We expect the Founder LLC Agreement to become effective substantially concurrently with the filing and acceptance of our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware. Our Class F common stock will be held by the Founder LLC. Our Class F common stock will be voted by the Founder LLC in a manner determined pursuant to the Founder LLC Agreement. Generally, the Founder LLC will vote as determined by a majority of the Continuing Founders. Our seven co-founders will each initially be a Continuing Founder. Upon the incapacity or death of any of our co-founders, a successor member may be admitted to the Founder LLC as a Continuing Founder until the tenth anniversary of the completion of this Offering. When there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a “Non-Qualifying Member” as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days, the 450-day Class F Transition Period will commence. Upon completion of the Class F Transition Period, all of our Class F common stock and Class E common stock then issued and outstanding will be redeemed by us for no consideration and certain other governance changes will take effect. Regardless of the length of time that has elapsed since the completion of this Offering or the circumstances that resulted in the removal of a Continuing Founder, one or more successor members may be admitted to the Founder LLC during the Class F Transition Period as needed to ensure that there are three Continuing Founders serving until completion of the Class F Transition Period. The admission of any successor member during the Class F Transition Period will not cure the event that commenced the Class F Transition Period or extend the Class F Transition Period. A Continuing Founder will be removed from the Founder LLC upon the earliest to occur of (i) such Continuing Founder’s resignation as a member of the Founder LLC; (ii) such Continuing Founder’s death or incapacity; (iii) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, such original co-founder’s ceasing to hold (together with such original co-founder’s related holders) on any record date for a vote of our stockholders a number of shares of Class A common stock (including shares subject to options, RSUs, and other convertible securities) equal to at least 2% of the shares of Class A common stock held by such original co-founder and their related holders as of the completion of this Offering; (iv) such Continuing Founder’s removal for “cause” (as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement), which includes specified competitive activities described in the Founder LLC Agreement; (v) with respect to any successor member admitted to the Founder LLC prior to the commencement of the Class F Transition Period, other than a successor member who is a member during the Class F Transition Period, the tenth anniversary of the completion of this Offering; or (vi) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, the commencement of a leave of absence approved by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders, which may not be approved during the Class F Transition Period or if the grant of the leave of absence would itself cause the Class F Transition Period to commence. 52 Each Continuing Founder will be entitled to one vote when determining how our Class F common stock will be voted. If a majority of the Continuing Founders cannot agree on how our Class F common stock will be voted, then our Class F common stock will generally be voted proportionately with the votes of our Class A common stock cast on the matter (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock). With respect to certain matters, our Class F common stock will be voted “for” the proposal only if a greater threshold of Continuing Founders agree, and if the greater threshold is not met, our Class F common stock will be voted “against” the proposal. See the section titled “—Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics.” The Founder LLC Agreement will not govern the voting of any shares of our Class A common stock held by the co-founders or their related holders. Each co-founder (or their related holders) will be able to vote shares of our Class A common stock held by them in their discretion, regardless of the manner in which the Founder LLC will vote our Class F common stock. Class F common stock is voted proportionately with the votes of Class A common stock cast (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock). Class F common stock is voted “against” (or “withhold” as to) the proposal.
