Limitation of Liability and Indemnification Please refer to “Section 5: Status of the Filing Company—3: Status of Corporate Governance, etc.—(1) Overview of Corporate Governance—Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions—Limitation of Liability and Indemnification of Officers and Directors.” (b) Shareholders’ Meetings The Company’s amended and restated certificate of incorporation, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this Offering, will provide that, for so long as the Class F common stock or Class T common stock remains outstanding, the Company’s stockholders may act by written consent with respect to certain actions, including any action to elect or remove directors. Notwithstanding the availability of action by written consent, the Company expects to hold an annual meeting of stockholders and to solicit the votes of holders of Class A common stock in accordance with applicable exchange listing rules, including with respect to the election of directors other than the Class T directors. The Company’s amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws will further provide that special meetings of stockholders may be called only by (i) its board of directors acting pursuant to a resolution adopted by a majority of the authorized members of the board of directors; (ii) the chairperson of its board of directors; (iii) its Chief Executive Officer; (iv) its President; (v) following the Class F Sunset Time, a majority of the directors who are not Class T directors; (vi) prior to the Class F Sunset Time and only with respect to a special meeting at which holders of the Class E common stock will be asked to vote on a proposal, the secretary of the company; or (vii) prior to the Class F Sunset Time, the Founder LLC as the holder of the Class F common stock. (c) Board of Directors, Directors and Officers The Company’s amended and restated certificate of incorporation, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of the offering, will provide that prior to the Class F Sunset Time, the Company will not have a classified board of directors, and all directors will be elected for annual terms, each continuing until the election and qualification of a successor or the director’s earlier death, resignation, or removal. Following the Class F Sunset Time, the board of directors will shift to having a classified board of directors consisting of three classes of approximately equal size, each serving staggered three-year terms. Regardless of the class or classes of stock by which a director is elected, there is no limit on the number of terms a director may serve. The Company, the LTBT and the Founder LLC will enter into a Stockholders’ Agreement, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of the offering (“Stockholders’ Agreement”). The Stockholders’ Agreement will provide that, prior to nominating or removing a person to serve as a director, the nominating party must provide at least 30 days’ prior notice to the Company’s nominating and corporate governance committee (“NGC”), which notice period the NGC may waive in its discretion. Following the completion of this Offering, the NGC will be composed of one Class T director and two directors who are not Class T directors and will act by majority vote. With respect to one Class T director seat (“Specified Class T Director”), the LTBT’s ability to nominate that director, or remove that director without cause, or change the director designated as the Specified Class T Director is subject to the concurrence of the NGC; if the NGC 54 does not concur with such nomination, removal, or change in designation within 15 days of receiving notice, the matter will be submitted to a vote of the holders of the Company’s Class E common stock unless the LTBT elects to withdraw the notice of nomination or removal. When voting upon a proposal to nominate, remove, or change the director designated as the Specified Class T Director, the requisite approval of the Class E common stock will require a majority of votes cast by the Class E common stock and quorum will require the presence, in person or by proxy, of a majority of the outstanding shares of Class E common stock. The LTBT may withdraw any notice of nomination, removal, or change in designation at any time before the taking of such a vote. Any Class T director, including the Specified Class T Director, may be removed for cause, which will be determined in accordance with Delaware law, without the concurrence of the NGC or the approval of the holders of the Class E common stock; provided, however, that each of the LTBT and the Founder LLC has agreed to provide 30 calendar days’ notice to the other stockholder and the NGC prior to effecting a removal of any director for cause. 2. 【Foreign Exchange Control System】 In the United States, there are no foreign exchange control restrictions on the acquisition of shares in a domestic company by a U.S. non-resident, the remittance of dividends and proceeds from the sale of such shares to said non-resident, or the distribution of assets upon the liquidation of the company. 3. 【Tax Treatment】 (1) U.S. Tax Treatment for Non-U.S. Shareholders of the Company’s Class A Common Stock Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences to Non-U.S. Holders of Our Class A Common Stock The following is a summary of the material U.S. federal income tax consequences to certain non-U.S. holders (as defined below) of the ownership and disposition of our Class A common stock acquired in this Offering but does not purport to be a complete analysis of all the potential tax considerations relating thereto. This summary is based upon the provisions of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the “Code”), the Treasury regulations promulgated thereunder, administrative rulings, and judicial decisions, all as of the date hereof. These authorities may be changed, possibly retroactively, so as to result in U.S. federal income tax consequences different from those set forth below. This summary does not address the tax considerations arising under the laws of any state, local, or non- U.S. jurisdiction, or under U.S. federal non-income tax laws (such as gift and estate tax laws), except to the limited extent set forth below. In addition, this discussion does not address tax considerations applicable to a non-U.S. holder’s particular circumstances or non-U.S. holders that may be subject to special tax rules, including, without limitation: • banks, insurance companies, or other financial institutions (except to the extent specifically set forth below), regulated investment companies, or real estate investment trusts; • persons subject to the alternative minimum tax or Medicare contribution tax on net investment income; • tax-exempt organizations or governmental organizations; • pension plans or tax-exempt retirement plans;

 
55 • controlled foreign corporations, foreign controlled foreign corporations, passive foreign investment companies, and corporations that accumulate earnings to avoid U.S. federal income tax; • brokers or dealers in securities; • traders in securities or other persons that elect to use a mark-to-market method of accounting for their holdings in our stock; • persons that own, or are deemed to own, more than five percent of our capital stock (except to the extent specifically set forth below); • certain former citizens or long-term residents of the United States; • partnerships or entities classified as partnerships for U.S. federal income tax purposes or other pass-through entities (and investors therein); • persons who hold our Class A common stock as a position in a hedging transaction, “straddle,” “conversion transaction,” or other risk reduction transaction or integrated investment; • persons who hold or receive our Class A common stock pursuant to the exercise of any employee stock option or otherwise as compensation; • persons subject to special tax accounting rules as a result of any item of gross income with respect to our Class A common stock being taken into account in an “applicable financial statement” (as defined in Section 451(b) of the Code); • persons who do not hold our Class A common stock as a capital asset within the meaning of Section 1221 of the Code (generally, property held for investment); or • persons deemed to sell our Class A common stock under the constructive sale provisions of the Code. In addition, if a partnership, arrangement, or entity classified as a partnership or other pass-through entity for U.S. federal income tax purposes holds our Class A common stock, the tax treatment of a partner in such partnership or owner in such pass-through entity generally will depend on the status of the partner or owner and upon the activities of the partnership or other pass-through entity. Accordingly, partnerships and other pass-through entities that hold our Class A common stock, and partners in such partnerships and owners in such other pass-through entities, should consult their tax advisors. This discussion is for informational purposes only and is not tax advice. You are urged to consult your tax advisor with respect to the application of the U.S. federal income tax laws to your particular situation, as well as any tax consequences of the purchase, ownership and disposition of our Class A common stock arising under the U.S. federal non-income tax laws (such as gift and estate tax laws) or under the laws of any state, local, non-U.S., or other taxing jurisdiction or under any applicable tax treaty. Non-U.S. Holder Defined For purposes of this discussion, you are a non-U.S. holder if you are a beneficial owner of our Class A common stock that is not a partnership, arrangement, or entity classified as a partnership or other pass- through entity for U.S. federal income tax purposes and are not, for U.S. federal income tax purposes, 56 treated as any of the following: • an individual who is a citizen or resident of the United States; • a corporation (or any other entity treated as a corporation for U.S. federal income tax purposes) created or organized in the United States or under the laws of the United States, any state thereof or the District of Columbia; • an estate whose income is subject to U.S. federal income tax regardless of its source; or • a trust (x) whose administration is subject to the primary supervision of a U.S. court and which has one or more “United States persons” (within the meaning of Section 7701(a)(30) of the Code) (“U.S. persons”) who have the authority to control all substantial decisions of the trust or (y) which has made a valid election to be treated as a U.S. person. Distributions Distributions on our Class A common stock will constitute dividends for U.S. federal income tax purposes to the extent paid from our current or accumulated earnings and profits, as determined under U.S. federal income tax principles. To the extent those distributions exceed both our current and our accumulated earnings and profits, the excess will constitute a return of capital and will first reduce your basis in our Class A common stock, but not below zero, and then will be treated as gain from the sale or other disposition of stock as described below under the section titled “—Gain on Disposition of Our Class A Common Stock.” Except as otherwise described below in the paragraph on effectively connected income and the sections titled “—Backup Withholding and Information Reporting” and “—FATCA,” any dividend paid to you will generally be subject to U.S. federal withholding tax either at a rate of 30% of the gross amount of the dividend or such lower rate as may be specified by an applicable income tax treaty between the United States and your country of residence. Under applicable Treasury regulations, the applicable withholding agent may withhold up to 30% of the gross amount of the entire distribution even if the amount constituting a dividend, as described above, is less than such amount. If we or another withholding agent over-withhold or if you do not timely provide us with the required certification, you may be entitled to a refund or credit of any excess amounts withheld by timely filing an appropriate claim with the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”). In order to receive a reduced treaty rate, you must provide the applicable withholding agent with an IRS Form W-8BEN, IRS Form W-8BEN-E, or other appropriate version of IRS Form W-8, including any required attachments and your taxpayer identification number, certifying qualification for the reduced rate. Additionally, you will be required to update such forms and certifications from time to time as required by law. If you are eligible for a reduced rate of U.S. withholding tax pursuant to an income tax treaty, you may obtain a refund of any excess amounts withheld by timely filing an appropriate claim for refund with the IRS. If you hold our stock through a financial institution or other agent acting on your behalf, you will be required to provide appropriate documentation to the agent, which then will be required to provide certification to us or our paying agent, either directly or through other intermediaries. You should consult your tax advisor regarding entitlement to benefits under any applicable income tax treaties. Dividends received by you that are effectively connected with your conduct of a U.S. trade or business (and, if required by an applicable income tax treaty, that are attributable to a permanent establishment or fixed base maintained by you in the United States) are generally exempt from such withholding tax, subject to the discussions below on backup withholding and FATCA (as defined below) withholding. To obtain this exemption, you must provide us with an IRS Form W-8ECI, including any required attachments and your

 
57 taxpayer identification number, certifying qualification for the exemption. Additionally, you will be required to update such forms and certifications from time to time as required by law. Such effectively connected dividends, although not subject to U.S. federal withholding tax, are includable on your U.S. federal income tax return and taxed to you at the same rates applicable to U.S. persons, net of certain deductions and credits. If you are a corporate non-U.S. holder, dividends you receive that are effectively connected with your conduct of a U.S. trade or business may also be subject to a branch profits tax at a rate of 30% or such lower rate as may be specified by an applicable income tax treaty between the United States and your country of residence. You should consult your tax advisor regarding the application of tax treaties in light of your particular circumstances. Gain on Disposition of Our Class A Common Stock Except as otherwise described below in the sections titled “—Backup Withholding and Information Reporting,” and “—FATCA,” you will generally not be subject to U.S. federal income tax on any gain realized upon the sale or other disposition of our Class A common stock unless: • the gain is effectively connected with your conduct of a U.S. trade or business (and, if required by an applicable income tax treaty, the gain is attributable to a permanent establishment or fixed base maintained by you in the United States); • you are a non-resident alien individual who is present in the United States for a period or periods aggregating 183 days or more during the calendar year in which the sale or other disposition occurs and certain other conditions are met; or • our Class A common stock constitutes a U.S. real property interest by reason of our status as a “United States real property holding corporation” (“USRPHC”) for U.S. federal income tax purposes at any time within the shorter of the five-year period preceding your disposition of, or your holding period for, our Class A common stock, and, in the case where shares of our Class A common stock are regularly traded on an established securities market, you own, or are treated as owning, more than 5% of our Class A common stock at any time during the foregoing period. Generally, a corporation is a USRPHC if the fair market value of its U.S. real property interests equals or exceeds 50% of the sum of the fair market value of its worldwide property interests and its other assets used or held for use in a trade or business (all as determined for U.S. federal income tax purposes). We believe that we are not currently and will not become a USRPHC for U.S. federal income tax purposes, and the remainder of this discussion so assumes, although, there can be no assurance in this regard. You are encouraged to consult your own tax advisor regarding the possible consequences to you if we are, or were to become, a USRPHC. If you are a non-U.S. holder described in the first bullet above, you will generally be subject to U.S. federal income tax on the net gain derived from the sale under regular graduated U.S. federal income tax rates, and if you are a corporate non-U.S. holder described in the first bullet above, you also may be subject to the branch profits tax at a 30% rate, in each case unless otherwise provided by an applicable income tax treaty between the United States and your country of residence. If you are a non-U.S. holder described in the second bullet above, you will generally be subject to U.S. federal income tax at a 30% rate (or such lower rate specified by an applicable income tax treaty between the United States and your country of residence) on the gain derived from the sale or other disposition of our stock, which gain may be offset by certain U.S. source capital losses (provided you have timely filed U.S. federal income tax returns with respect to such losses). You should consult your tax advisor regarding the application of tax treaties in light 58 of your particular circumstances. Backup Withholding and Information Reporting Generally, we must report annually to the IRS the amount of dividends paid to you, your name and address, and the amount of tax withheld, if any. A similar report will be sent to you. Pursuant to applicable income tax treaties or other agreements, the IRS may make these reports available to tax authorities in your country of residence. Payments of dividends on or of proceeds from the sale or other disposition of our Class A common stock made to you may be subject to information reporting and backup withholding (currently at a rate of 24%) unless you establish an exemption, for example, by properly certifying your non-U.S. status on an IRS Form W-8BEN, IRS Form W-8BEN-E, or another appropriate version of IRS Form W-8. Any documentation provided to an applicable withholding agent may need to be updated in certain circumstances. Information reporting and backup withholding will generally apply to the proceeds of a sale or other disposition by you of our Class A common stock effected by or through the U.S. office of any broker, U.S. or foreign, unless you certify your status as a non-U.S. holder and satisfy certain other requirements, or otherwise establish an exemption. Generally, information reporting and backup withholding will not apply to a payment of the proceeds from a sale or other disposition of our stock to you where the transaction is effected outside the United States through a foreign broker. However, for information reporting purposes, sales or other dispositions effected through a non-U.S. office of a broker with substantial U.S. ownership or operations will generally be treated in a manner similar to sales or other dispositions effected through a U.S. office of a broker. Notwithstanding the foregoing, backup withholding and information reporting may apply if either we or our paying agent has actual knowledge, or reason to know, that you are a U.S. person. You should consult your own tax advisors regarding the application of the information reporting and backup withholding rules in light of your particular circumstances. Backup withholding is not an additional tax. Rather, the U.S. federal income tax liability of persons subject to backup withholding will be reduced by the amount of tax withheld. If withholding results in an overpayment of taxes, a refund or credit may generally be obtained from the IRS, provided that the required information is furnished to the IRS in a timely manner. FATCA Sections 1471 through 1474 of the Code, and the Treasury regulations and administrative guidance issued thereunder (collectively, “FATCA”), generally impose a U.S. federal withholding tax at a rate of 30% on dividends on and, subject to certain proposed Treasury regulations discussed below, the gross proceeds from a sale or other disposition of our Class A common stock if paid to a “foreign financial institution” (as defined in the Code), unless otherwise provided by the Treasury Secretary or such institution enters into an agreement with the U.S. government to withhold on certain payments and to collect and provide to the U.S. tax authorities substantial information regarding the U.S. account holders of such institution (which includes certain equity and debt holders of such institution, as well as certain account holders that are non- U.S. entities with U.S. owners) or otherwise establishes an exemption. FATCA also generally imposes a U.S. federal withholding tax of 30% on dividends paid on and, subject to certain proposed Treasury regulations discussed below, the gross proceeds from a sale or other disposition of our Class A common stock if paid to a “non-financial foreign entity” (as defined in the Code) unless otherwise provided by the Treasury Secretary or such entity provides the withholding agent with a certification identifying, and information with respect to certain direct and indirect “substantial United States owners” (as defined in the

 
59 Code) of the entity, certifies that it does not have any such substantial United States owners or otherwise establishes and certifies to an exemption. The withholding provisions under FATCA generally apply to dividends on our Class A common stock. The Treasury Secretary has issued proposed regulations providing that the withholding provisions under FATCA do not apply with respect to the gross proceeds from a sale or other disposition of our Class A common stock, which may be relied upon by taxpayers until final regulations are issued. An intergovernmental agreement between the United States and your country of tax residence may modify the requirements described in this paragraph. You should consult your own tax advisors regarding the possible implications of FATCA on your investment in our Class A common stock. This preceding discussion is for informational purposes only and is not tax advice. Each prospective investor should consult its own tax advisor regarding the particular U.S. federal, state, and local and non-U.S. tax consequences of purchasing, holding, and disposing of our Class A common stock, including the consequences of any proposed change in applicable laws. (2) Tax Treatment in Japan Subject to compliance with and the limitations of the Income Tax Law, the Inheritance Tax Law and other current and pertinent laws and regulations of Japan, and applicable tax convention, persons who are Japanese residents may claim credits as offsets to Japanese taxes in the amount of the United States taxes paid on the income (and estates) of such persons as noted in subsections “(1) U.S. Tax Treatment for Non- U.S. Shareholders of the Company’s Class A Common Stock,” above. Please refer to “Section 8: Overview of Shareholder Services, Etc. of the Filing Company in Japan, 2: Methods for Exercising Shareholder Rights in Japan, (4): Tax Treatment in Japan with Respect to Dividends, etc.” below. 4. 【Legal Opinion】 Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati, P.C., legal counsel to the Company, submitted a legal opinion to the following effect: (i) The Company is a validly existing public benefit corporation in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware. As a public benefit corporation, the Company is required to balance the pecuniary interests of its stockholders, the best interests of those materially affected by its conduct, and the specific public benefit purpose identified in its amended and restated certificate of incorporation. The Company’s specific public benefit purpose is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. Since inception, the Company has financed its operations, corporate investments, and capital expenditures primarily through proceeds from the issuance of convertible promissory notes, redeemable convertible preferred stock, and SAFEs, and cash generated from sales. To date, the Company has financed its compute and infrastructure primarily under arrangements with its cloud service providers, as well as through proceeds from the financing activities described above and cash generated from operations. The Company launched its first commercial product, Claude, publicly in the first quarter of 2023, and has since released successive model generations. The Claude model family is currently composed of four model classes: Mythos (including Fable), Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku. The Company has also launched multiple direct applications and integrations, including Claude Code and Claude Cowork.

 
65 3. 【Business】 Overview For the first time in history, intelligence is something humans can build. The cognitive capability to reason, analyze, synthesize, decide, and create is producible at scale and accessible on demand. We believe this abundance of super intelligence2 will rapidly transform every sector of the global economy in ways greater than the impact of industrialization, electricity, semiconductors, and the internet. If this technology truly delivers on its potential—with the risks well managed—it could significantly accelerate global growth and dramatically improve quality of life for people around the world. Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a team of researchers responsible for many of the breakthroughs that define AI. We are first and foremost a research lab—our mission is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. This mission directs our focus—along with our talent and culture, our frontier and safety research, our approach to compute, and our enterprise strategy, it is one of the core advantages that set us apart. These advantages enable us to continuously advance frontier intelligence and shape the standards for its safe and responsible development. Our frontier intelligence, Claude, is delivered to customers through our models, platform, and applications. Claude has experienced the fastest enterprise adoption of any technology in history, as demonstrated by revenue growing from $0 at commercial launch in the first quarter of 2023 to $17.0 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2026. This rapid and growing adoption generates two self-reinforcing dynamics—an improvement loop that advances Claude and an investment loop that helps fund our continued research at the frontier. We believe the diffusion of AI through the global economy represents one of the largest opportunities in 2 For purposes of this document, we use the terms “super intelligence,” “SI,” “artificial intelligence,” and “AI” interchangeably. 66 history to improve how humans live and work, and it is just beginning. In our view, the world has only begun to use the capabilities of today’s frontier models, and the gap between what Claude can do and how broadly it is used represents one of our largest growth opportunities, alongside continued advances at the frontier. Claude’s capabilities have evolved significantly in recent years, and we expect they will continue advancing rapidly. This will lead not only to an expanding addressable market, but also to an expanding scope of impact on the world. We aim to ensure that impact is as positive as possible. Our Core Advantages Mission & Focus. All of our efforts are guided by a singular focus on our mission. This focus enables us to concentrate talent, research, and compute investment on the highest-value work for humanity and to avoid conflicting priorities. Achieving our mission means the world gains the enormous benefits of frontier intelligence while mitigating the most significant risks, and we believe this requires safety and capability to advance together. Talent & Culture. Our mission and focus enable us to attract and retain world-class talent, including researchers and engineers who want their work to shape a better future. We also have a culture that promotes a low-ego, truth-seeking environment, where frontier capability and safety are mutually reinforcing. We believe our culture has driven our talent density as we have scaled. Frontier & Safety Research. We believe that sustained, focused research at the frontier of intelligence is required to build the most capable and safest AI systems. Our frontier capabilities and safety research are deeply integrated and directly shape model design, training, and deployment, helping us produce systems that are more reliable, steerable, and well suited for real-world deployment, particularly in demanding enterprise environments. We translate our research leadership into innovation velocity and have consistently released better models, platform capabilities, and applications. Each version of a Claude model assists in building the next, helping to compress development timelines and produce compounding improvements in the speed at which we innovate. We refer to this recursive dynamic as “closing the loop,” and we believe it is one of the most significant structural advantages in frontier intelligence and can greatly accelerate the rate at which capabilities advance. We believe that model capabilities must be advanced together with safety, alignment, and security practices, particularly as the speed of AI development accelerates. We assess the risks of each model during development and before and after release, and take the steps we believe are appropriate to balance model capabilities with safety, alignment, and security, even where doing so may moderate the rate at which we release new capabilities. We view decisions of this kind as deliberate tradeoffs that we make because they serve the Company Purpose, the long-term interests of our mission, and our customers’ demand for safe and aligned models. Our Approach to Compute. We manage compute as a single, fungible pool from multiple strategic partners, and we dynamically direct available compute between workloads based on where the marginal unit is expected to be most productive at any given time. We believe that this approach to compute enables us to deliver superior models, serve more customers, and achieve greater productivity from our compute investment. This compute efficiency creates the foundation for us to advance frontier capabilities through research and model development, meet growing demand from customers, and provide for internal usage of Claude. We have achieved this through our research breakthroughs and our multi-chip compute architecture across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD GPUs, enabling us to orchestrate workloads to optimize for price and performance. To support our research, model development, customer demand, and internal usage of Claude, we continue to invest at scale. As of and subsequent to September 30, 2026, we have entered into purchase commitments and lease agreements, including short-

 
67 term commitments, as well as leases not yet commenced, with an aggregate committed spend of approximately $900.9 billion, substantially all of which is related to compute and infrastructure. These commitments include approximately $451.6 billion expected to be incurred before December 31, 2030, and substantially all of the remainder is expected to be incurred between 2031 and 2045. Approximately $70.7 billion of these commitments are due in the 12 months following September 30, 2026. Please refer to “Section 3: Business Conditions—4: Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition, Operating Results, and Cash Flows—Liquidity and Capital Resources—Contractual Obligations” for more information. Enterprise Strategy. Our enterprise strategy is built on the belief that frontier intelligence is most valuable in real-world settings, as deployment across enterprises is where economic impact is greatest and where the improvement loop from customer feedback is richest. Accordingly, we have organized our research priorities, our product roadmap, and our go-to-market and Applied AI teams around enterprise use cases, which range from routine knowledge work to the most complex problems. The customer feedback we gather directs our research focus and makes Claude more capable over time. This broadens where Claude can be deployed and further expands enterprise adoption, which helps ensure that the benefits of our technology reach people and organizations at scale. Enterprise Adoption of Claude The speed and depth of our enterprise customer adoption are powerful evidence of Claude’s position at the frontier of AI. Our customer base as of September 30, 2026 includes: • More than 11,900 customers with $100,000 or more of revenue on a TTM basis; • More than 1,900 customers with $1 million or more of revenue on a TTM basis; and • Approximately 250 customers with $10 million or more of revenue on a TTM basis. Unlike a static product that serves a single use case, Claude is frontier intelligence with rapidly advancing capabilities. We build at three layers of the stack: the models themselves, the platform for building on those models, and the applications that place Claude directly in the hands of our users. An advance at any layer compounds across all three layers, accelerating the pace at which we can deliver more capable intelligence. We believe the value of this integrated approach is reflected in the increasing number of customers that use both Claude Platform and our first-party applications. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, over 50% of our customers with $100,000 or more of revenue on a TTM basis used Claude Platform and at least one of our first-party applications, up from approximately 30% for the three months ended December 31, 2025. Today, enterprises rely on Claude to reason, plan, and execute across complex workflows with a level of trustworthiness and judgment that we believe was not available from earlier generations of these technologies. Customers realize value from Claude in three primary ways: more productive employees, faster processes, and embedded intelligence in their products. As Claude’s capabilities grow, our customers benefit and often broaden their adoption of Claude in new workflows. This expanding role reflects a broader shift in how Claude is used inside the enterprise, from a tool that responds to discrete prompts to what we call a Virtual Collaborator: an AI system that works alongside humans to perform complex, multi-step work at professional levels. We drive the diffusion of Claude primarily by making it accessible across multiple product surfaces. For 68 example: • Claude Platform, our comprehensive agentic development environment, provides customers with direct access to the primitives to build, deploy, and scale their own applications that leverage Claude’s capabilities within their own products and workflows. • Claude Code, our coding agent, works alongside human software developers on end-to-end software development: writing, planning, editing, testing, debugging, and committing code across production-scale codebases. • Claude Cowork, our knowledge work agent, has computer use capability that enables it to work with professionals on end-to-end business tasks: autonomously researching, drafting, analyzing, synthesizing, and executing other knowledge work. Much of the diffusion of Claude has been organic. We amplify this with our go-to-market and Applied AI teams, which extend our reach by meeting customers where they are through distribution partnerships that place Claude inside customers’ existing technology stacks. For example, Claude is accessible on all three major cloud platforms—AWS, GCP, and Azure. We have a joint go-to-market approach with these CSPs through which we establish direct contractual relationships with our customers while paying a fee to each CSP. This structure allows us to foster stronger commercial alignment with these CSPs, avoid channel conflict, set pricing, and realize the financial benefits of ongoing compute efficiency improvements. Ecosystem partnerships also expand our reach, allowing customers to adopt Claude through systems integrators, such as Accenture, Deloitte, KPMG, and PwC; consultants; and data platforms, such as Salesforce and Snowflake. We recently launched Ode with Anthropic, an AI services company, in partnership with leading private equity firms to bring Claude’s capabilities to mid-sized companies across sectors, building solutions on the Claude Platform and supporting customers over the long term. Strengths of Our Financial Model Building and scaling frontier intelligence is one of the most important and capital-intensive endeavors in history. Our financial model provides us with the following strengths that allow us to build and scale efficiently: • Rapid Revenue Growth. Our enterprise strategy is designed to drive durable customer adoption by embedding Claude directly into business-critical workflows and enabling the development of products built on Claude. We believe that enterprise customers achieve a compelling return on investment from Claude, as agentic workflows can drive both top-line growth and efficiency. This enables us to expand quickly with customers, as demonstrated by our Net Revenue Retention of approximately 900% as of September 30, 2026. • Compute Efficiency. Our compute efficiency drives more intelligence from research and model development, and we believe this approach can support more customer and internal usage of Claude for the same amount of compute compared to other approaches. Our compute efficiency is demonstrated by revenue that grew 1,127% year over year for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to compute and infrastructure expenses that grew 382% during the same period. • Operating Efficiency. Our operating efficiency, derived from our high talent density, our efficient go- to-market, and how extensively our teams leverage Claude in their work, enables us to scale with a smaller team relative to other large enterprise technology companies. Our operating efficiency is

 
69 demonstrated by TTM revenue per employee of over $6.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $1.4 million as of September 30, 2025. Our financial results reflect continued growth alongside ongoing investment in frontier intelligence, as demonstrated below: • Our revenue was $17.0 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2026, up from $1.4 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2025. • Our operating margin was (3)% and operating loss was $567 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to an operating margin of (224)% and operating loss of $3.1 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2025. • The combination of our revenue growth, compute efficiency, and operating efficiency has resulted in an Adjusted Operating Margin of 15% and Adjusted Operating Income of $2.5 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to an Adjusted Operating Margin of (93)% and Adjusted Operating Loss of $1.3 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The demonstrated growth, scale, and efficiency of our financial model help us to continue making significant long-term investments to build at the frontier responsibly. Our business trajectory and financial profile have enabled us to access capital and secure compute from investors and partners. As of September 30, 2026, we had raised an aggregate of $141.1 billion of capital and had cash and cash equivalents of $95.6 billion and short-term investments of $36.3 billion. Long-term investments come with risks, as we must predict compute needs multiple years into the future. However, we believe our compute efficiency positions us to amplify returns if demand is greater than our forecast and can provide financial resilience if demand is lower or arrives later than we anticipate. Our Self-Reinforcing Loops Our scale and growth create self-reinforcing loops that make Claude better over time and that we believe create durable competitive advantages. • Improvement Loop. Enterprise deployments of Claude deepen our understanding of the hard problems, edge cases, and domain-specific challenges that matter most to our customers. We improve our models, platform, and applications based on feedback from customers using our offerings in production across their businesses. These improvements result in wider deployments and adoption that fuel the next cycle of improvement. • Investment Loop. Revenue from expanding enterprise adoption helps us to fund the compute, research, and talent needed to improve Claude. Claude’s advancing capabilities expand the range of tasks and workflows customers use Claude for, broadening our addressable market and driving deeper deployment, additional revenue, and continued reinvestment in Claude. 70 Claude is Accelerating Our Ability to Close the Loop Claude itself has become one of the most powerful drivers of our progress—each new version of a Claude model directly accelerates development of the next. Many aspects of the research, training, and testing of subsequent model generations now involve Claude, including running experiments, generating and processing training data, automating evaluations and safety audits, and writing and reviewing code. We refer to this recursive dynamic as “closing the loop.” A direct expression of this dynamic is our accelerating pace of producing compute multipliers. More capable models help our researchers discover these improvements faster; in turn, more powerful compute multipliers enable us to train even more capable models and deploy them more efficiently. A clear example of our ability to close the loop is the deployment of Claude Code, our agentic coding product, across our engineering organization. As our models have advanced, we have seen significant improvement in Claude’s capability on more challenging, open-ended engineering problems that lack a clear specification and have historically depended on experienced human judgment. Claude’s success rate on these problems reached approximately 90% in September 2026, up approximately 50 percentage points in nine months, based on our internal benchmarks. Claude Code has progressed from suggesting code to writing and running it directly and working autonomously over long time horizons on complex, multi-step engineering tasks. This has enabled our engineers to increasingly direct and review its work rather than write code line by line. As a result, the average daily volume of code contributed to our codebase per engineer in the three months ended September 30, 2026 was over 45 times the average daily volume in the year ended December 31, 2024. Over 90% of the contributions to our codebase in September 2026 were written by Claude. The impact of Claude extends beyond research and engineering. From December 31, 2024 to September 30, 2026, our headcount grew over five times, while our revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was 86 times our revenue for the three months ended December 31, 2024. We believe this operating leverage has been driven by the use of Claude throughout our organization.

 
71 Across our research, engineering, go-to-market, and operations teams, Claude allows employees to leverage a team of agents in their daily work, enabling a comparatively small team to take on work that would traditionally require a far larger one by multiplying the impact of each person. The expansion of our own use of Claude reflects this leverage directly. The value of our own internal Claude usage at list prices has grown by over 250 times from January 2026 to September 2026, and in April 2026, this monthly value first exceeded our monthly personnel expense, excluding stock-based compensation. Because each version of Claude is used to help build the next and because Claude makes our teams more productive across the company, we believe the compute we devote to internal usage compounds these gains, continuously accelerating our pace of development and further strengthening our leadership position. Using AI to help build more capable AI could also pose a considerable safety risk, particularly if it sharply accelerates the pace of progress. This is one of the areas covered by our Responsible Scaling Policy, which sets out our plans to monitor and mitigate the risks as we approach what has been termed “recursive self- improvement.” We believe our investments in safety techniques will enable us to manage these risks and responsibly realize substantially more leverage from Claude than we do today in developing AI models. However, we do not anticipate being able to safely use Claude to fully autonomously design and build successive generations of frontier models without meaningful human supervision or understanding, if and when that becomes technically possible. Accordingly, we are considering updates to our Responsible Scaling Policy to keep humans in control of frontier model development at Anthropic. The Transformation of Intelligence We believe that Powerful AI, a highly capable and impactful form of frontier intelligence characterized by the following key attributes, will become widely available within a few years: • cognitive capabilities matching or exceeding those of top human experts across most professional and scientific disciplines; • the ability to navigate all interfaces available to a human working virtually, including text, audio, video, and direct computer control; • the ability to reason through complex tasks autonomously over extended periods—lasting hours, days, or weeks—and seek clarification and feedback when needed; • the ability to coordinate across multiple instances and collaborate with both humans and other systems; and • the ability to interface with the physical world by controlling laboratory equipment, robotic systems, and other machines through digital connections. If Powerful AI is directed at solving humanity’s hardest problems and the risks are managed responsibly, the potential is extraordinary. The possibilities include compressing decades of scientific progress into years; accelerating drug discovery, disease detection, and the delivery of personalized therapy; providing individually tailored education and expert financial and legal advice; advancing power grids and battery design for greater efficiency and reliability; and extending to the developing world capabilities that took wealthy nations generations to build. Scaling Laws and the Predictability of Progress The intelligence and capabilities of AI systems have advanced dramatically. Tasks that were beyond the 72 reach of AI systems just a few years ago, such as complex mathematical reasoning, designing scientific experiments, and executing substantial portions of software development, are now routinely performed by AI. These advances have followed empirical “Scaling Laws,” the finding that AI model performance improves predictably with increases in model size, training data, and compute. The foundational paper, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models, whose lead authors (including Dario Amodei, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, and Tom Brown) later co-founded Anthropic, was critical in establishing these relationships and helped guide the wave of modern LLMs. We expect AI capabilities—across language, reasoning, mathematics, coding, scientific analysis, and an expanding range of agentic tasks and knowledge work—to continue advancing for many years. We believe this will drive demand for AI that outstrips supply for the foreseeable future, limited principally by the availability of compute. We believe that the majority of this demand will be concentrated at the frontier: our experience has been that enterprises gravitate to our most capable models across a wide variety of workloads, including their highest-value work. In addition, we believe that each successive expansion of the frontier will unlock new categories of work that, in turn, will generate the majority of incremental industry demand. We expect the industry to continue increasing investment in compute, research talent, and engineering resources to advance the frontier of AI. Within this framework, research labs with proprietary training methods, strong data quality, and differentiated research talent are well-positioned to outpace what scale alone would predict. A Near-Term Opportunity to Transform Cognitive Work Frontier intelligence is transforming cognitive work—the application of knowledge, reasoning, and judgment to produce economic value. We believe it will make humans far more capable and expand the world’s overall capacity for that work, including accelerating scientific discovery and helping businesses grow. Knowledge workers are the leading edge of this opportunity. As the frontier advances, more capable models can unlock entirely new use cases while also efficiently serving a wide range of cognitive work at scale across the capability-cost-speed curve. We believe the work that knowledge workers perform represented more than $40 trillion in economic value globally in 2025,3 and with the potential for frontier intelligence to make them meaningfully more productive, our near-term opportunity is to expand this value and accelerate economic growth. While it is still early to forecast the full impact of frontier intelligence across the economy, IDC estimates that investment in AI solutions and services will yield a cumulative global economic impact of $22.5 trillion by 2031.4 We believe the impact could be even greater. History suggests that transformative technologies expand the markets they enter. For example, information technology spend grew from approximately $1.2 trillion in 2006 to $4.3 trillion in 2025, a CAGR of approximately 7%, as cloud computing spend grew from zero to $1.9 trillion over the same period and expanded information technology budgets.5 We have seen other technologies, including the personal computer, the internet, and the smartphone, grow their markets as well. The companies that built these technologies grew at a far faster rate than the economy as a whole. Global GDP grew from approximately $34 trillion in 2000 to more than $118 trillion in 2025 according to the World Bank, more than tripling. Over 3 Please refer to “Industry, Market, and Other Data” for a description of how we calculate annual economic value attributable to knowledge workers globally. 4 IDC, The Economic Impact of AI: 2026 Edition, doc # US54452226, April 2026. Reflects cumulative economic impact as the sum of the annual impact estimated for each year from 2025 through 2031. Includes the annual value created across AI solutions and services, investments in the AI infrastructure supply chain, and enhancements in enterprise productivity and efficiency unlocked by AI. 5 IDC, Worldwide Black Book: Live Edition V2 2026 Forecast, July 2026.

 
73 that same period, the 10 largest publicly traded technology companies by market capitalization as of September 30, 2026 grew their aggregate revenue from $68 billion to more than $2.5 trillion, an increase of approximately 38 times, or approximately 11 times the rate of global GDP growth. Frontier Intelligence May Reshape Entire Sectors and Accelerate Novel Discoveries We believe frontier intelligence represents a larger opportunity than any prior technology cycle, and Claude is already demonstrating this potential. Claude can now execute complex projects autonomously over hours and days, coordinating thousands of agents in parallel to carry out sophisticated planning, long-form research, and self-correcting analysis. Claude also turns open-ended tasks into finished, high-quality deliverables—work that was beyond the reach of frontier models only a short time ago. These capabilities position Claude to transform the largest sectors of the global economy, including software development, business and professional services, cybersecurity, financial services, and healthcare and life sciences, driving meaningful gains in productivity and output for the organizations that deploy it. Cybersecurity represents one of our most important near-term opportunities. As each new generation of AI models grows more capable of finding and exploiting vulnerabilities, we expect that defending enterprise networks and critical infrastructure will increasingly require frontier models. At the same time, the diffusion of AI is expanding the threat surface, as organizations deploy agents and autonomous capabilities at an accelerating pace. Our leadership in coding has allowed us to advance Claude’s cybersecurity capabilities and build products that help enterprises secure their most critical infrastructure. For example, Claude Security can continuously scan customers’ codebases, triage vulnerabilities, and write fixes. We also recently launched OSS Scanner, which extends some of these capabilities to the open-source projects that enterprise software is built on. Through our trusted-access programs, vetted cyberdefenders can also use our most capable models for security operations, incident response, and authorized penetration testing, shifting security to a continuous protection model. We expect other sectors to follow as Claude’s frontier capabilities extend beyond current markets to open entirely new ones, reaching domains such as robotics, advanced manufacturing, and logistics, and accelerating progress in scientific research, including drug discovery and materials science. For example, in the life sciences sector, where annual global pharmaceutical spend is expected to exceed $2 trillion in 2026,6 Claude is used in drug discovery and development by our customers, our biotechnology partners, and our own researchers. We are also extending Claude into robotics, where our Model Hardware Standard enables AI agents to operate lab and manufacturing equipment such as microscopes, liquid handlers, and off-the-shelf robotic arms. Ultimately, we believe frontier intelligence will help drive global economic growth. As frontier models make workers and organizations more productive, become embedded in the products and services they deliver, and unlock new business models, they create economic output that did not previously exist. We believe our opportunity is to capture a share not only of today’s economic activity but also of that newly created output as the global economy expands. The Importance of Safety and Ethical Behavior While the potential benefits of AI are extraordinary, its rapid advancement will impact the economy and society in ways that could create significant disruption, particularly if these technologies are not developed and deployed responsibly. For example, bad actors have already conducted high-profile cyberattacks using 6 IQVIA Institute for Human Data Science, Global Medicine Use Trends 2026, February 2026. 74 frontier model capabilities to discover vulnerabilities, generate malware, and evade detection tools; other risks associated with misuse, including in the domain of biology, could result in even greater harm. Frontier models deployed at scale also have the potential to concentrate power and wealth both within and between countries in ways that could erode trust, harm society, and destabilize the geopolitical order. Misaligned models could corrupt institutional decision-making or cause large-scale harm through autonomous actions that are not visible or understandable to their users and operators. We believe that companies at the frontier must invest in safety and alignment to help ensure the responsible diffusion of this technology. We also believe that safety, alignment, and ethical behavior resonate particularly strongly with enterprises, where rigorous safeguards, predictable model behavior, and demonstrable accountability have become decisive criteria in selecting a partner for mission-critical workloads. Our Core Advantages We have five core advantages that define our position at the frontier: our mission and focus, our talent and culture, our frontier and safety research, our approach to compute, and our enterprise strategy. Mission and Focus Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a team of researchers responsible for many of the breakthroughs that define frontier intelligence. They share a conviction that safety must be a foundational principle for building Powerful AI. We have a corporate structure consistent with that objective, incorporating as a Delaware PBC and implementing the LTBT with an explicit mandate to advance our mission. Further, we publish safety methodologies, model evaluations, and our Responsible Scaling Policy because we believe transparency is a prerequisite for trust, and trust is a prerequisite for the responsible deployment of frontier models at scale. Every employee at Anthropic works towards the same mission, and that mission guides every decision— from model architectures, to product strategy, to partnership terms, and to how we direct research and compute. We do not pursue projects based on commercial opportunity or research novelty alone; our efforts must advance our mission. When difficult tradeoffs arise between commercial gain and safety or trust, we have a clear answer. For example, in April 2026, we initially released our frontier model, Mythos, as a gated research preview through Project Glasswing, available to select organizations for cybersecurity applications, rather than making it broadly available at launch due to its advanced capabilities in cyber vulnerability discovery. We believe this clarity of mission reduces friction, accelerates decision-making, and fosters a culture where safety and capability are pursued in tandem. Talent and Culture Talent is one of our most important advantages, because technology, capital, product, and distribution all flow from superior talent. Talent density matters more than talent mass. Brilliant people are inspired and motivated when surrounded by equally brilliant colleagues, creating an environment that attracts more exceptional people. This talent can leverage Claude to maximize each individual’s impact. We believe we have assembled the deepest concentration of AI research talent in the world, including many of the researchers who pioneered the techniques that underlie modern LLMs. Our founding team originated several foundational advances in AI, including Scaling Laws, GPT-2 and GPT-3, RLHF, and mechanistic interpretability. Our conviction that safety and capability must advance together helps us attract and retain world-class talent, including researchers and engineers. For example, we have experienced approximately 1% regrettable attrition of our employee base overall in the TTM period ended September 30, 2026.

 
75 We maintain a commitment to open internal collaboration and truth seeking, which is underpinned by our low-ego, high-impact, and mission-aligned culture. Researchers share results openly, and colleagues critique and redirect in real time. When multiple teams pursue parallel approaches, the norm is to rigorously evaluate which approach is demonstrating stronger and more aligned results. This collaborative dynamic is difficult to replicate because it requires both the foundation of trust we have built from the earliest days of our organization and a relentless commitment to preserving such trust. That trust manifests in ways that are uncommon at our scale: teams that consistently pull in the same direction rather than at cross-purposes. We believe our culture has driven our talent density as we have scaled. Frontier and Safety Research Our frontier model leadership is a direct product of our talent density. We believe our researchers have consistently pushed the boundaries of intelligence, capability, and reliability further than bigger teams or those with larger budgets. Claude is widely recognized for its performance on real-world tasks across industries, including coding, medicine, law, science, and mathematics. Our approach to research provides key advantages to our business: • Our Model Research and Compute Performance Are Co-designed from the Start. Architectural decisions are made with compute efficiency in mind from day one. Our model architecture and inference infrastructure are designed in a single unified process. AI researchers and inference infrastructure engineers share planning cycles, reporting lines, and performance targets. This approach enables us to develop model versions that are both more capable and more efficient compared to prior versions. • Our Pre-training Process Is Engineered for Capital Efficiency. We focus on a clear pipeline for developing model improvements to architecture, training methodology, and data. These are tested at a smaller scale before they consume significant compute. The bar for inclusion in a frontier training run is high and strictly evidence-based: we require demonstration that a given improvement holds as models increase in size, not merely that it performs well at reduced scale. Frontier training runs are planned, scheduled capital deployments with known inputs and rigorous inclusion criteria. The result is a repeatable process for converting research investment into capability gains, while managing the risks inherent to frontier training runs. • Our Post-training Investment Is Purpose-Built for Agentic Capabilities. Post-training has grown from a finishing step into a major research investment, reflecting the market shift from assistants to agents. This is where our models hone their ability to write code, use tools, follow instructions, and operate software on a user’s behalf. We train against complete, realistic tasks whose complexity reflects real professional work. • Our Safety Research Is a Commercial Benefit. As models take on agentic roles with access to critical business systems, trust and reliability are paramount. And as capabilities increase, the ability to operate safely becomes one of the key determining factors for commercial viability. Models that are well-aligned are better at following a user’s instructions—for example, they avoid taking potentially destructive actions without fully understanding user intent. They are also more robust against attacks such as prompt injection, where malicious actors attempt to hijack the model by feeding it illicit instructions. Our work on alignment, interpretability research, safeguards, and red- teaming, as well as the use of external reviewers who can assess our safety practices, helps us 76 create safer, more reliable models, and therefore positions us to meet our customers’ rigorous requirements. Safety and capability research are integrated, which enables us to deliver the trust and performance required for enterprise workflows. Our Approach to Compute Our approach to compute starts with training models that are designed to be more capable and run more efficiently on any given type of compute. Our ability to build more capable models and serve them more efficiently reflects the compounding returns of an iterative cycle between our pre-training, post-training, and inference research, all of which is enabled by our fungible compute pool. Pre- and post-training research produces proprietary compute multipliers that make our models more capable. Research and inference engineering drive sustained reductions in the compute required to serve those models. In addition to enabling more capable and efficient models, our multi-chip compute architecture across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD GPUs allows us to orchestrate workloads to optimize for price and performance. We have years of experience effectively training and running our models across multiple chip families, which we believe is differentiated and difficult to replicate. This foundation, paired with Claude’s increasing understanding of chip and model architectures, allows us to onboard new chip platforms in a fraction of the time this once required. Our compute pool is fungible by design. We have made substantial engineering investments to build the internal orchestration, scheduling, and capacity management systems that allow accelerator capacity, regardless of provider, chip architecture, or physical location, to be directed across workloads. The same infrastructure that serves customer workloads is also directed to research, model development, and internal usage of Claude. These systems manage the underlying hardware as a unified capacity pool, monitor utilization and demand across that pool, and direct compute to wherever it is expected to be most productive at any given time. Our multi-chip compute approach provides us with substantially greater chip access than relying on one platform and enables us to opportunistically capture the price-performance benefits of each chip family and generation. Securing this access requires significant advance commitment. Given the long lead times between contracting for compute and that compute becoming available to serve workloads, we secure compute well in advance of anticipated demand. In some cases, we may also make payments in advance of the delivery of the equipment or infrastructure. We anticipate making significant investments for the foreseeable future, including in compute and infrastructure, to ensure we have the technological resources to maintain and expand our position at the frontier of AI. Enterprise Strategy Our enterprise strategy aligns with our mission. We build our most capable models for the problems that demand the highest intelligence. That same intelligence is also applied efficiently to everyday work— calibrating effort to the difficulty of each task and routing workloads to the models within our model family that are best suited for them. As a result, our customers around the world are adopting Claude across a broad range of work, from routine knowledge tasks to their most important problems. Today, Claude is deployed for knowledge work across major industries, including financial services, insurance, healthcare, life sciences, law, education, retail and commerce, telecommunications, professional services, technology, and cybersecurity. Beyond practical enterprise challenges, Claude is also being applied to pressing global

 
77 problems in scientific research, drug discovery, education, and climate analysis. We have built our models, platform, and applications for usefulness in production environments instead of benchmark performance. This distinction matters, as many AI systems prove difficult to implement and fail to deliver the expected value in complex enterprise environments, where governance and security concerns remain among the top barriers to adoption. Our applications, such as Claude Code and Claude Cowork, multiply the impact of employees. Over time, our applications have become more capable and are now frequently being used to conduct long-running autonomous work alongside employees. Organizations also integrate Claude as the intelligence that powers and transforms internal business processes. In addition, the Claude Platform is used as the foundation for enterprises building AI-native products. As enterprise customers integrate Claude into increasingly complex workflows, they surface the use cases and requirements that shape our roadmap. They also provide feedback that allows us to continuously improve our models, platform, and applications as well as develop new solutions to advance their AI adoption. With each model and product advancement, Claude is able to address more valuable use cases, deepening its impact for existing customers while lowering the adoption threshold for new ones. When a model crosses the capability, reliability, and trust threshold required for a category of work, adoption in that category generally moves quickly from experimentation into production. Coding was the first such category: within roughly a year, Claude progressed from suggesting individual lines of code to operating fleets of agents working autonomously across production codebases. Cybersecurity is following a similar curve, with Claude’s performance on ExploitBench, a benchmark developed by Carnegie Mellon researchers that evaluates AI models’ ability to exploit software vulnerabilities, increasing from 40% with Opus 4.8, to 78% with Mythos 5, and to 91% with Opus 5.5 over a period of approximately four months. Cyberdefenders are now identifying and patching vulnerabilities at scale. We expect these improvements in model capabilities to unlock additional use cases. Claude Security and our recently launched OSS Scanner are early examples, providing the ability to scan codebases on a continuous basis and propose fixes before attackers find vulnerabilities. Claude as a Virtual Collaborator We believe we have reached an inflection point where Claude and other systems can function as genuine collaborators in professional work. They quickly complete substantive tasks that might otherwise occupy a skilled professional for several hours, a full day, or longer. These systems are also becoming increasingly capable of performing tasks that were previously too difficult or costly to complete or surfacing original insights and analyses. We refer to these AI systems that work alongside humans to perform complex, multi-step work at professional levels as Virtual Collaborators. Virtual Collaborators carry the access rights, system connections, and context that their organizations grant them, which allows them to function more accurately and reliably. They can navigate and use internal tools and execute workflows that span multiple steps that require sustained reasoning. Virtual Collaborators are AI designed to be embedded where work gets done, and our aim is to continue extending them to knowledge workers globally, a population that is estimated to 78 exceed one billion in 2028.7 Claude Code The clearest manifestation of Virtual Collaborators today is Claude Code, our coding agent and the product we believe has most concretely defined what autonomous work at the frontier looks like. Claude Code shifted the market’s understanding of what frontier models could do in collaboration with software developers: the model suggests the next line of code and goes further by planning, writing, testing, and debugging—a process that results in production-grade code. Within months of its release, autonomous coding became the reference point for measuring the progress of frontier intelligence. For enterprise use cases, we believe the launch of Claude Code was comparable in its impact to the introduction of the first widely adopted conversational AI assistants. What makes Claude Code a Virtual Collaborator is its sustained reasoning, a harness that translates intent into actions, an execution environment that maintains a persistent state whether on a developer’s machine or in a sandboxed cloud environment, integration with existing tools and systems, and a user-friendly interface. Its uses are highly varied and often surprising: for example, NASA engineers used Claude Code to plan and write navigation commands for the Mars Perseverance rover, resulting in the first AI-planned drive on Mars. Software developers are powerful advocates for Claude—they understand how systems work, have credibility evaluating technical tools, and often serve as internal champions for adopting new technologies. Winning their trust creates a foundation for broader diffusion of Virtual Collaborators across enterprise workforces. We are already seeing this pattern play out with non-technical teams increasingly adopting Claude Code and Claude Cowork to manage their own workflows. Claude Cowork All digital work is ultimately an expression of code, and Claude’s mastery of it powers Virtual Collaborators capable of handling complex work far beyond software development. Claude Cowork extends the agentic 7 IDC, Worldwide Developer Population Growth Forecast, 2025–2029, doc # US53789825, September 2025.

 
79 architecture of Claude Code to knowledge workers broadly by translating a user’s intent into completed work, autonomously reading files, navigating applications, and executing multi-step workflows on a user’s desktop while the underlying code is abstracted away. By extending beyond Claude Code with applications purpose-built for specific professions and industry verticals, we accelerate Claude’s diffusion into new categories of knowledge work and deepen our presence across the enterprise. As of September 30, 2026, adoption of Claude Cowork, which we made available as a research preview in January 2026, outpaced the adoption Claude Code achieved at the equivalent point following its research preview release in February 2025. In September 2026, we began merging Claude Cowork and Claude.ai, bringing agentic and conversational work into a unified application. Users can now move from a simple question to complex, multi-step tasks in the same conversation. Extending Virtual Collaborators We believe the trajectory for Virtual Collaborators is clear and accelerating. Each generation of Claude models has expanded along multiple dimensions: the depth and rigor of their reasoning, the duration and autonomy of the work they can sustain, the complexity of tasks they can complete, and the volume of useful output they can produce. Capability evaluations and benchmarking have shown substantial improvements across Claude model versions in the duration and complexity of tasks that can be completed reliably, with more recent model versions demonstrating particularly significant advances. We are building towards a world where Claude can be given open-ended tasks lasting hours, days, or weeks, and then execute them autonomously with the judgment and initiative of a brilliant colleague. Ultimately, millions of Virtual Collaborators can run in parallel, each working independently on unrelated problems or collaborating seamlessly to achieve a shared objective. The result is something without historical precedent: what we refer to as a country of geniuses in a data center, available to every organization and sector of the economy. Claude is the Partner of Choice for Enterprises Enterprise customers across different industries rely on Claude to enhance their productivity and transform their businesses. These customers range from AI-native startups to the largest enterprises in the world. We believe customers choose Claude for a wide variety of use cases, from routine knowledge work to their most important problems.
