Our customers see us as a long-term partner for the frontier capabilities we offer today, for the innovation they expect from us in the future, and for our ability to meet their needs across the capability-cost-speed curve. Beyond our models, the Claude Platform provides primitives that enable customers to accelerate time-to- value and leverage Claude’s intelligence in a variety of use cases. These primitives are the same ones we use to build our own applications. Our applications, such as Claude Code and Claude Cowork, multiply the impact of employees. Over time, our applications have become more capable and are now frequently being used to conduct long-running autonomous work alongside employees. Improvements to our models, platform, and applications accrue to the benefit of our customers and drive continued adoption. Our commitment to our mission instills confidence in our customers to choose Claude as a trusted partner. Our investments in research on alignment, interpretability, cybersecurity, and enterprise-grade controls aim 80 to deliver the predictability and dependability that organizations need in customer-facing and regulated contexts. This trust means that enterprises can expand the scope of the work that they delegate to Claude, as well as the systems into which Claude is integrated. Enterprises are aligning their strategies around Claude with the confidence that we are building frontier intelligence that serves their needs in the long term. We deliver this intelligence through an integrated approach. Our Claude model family is the foundation, with model classes optimized for different points along the capability-cost-speed curve. On top of our models, Claude Platform gives developers access to the primitives we use ourselves, which they can use to build their own AI solutions. We have also built first-party applications on Claude Platform for customers that prefer a ready-to-deploy option. Claude Platform—A Composable System for Building AI Solutions We seek to bring Claude to every corner of the economy at whatever level of autonomy each task demands, from a single suggestion to an agent that runs independently for hours. Achieving this goal requires more than a capable model. The most demanding deployments need intelligence that is reliable, connectable, and deployable within the specific data environments, regulatory constraints, and workflow patterns of each organization. Intelligence is one limiting factor, but so are connectors that do not yet exist, governance frameworks that are not yet written, and orchestration logic that needs to be built from scratch. Our platform seeks to close these gaps, and we believe the breadth and speed with which we have done so are primary reasons customers build on Claude. Our platform provides our customers with direct access to the primitives to build, deploy, and scale AI- native applications. At the foundation are model capabilities that make Claude’s autonomy possible: native tool use, computer use for desktop control, memory, and extended thinking. Long context and low-latency model variants make that action sustainable: for example, an agent could hold an entire codebase, a full data room, or hours of accumulated task state in working memory and iterate fast enough that autonomy persists rather than stalls. Above these sit composition primitives such as our Agent Software Development Kit (“SDK”), Claude Managed Agents, Agent Skills, multi-agent orchestration, and the Model Context Protocol (“MCP”) for universal connectivity to enterprise data and tools. Together, these assemble into complex production workflows. These building blocks are composable and interoperable. The same primitives that power a coding agent also power a research agent, a financial analyst agent, or a compliance-review agent. While these agents have different connectors and agent skills, they have the same SDK, protocol, and orchestration framework. That composability is one of the reasons our customer base spans industries and why customer expansion can happen seamlessly across additional use cases without significant integration work. Applications That Meet Users Where They Are Our portfolio of applications sits on top of our platform and is deliberately broad to meet users across a number of key dimensions: • In their Work. Claude Code works with software developers in the terminal, while Claude Cowork extends the same agentic paradigm to knowledge workers. • In their Domain. Claude for Financial Services, Claude for Financial Advisors, Claude for Healthcare, Claude for Life Sciences, Claude for Legal, Claude for Education, and Claude for Government come with domain knowledge, data connectors, skills, and compliance controls pre- loaded.

 
81 • In their Applications. Claude for Microsoft 365 and Claude in Chrome are embedded into the software that knowledge workers use every day. A Platform Customers Build Their Businesses On Customers of all sizes and across every major industry have adopted Claude. Fortune 500 companies, including American International Group, Inc. and Bristol Myers Squibb, rely on Claude for mission-critical workflows. Research institutions, such as the Garvan Institute of Medical Research, Gladstone Institutes, and the University of California, San Francisco, are applying Claude to some of the world’s hardest scientific problems. In addition, prosumers around the world use Claude as a daily tool. As enterprises adopt our platform and applications, we become deeply embedded in their businesses over time. Software developers build applications and internal tools on our platform, and they encode their workflows and institutional knowledge into Claude-powered agents. Organizations integrate Claude into essential business processes. Each additional integration deepens the relationship and increases the value customers derive from the platform. This dynamic extends beyond our direct customers. Leading companies such as Legora and Salesforce have built AI-powered products on Claude that reach millions of end users. This reach can increase awareness of Claude, which we believe drives adoption far beyond our direct customer base. When such end users experience Claude, it can build preference and familiarity that travel with users across roles and organizations. The result is an ecosystem where we build on our own platform and applications, our customers build on us, our partners build on us, and their end users experience Claude across surfaces, creating the kind of deep workflow integration that makes our platform and applications increasingly central to how organizations operate. We believe the revenue we generate today does not reflect the full economic value Claude creates for our customers—not just for the organizations that build on us, but for the people whose work, learning, and creativity are expanded by the intelligence and skills they gain through Claude. We believe that there is substantial opportunity ahead as Claude’s capabilities, adoption, and integration into critical workflows continue to grow. Diffusion: Intelligence Available Everywhere Our distribution strategy is built around one objective: getting Claude’s intelligence in the hands of every enterprise, team, and individual that can benefit from it. A core driver of Claude’s diffusion is its intelligence—as Claude’s capabilities advance, value to customers expands, and that value drives greater adoption. Our role is also to ensure that intelligence is accessible, and we do that in the following ways: through our composable platform and applications that meet customers where they are, through our go-to- market and Applied AI teams directly, and through partnerships that extend our reach at scale. Intelligence-Led Growth. Our platform and applications are the primary mechanism through which Claude’s intelligence reaches users. As users begin building, brainstorming, and problem-solving with Claude, they quickly come to rely on it as a trusted partner in their work. As Claude takes on more of their work, people experience firsthand what frontier intelligence makes possible and expand their usage significantly. This pattern repeats across organizations: prosumers become internal champions, teams expand their use of Claude, and what begins as a single workflow grows into something that impacts how an entire organization operates. Direct Teams. This organic adoption is complemented and enhanced through our direct go-to-market teams who help scale Claude to organizations with complex workflows and business processes. By the time our 82 direct teams engage a customer, Claude is often already in use. Our go-to-market teams use this organic momentum to build executive sponsorship and drive enterprise-wide adoption. Applied AI Teams. Our Applied AI teams embed more deeply with select customers, building solutions that make it easier for organizations to benefit from Claude’s intelligence. They work with enterprises to design and deploy custom solutions, specialized workflows, and domain-specific implementations tailored to the customer’s own requirements. This work drives deeper adoption within individual customers and generates the feedback and information from users that help to shape our platform and product roadmap. Our direct and Applied AI teams work together as a hybrid sales and engineering function, organized by geography and then by industry so that they bring domain expertise to each customer. Partnerships. We complement our direct efforts through distribution partnerships that place Claude inside customers’ existing technology stacks. • Cloud Partnerships. Our cloud partnerships, and the way we structure them, provide three distinct advantages. First, Amazon.com, Inc. (together with its affiliates, “Amazon”), Google, and Microsoft each host Claude natively on their respective cloud platforms, AWS, GCP, and Azure, allowing enterprises to deploy Claude within the infrastructure, security perimeters, and commitment structures they already operate. Second, these CSPs extend our reach through their large combined field teams that are empowered to sell our platform and applications, accelerating market penetration at a scale we believe would be difficult for any single organization to directly replicate. Third, we have a joint go-to-market approach with these CSPs through which we establish direct contractual relationships with our customers while paying a fee to each CSP. This structure allows us to foster stronger commercial alignment with these CSPs, avoid channel conflict, set pricing, and realize the financial benefits of ongoing compute efficiency improvements. • Ecosystem Partnerships. Major global systems integrators have built dedicated Claude practices with teams trained to deploy our platform and applications. Go-to-market alliances with leading data platforms embed Claude into data infrastructure that enterprises already operate, facilitating adoption of Claude within existing workflows and making it easier for enterprises to realize value from Claude. To accelerate the growth and capability of this ecosystem, in March 2026, we launched the Claude Partner Network, committing an initial $100 million in 2026 to fund partner training, technical certification, and joint market development with the firms that bring Claude into enterprise environments. As of September 30, 2026, this network comprised over 150,000 practitioners across over 4,000 organizations who have received certifications through our Claude Certification Program. Certifications represent role-specific capabilities validated through proctored examinations designed to give enterprises confidence in the partner they are selecting. In October 2026, we launched the Claude Frontier Academy (the “Academy”), backed by a $100 million commitment, to address a key constraint on enterprise AI adoption: the shortage of engineers who can take AI from an initial use case into production. Drawing on our own experience deploying Claude inside large enterprises, the Academy trains our customers’ and partners’ engineers to the same standard as our own engineers, with each participant leading a Claude deployment at their own organization. We aim to train 10,000 engineers through the Academy by the end of 2027, beginning with cohorts from leading consulting firms and enterprises. • Ode with Anthropic. We recently launched an AI services company in partnership with leading private equity firms to bring Claude’s capabilities to mid-sized companies across sectors, building

 
83 solutions on the Claude Platform and supporting customers over the long term. Ode with Anthropic will partner closely with our Applied AI and go-to-market teams. Our broad and diverse distribution strategy seeks to maximize customers’ access to our platform and applications regardless of where they work. From there, adoption can scale frictionlessly, and through our Applied AI teams and partnerships, we help enterprises realize more value as their adoption grows. Our Growth Strategy Our growth strategy reflects our conviction that sustained leadership at the frontier requires continuous investment in our people and culture, compute and infrastructure, Claude’s intelligence, capability, and safety, the breadth of Claude’s availability, customer adoption and expansion, entry into new markets, and strategic transactions and partnerships that accelerate our mission. • Invest in our Talent and Culture. As Claude’s capabilities advance, we believe it will address entirely new categories of use, resulting in deeper adoption and greater demand for our platform. • Make Claude Available Everywhere. Our Models, Platform, and Applications We are building at every layer of frontier intelligence. Our Claude model family provides the underlying intelligence. The Claude Platform makes that intelligence available as a set of composable primitives that developers and enterprises can assemble into their own solutions. Our applications draw on those same primitives, packaged into products customers can deploy directly. Because we build these layers cohesively, improvements at any layer compound across the stack and benefit our customers. We believe this integrated approach has made us a partner of choice for customers transforming their business through AI. Customers can adopt, govern, and scale our technology immediately, and each new primitive and application we release expands the range of workflows they can run on Claude. 9 IQVIA Institute for Human Data Science, Global Medicine Use Trends 2026, February 2026. 88 Our platform unifies frontier intelligence with the harnesses, connectors, governance, and orchestration that are all required to put that intelligence into production. As customers build on the primitives we provide, Claude becomes an integral part of their data, workflows, and institutional knowledge, and the relationship deepens with each integration. We open our platform to all builders because we believe enabling a wide range of companies to build on Claude generates more innovation and value than we could create on our own. We build first-party applications to demonstrate where frontier models are heading and to deliver fully integrated solutions where we have a distinct viewpoint on the workflow. Applications like Claude Code and Claude Cowork are early examples of what the future of agentic work might look like; they put our latest AI capabilities directly into the hands of users while accelerating the market’s understanding of AI’s possibilities. Because our research and product teams work side by side, new model capabilities inform our products and customer feedback on those products informs our research priorities. This allows us to build products for where we believe model capabilities are going, not just where they are today. For example, we designed Claude Code around the agentic coding capabilities we expected our models to achieve, which positioned it to scale rapidly as those capabilities arrived. We have taken a similar approach with Claude Cowork. We also design our products to close the gap between what Claude can do and how fully customers use it, which we believe is important to helping customers realize the value of frontier intelligence. Rather than requiring customers to learn how the underlying models work, we build products that allow them to interact with Claude as they would with a colleague, simply and naturally, so they can adopt new capabilities as they become available. We believe that as we extend the frontier and broaden our application surfaces, customers realize value faster, embed Claude more deeply into their operations, and increasingly rely on us as a primary provider for their AI transformation.

 
89 The Claude Model Family The Claude model family is currently composed of four model classes: Mythos (including Fable), Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku. Our model classes can be used individually for certain tasks or in combination with one another. They offer broad flexibility to choose the ideal performance, cost, and speed for each use case. All models support text, code, and multimodal inputs. • Mythos (including Fable). Our most capable model class, delivering frontier performance across all domains and solving problems AI has not reliably handled before, especially in coding and long- running agentic tasks. Given its advanced capabilities in sensitive areas like software vulnerability discovery and biology, we deploy this underlying model in two distinct configurations. Fable is generally available and runs with our production safeguards, which block or limit performance on certain sensitive topics, including by routing requests to a less capable Claude model. Mythos runs with safeguards calibrated for vetted organizations and individuals doing cybersecurity and life sciences work, and is available through our trusted-access programs, including our Cyber Verification Program. We first made the class available in April 2026 as Claude Mythos Preview through Project Glasswing. We made Fable 5 generally available and offered Mythos 5 to Project Glasswing participants in June 2026, released Mythos 5.1 and Fable 5.1 in September 2026, and released Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 in November 2026. • Opus. Our powerful workhorse model class for reasoning-intensive tasks. Our most recent Opus release, Opus 5.5, is designed to serve as the enterprise daily driver, powering agents that run projects end to end and advancing capabilities across agentic coding, computer use, and knowledge work. Opus models consistently rank among leading models on key industry benchmarks. • Sonnet. Our versatile model class for everyday tasks, providing a balance of performance, cost, and speed for the widest set of general-purpose use cases, including high-volume sub-agents in multi-agent orchestration setups. • Haiku. Our lowest-cost and fastest model class. Haiku models are designed for high-volume workloads like customer service agents and large-scale document processing. The Claude Platform Customers choose Claude for more than the models. The Claude Platform lets developers and businesses build, manage, and deploy agentic AI applications on infrastructure with high reliability, security, and availability. Platform Features Platform features enable developers to customize their usage of Claude, including: • Extended Thinking. Claude can perform additional internal reasoning before producing a final response, working through complex, multi-step problems to improve response quality on tasks like analysis, math, and coding. • Adaptive Thinking. Claude automatically calibrates whether a given request calls for extended reasoning and how much reasoning to apply—so developers get the benefits of extended reasoning without configuring reasoning levels request by request. 90 • Effort Controls. Developers can specify an effort level on each request to guide how much reasoning Claude applies, allowing them to balance response quality against cost and latency. • Tool Use. Claude can natively call external functions and APIs throughout a conversation, with support for parallel execution and interleaved thinking between tool calls. The search tool loads only the tools required for a given task on demand, which can reduce token overhead compared to loading full tool libraries upfront. • Long Context. Claude supports large context windows and maintains its strong performance even as inputs grow, meaning that developers can include entire codebases, large document sets, or long agent histories in a single request. • Structured Outputs. Developers can constrain Claude’s responses to a specified schema, such as valid JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), so results integrate reliably with downstream systems and application code with less additional parsing or validation. • Code Execution. A sandboxed execution environment where Claude can write, run, and iterate on code within an agent loop, which is foundational for data analysis and automation workflows. This environment lets Claude call tools and process large volumes of data more efficiently and run the scripts packaged in Agent Skills. • Web Search. A native tool giving Claude access to real-time web information, enabling grounded, citation-aware responses in production applications. • Files API. Allows developers to upload documents once and reference them across multiple sessions, simplifying workflows that depend on persistent documents. Context Management Developers can connect context to Claude for their agents and applications using context primitives. • Model Context Protocol. MCP is an open standard we introduced in November 2024 and donated to the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation in December 2025. MCP defines a universal interface through which Claude, as well as other AI tools, can connect to enterprise data sources, tools, and workflows. Claude Platform’s native MCP connector handles connection management, tool discovery, and error handling automatically. • Agent Skills. A modular framework that lets organizations encode repeatable tasks, workflows, and domain expertise into reusable packages, or skills, that Claude loads on demand. We provide pre- built skills for common formats like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF, while custom skills can capture anything from engineering standards and regulatory processes to proprietary toolchains. These skills turn institutional knowledge into agent capabilities. • Model Hardware Standard. Currently in research preview, our Model Hardware Standard enables AI agents to find, understand, and safely operate lab and manufacturing equipment such as microscopes, liquid handlers, and off-the-shelf robotic arms. Our Model Hardware Standard is model-agnostic and lets any agent harness reach devices with a programmable interface through standard protocols such as MCP.

 
91 Infrastructure The Claude Platform offers high reliability and availability for enterprise-grade agentic workloads. Customers building on Claude need the model served dependably wherever they operate, they need it to run efficiently at scale and speed, and they need the tooling that allows a model to work on its own. We operate that infrastructure so our customers do not have to build and maintain it themselves. • Availability. The Claude Platform is available directly from Anthropic and through the major cloud providers, including AWS, GCP, and Azure. Feature availability varies by deployment. • Cost, Speed, and Scale. Developers can tune how Claude runs to fit the performance and economics of each workload: ◦ Prompt Caching. Large, reused prompt components can be cached for up to one hour, reducing cost by up to approximately 97% and latency by approximately 60% for long prompts, compared with processing the same requests without caching. ◦ Batch Processing. Enables high-volume asynchronous processing at reduced cost. ◦ Fast Mode. Delivers lower-latency responses for latency-sensitive and interactive applications where speed is critical. Harnesses A model alone is not an agent. Running one reliably in production is challenging, because agents must survive crashes and interruptions, act on systems with scoped and auditable credentials, and scale across variable workloads. Autonomous operation requires a harness, which provides the secure environment, credentials, memory, and orchestration loop a model needs to plan, call tools, verify its work, and complete a task safely on its own. Building and operating that infrastructure is specialized, continuous work that, until recently, each customer had to take on themselves. We offer two ways to run a harness on the Claude Platform: • Agent SDK. This solution makes the same production-grade harness that powers Claude Code available to all developers, to run on their own compute. It provides built-in context management, session handling, multi-agent coordination, and prompt optimization, so customers can build and run sophisticated agents on their own infrastructure in a fraction of the time otherwise required. • Claude Managed Agents. An out-of-the-box solution in which we operate the harness on our customers’ behalf, on Anthropic-managed compute. We host the sandboxes, store the credentials, maintain the memory, and run the agent loop; customers define their agent’s tasks, tools, and guardrails. When a new model becomes available, customers do not need to rebuild their agent loop. Direct Applications and Integrations Our platform primitives and models are the foundation for all of our products and support a wide range of use cases, from coding agents to specialized products in life sciences, finance, security, and more. Paired with our deep understanding of current and future capabilities of our models, this foundation allows us to 92 rapidly deliver products that unlock value across many user types and workflows. • Claude Code. A coding agent, available as a terminal tool, desktop app, web interface, and mobile app, with native integrations for GitHub and popular IDEs (Integrated Development Environments). Claude Code handles multi-step software development tasks—planning, writing, editing, testing, debugging, and committing code—across large codebases with sustained context and supports parallel agent sessions, so a single developer can keep multiple tasks moving at once. • Claude Cowork. A knowledge work agent on desktop, web, and mobile, built on Claude Code’s agentic architecture. Users describe a task in plain language and Claude breaks it into steps and completes them across local files, connected apps, Chrome, and the desktop itself, clicking and typing through native applications when no integration exists. It returns finished documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and organized folders, with no terminal or code required. An open- source plugin system lets users install or build packages bundling skills, data connectors, and workflows. • Claude.ai. Our flagship conversational product, available on desktop, web, and mobile. Claude.ai is the broadest entry point to Claude, available to enterprises, teams, and individuals, offering access across our Claude model family with support for file uploads, projects for persistent context across conversations, memory, web search, and artifacts for real-time code and document rendering. Claude.ai delivers top-of-funnel demand generation for enterprise adoption. In September 2026, we began merging Claude Cowork and Claude.ai into a unified application, such that any request is automatically handled using the appropriate tools, drawing on Claude Cowork’s capabilities. • Claude Security. A defensive cybersecurity product, available in public beta to Claude Enterprise customers, that puts frontier vulnerability detection and patching into the hands of security teams. Claude Security reasons about code the way a security researcher does, tracing data flows and examining how components interact across a codebase to uncover complex, context-dependent vulnerabilities that pattern-based scanners can miss. Each finding is surfaced with a confidence rating, severity assessment, and reproduction steps. Users can move directly into Claude Code to review and apply the proposed patch, compressing the time from scan to fix. • Claude Tag. A collaborative agent that works alongside teams in productivity tools like Slack, where users tag Claude into any channel or thread and delegate work in plain language. With the context of the surrounding conversation, enterprise software tools, shared documents, and channel-scoped memory, Claude returns answers, drafts, analyses, and pull requests directly in-thread, operating as an ambient teammate that knows when to proactively join the conversation. Claude Tag brings Claude into the multiplayer workflows where teams already coordinate, extending adoption from individuals to entire organizations. • Claude Design. Enables users to create polished designs, prototypes, presentations, and other visual work through natural language conversation and direct editing. Claude Design extends our platform into visual and creative work, broadening the range of professional tasks for which designers, marketers, founders, and go-to-market professionals can utilize Claude. • Claude Science. An AI workbench for scientific research that brings literature analysis, data processing, and manuscript preparation into a single desktop environment. Researchers describe an analysis in plain language, and Claude Science queries more than 60 scientific databases to

 
93 complete it end to end. Claude Science executes computationally intensive workloads on a lab’s own machines, institutional computing clusters, or on-demand cloud resources, without requiring researchers to manage the underlying infrastructure. It returns publication-ready figures and manuscripts—with natively rendered scientific outputs, fully reproducible code, agent-powered verification, and traceable results. Claude Science extends Claude into scientific research, putting frontier capabilities directly in the hands of researchers working on some of the world’s hardest problems. Customers can access each of these products through our Claude Enterprise offering. Claude Enterprise provides security and compliance controls, including SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language)-based single sign-on with SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) provisioning, role-based access controls, audit logging, a Compliance API, and configurations designed to support Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (“HIPAA”) compliance for healthcare and regulated-data workloads—alongside a centralized administrative console for IT oversight, cost visibility, and controls. Customers in regulated industries and beyond use our most capable models for sensitive work. These customers must keep their data private, and we must be able to detect misuse. In September 2026, we announced Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, which is designed to address both needs. The activity data we use for automated safety monitoring is stored in the customer’s own cloud account, under the customer’s encryption keys and access controls. Our automated systems review recent activity for signs of serious misuse and send alerts of such misuse directly to the customer’s security team. No review by Anthropic employees is required. We developed Enterprise Frontier Safeguards with more than 100 customers in industries including financial services, healthcare, and the public sector. We are rolling out this feature in phases and, until the completion of the rollout, eligible customers receive zero data retention on Fable 5, Fable 5.1, and Fable 5.2, meaning that, except where needed to comply with applicable law or combat misuse or harm, we do not store their inputs or outputs after we process a request. Vertical Solutions Beyond our horizontal platform and applications, we are building vertical solutions in industries where domain specificity and regulatory requirements make general-purpose tools insufficient. Our vertical solutions arrive purpose-built and are embedded with domain knowledge, controls designed to support industry-specific compliance requirements, and pre-configured data integrations that reduce time-to-value. Our vertical solutions are delivered through a range of channels, including our Claude Enterprise and Team plans, domain-specific connectors and plugins available on our individual subscription plans, Claude Platform, and, in the case of Claude for Education, institution-wide agreements. To date, we have launched seven vertical solutions: • Claude for Financial Services. Provides financial professionals with pre-built, customizable AI agents for common finance workflows, such as drafting pitch books, reviewing earnings, running know-your-customer screenings, and conducting financial analysis. Claude for Financial Services plugs directly into the data sources financial firms already use (e.g., market data, data warehouses) and runs inside the tools financial professionals utilize—such as Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, and Claude’s own apps. • Claude for Financial Advisors. Provides financial advisors and wealth management firms with pre- built, customizable workflows for common advisory tasks, such as preparing for client meetings, drafting follow-ups, reviewing portfolio rebalances, and preparing estate and tax briefs. Claude for Financial Advisors plugs directly into the systems advisors already use (e.g., custodial platforms, 94 portfolio management and financial planning tools, and customer relationship management software), with advisor review built into each workflow to help firms meet their compliance requirements. • Claude for Healthcare. Gives providers, payers, and health technology companies frontier models with domain intelligence across clinical reasoning, medical coding, and long-horizon agentic operations, as well as tools designed to support HIPAA compliance for medical and operational workflows. Claude for Healthcare also connects to industry systems including the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Coverage Database, ICD-10, and National Provider Identifier (NPI) Registry, with agent skills for Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) development and prior authorization reviews. • Claude for Life Sciences. Provides computational biologists, bioinformaticians, clinical trial managers, and regulatory affairs specialists with domain intelligence built into frontier models across organic chemistry, structural biology, lab protocols, and bioinformatics pipelines. Claude for Life Sciences supports work across the development chain, from early discovery and preclinical research through clinical trial operations and regulatory submissions. Claude plugs directly into the tools and databases researchers already use, such as electronic lab notebooks, data repositories, and scientific literature. • Claude for Legal. Provides legal professionals, including in-house counsel, law firm attorneys, and legal operations teams, with pre-built AI agents for common legal workflows. Claude for Legal plugs directly into the systems and tools legal professionals already rely on. Through MCP connectors, Claude for Legal connects to e-discovery and legal data intelligence platforms like Relativity, AI contracting platforms like Ironclad, legal research databases, deal rooms, and matter management systems. Each agent and workflow is configurable to a team’s own precedents, processes, escalation chains, risk calibration, and house style—with controls designed to support attorney- client privilege, ethical walls, and confidentiality obligations. • Claude for Education. Provides trusted AI solutions for higher education institutions and K-12 educators. Claude for Higher Education gives faculty, students, researchers, and administrators an AI partner for teaching, learning, research, and operations. This includes a learning mode for students, which is designed to strengthen critical thinking. Claude also helps university faculty across tasks such as research, drafting assignments, and supporting administrative work, all with the security and compliance built for institutional requirements. Claude for Teachers gives verified K-12 educators in the United States free access to premium Claude capabilities, a library of teaching skills, and a direct connection to evidence-based curricula, mapped to academic standards in all 50 states. Claude helps with the paperwork, so teachers can spend more time with their students. • Claude for Government. Brings Claude models to U.S. government agencies for drafting, research, analysis, and coding in a FedRAMP High authorized environment, designed to support the data handling and auditability requirements of government customers. Government customers outside the United States, and customers with workloads in classified environments, can access Claude models through Amazon Bedrock, subject to the authorizations and availability of that platform. Our Infrastructure Our infrastructure underpins our ability to train frontier models, serve inference at scale, manage internal

 
95 usage of Claude, and deliver Claude to our customers with the performance and reliability that enterprise deployments require. We have built a differentiated infrastructure layer that allows us to train and deploy frontier models more efficiently across multiple hardware platforms. This infrastructure advantage compounds over time: as we bring optimizations to each chip family, every layer of our system benefits accordingly. Multi-Chip Compute Approach We have built a deliberate and diversified compute sourcing strategy across multiple chip platforms that provides the following distinct advantages: • We can secure compute from multiple providers rather than being constrained by any single provider. • We can select chips based on the best price-performance and efficiency characteristics for each workload, benefiting from the differentiated strengths of each platform. • We maintain collaborative relationships with each of our providers, and we influence roadmaps and features of future chip generations. Our chip platforms include: ◦ AWS Trainium. Our strategic collaboration with Amazon provides us with access to accelerators, including custom-designed Trainium chips, and compute infrastructure, as well as the opportunity to influence future generations of Trainium chips. ◦ Google TPUs. Our partnerships with Google and Broadcom provide us with access to compute capacity powered by Google TPUs across multiple generations of the TPU platform. ◦ NVIDIA GPUs. Our strategic partnership with NVIDIA, together with our arrangements with Microsoft, SpaceX.AI LLC (formerly known as X.AI LLC) (“SpaceXAI”), wholly owned subsidiaries of Nscale Global Holdings Limited (together with its affiliates, “Nscale”), Lambda, Inc. (“Lambda”), and other cloud providers, provides us with access to compute capacity powered by NVIDIA GPUs, including NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin GPU systems, as well as the opportunity to collaborate directly with NVIDIA on design and engineering to optimize future NVIDIA hardware for our workload profile. ◦ AMD GPUs. Our relationship with AMD, together with our arrangements with approved manufacturers of AMD-based Helios rack-scale systems and third-party service providers, provides us with access to compute capacity powered by AMD Instinct™ GPUs, including AMD Instinct™ MI450 Series GPUs, as well as the opportunity to collaborate directly with AMD through a multi-year engineering collaboration. • We can onboard new chip platforms in a fraction of the time it once took. Historically, bringing a new chip platform into production required intense engineering effort over many months. By leveraging Claude, our engineering teams can now bring new chip platforms into production more quickly. This speed and efficiency also rely on the robust foundation we have already built across multiple chip families, including a proprietary orchestration layer designed to seamlessly test and measure performance against our actual workloads. As a result, we are able to adopt new accelerators as they become available, expanding our access to compute capacity while reducing our dependence on any single hardware provider. 96 Please refer to “Section 3: Business Conditions, 4: Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition, Operating Results, and Cash Flows—Liquidity and Capital Resources—Contractual Obligations—Infrastructure Service Arrangements” for more information regarding the terms of these arrangements. Our Data Center Strategy Historically, we purchased compute under fixed-time agreements. As our compute requirements have scaled, we have transitioned to a hybrid model in which, in addition to purchasing compute as a cloud service, we also procure specialized accelerators directly and operate this hardware in dedicated data center facilities leased and operated on our behalf, to our specification. We refer to this additional source of compute as Anthropic Direct. This transition is driven in part by the scale of our compute requirements as well as the potential long-term economic advantages of direct infrastructure leasing and hosting. Our first data center facility became operational this year. Anthropic Direct also lets us separate our commitment to data center capacity from our commitment to the accelerators deployed inside it. Because data centers require longer lead times but represent a smaller fraction of total compute costs, this approach enables us to secure data center capacity early while deferring larger accelerator investments until our specific compute needs are more certain. Our data center infrastructure strategy includes several contractual arrangements that, taken together, form a new source of compute to supplement the capacity we procure from our CSPs. Such arrangements include the following: • Compute Infrastructure Equipment. We procure specialized accelerators and associated components, including CPUs and high-bandwidth memory, through master equipment leases, including the 2026 Lease Arrangement (as defined in “Section 3: Business Conditions, 3: Business and Other Risks—We have incurred significant indebtedness in order to operate and grow our business, including to fund our substantial compute commitments, and our ability to service this indebtedness may be constrained by our cash flows and liquidity.”), pursuant to which we receive such hardware for deployment in dedicated data center facilities operated by others on our behalf. Please refer to “Section 3: Business Conditions, 4: Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition, Operating Results, and Cash Flows—Liquidity and Capital Resources— Contractual Obligations—Infrastructure Equipment Leases” for more information regarding the terms of these leases. • Data Centers. In certain of our data center infrastructure arrangements, third-party partners procure the underlying real estate, power, and data center facilities, while we lease capacity in those facilities and contract with specialized third-party operators for ongoing facility management. For example, we have entered into a colocation and services agreement with Fluidstack USA I Inc. (“Fluidstack”), under which Fluidstack provides data center development and operations services to us. We have also executed data center leases directly and expect to do so increasingly over time. To secure certain data center development projects, which require significant capital commitments in advance of deployment, we have in some cases relied, and expect to continue to rely, on arrangements with financing sources or partners who guarantee the lease obligations to support the development of data center capacity that is expected to host such partner’s chips or computing infrastructure. Our ability to expand compute and infrastructure capacity through these arrangements in the future may depend on the continued willingness and ability of a limited number of CSPs, partners, and financing sources to enter into and perform under them.

 
97 • Electrical Power. Electrical power procurement requires separate arrangements with utility providers or, in some cases, development of behind-the-meter power generation capacity that supplies electricity directly to the facility rather than through the broader electric grid. Securing adequate power capacity for data center projects, whether through grid-connected or behind-the- meter arrangements, typically requires long lead times and significant financial commitments well in advance of when facilities become operational. Our data center infrastructure projects are currently located primarily in the United States. As we continue to expand our global customer base and research operations, we are pursuing additional data center capacity internationally to support our full range of workloads. Multi-Cloud Distribution Claude is available across the three major cloud platforms via their dedicated AI service layers (Amazon Bedrock, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry), ensuring that organizations can deploy our models within the infrastructure they already use and trust, while providing enterprises with deployment flexibility and avoiding vendor lock-in. Our Customers Organizations around the world rely on Claude. We serve a breadth of customers, from the largest enterprises to AI-native companies, government and research institutions, as well as prosumers. As of September 30, 2026, our customers with $100,000 or more of revenue on a TTM basis included every company in the Fortune 10, over 50% of the Fortune 500, and over 30% of the Global 2000. Across industries, enterprises deploy Claude in mission-critical production workflows—for example, underwriting insurance policies, writing clinical reports for life-saving drugs, detecting and remediating cybersecurity threats, and analyzing portfolios for asset managers. Claude has achieved particularly deep adoption in highly regulated sectors where the cost of unreliable AI is prohibitive and trust cannot be retrofitted. In addition, leading AI-native companies build next-generation coding tools, design platforms, and productivity applications on Claude. Government and research institutions also apply Claude to work that ranges from materials science to energy security; mission-driven organizations use Claude to compress the expected timeline of scientific research, clinical workflows, and the delivery of public benefits. Our customer base has grown rapidly in both the number and scale of customer relationships, with organizations expanding from initial use cases into enterprise-wide production deployments. As of September 30, 2026, we had more than 11,900 customers with $100,000 or more of revenue on a TTM basis, up from more than 950 as of September 30, 2025. Our customers fall into two primary categories: enterprises and prosumers. Enterprises Our enterprise customers include a wide range of organizations deploying AI at scale, from AI-native startups building products to the world’s largest organizations that require enterprise-grade security, governance, and compliance before a single workflow impacts production. We serve this full spectrum from a single composable platform, providing frictionless access to our frontier models as well as the controls customers require, such as single sign-on, audit logging, data retention policies, role-based access controls, and native deployment within their existing cloud infrastructure. 98 Software developers remain a critical adoption force within enterprises: they are simultaneously customers, the architects of applications built on our platform, and the internal champions of organization-wide adoption. Software developers use Claude Code and the Claude Platform to write, debug, and ship production-quality code faster—architecting systems, implementing features, building agentic workflows, and resolving complex issues in hours that previously took days. These production deployments surface the governance, reliability, and integration requirements that only emerge under real enterprise load, which creates feedback that flows back into our roadmap and deepens our customer relationships with every release. Prosumers Knowledge workers, including researchers, developers, analysts, and writers, subscribe to our Claude Pro, Max, and Ultra plans to perform complex cognitive work, including drafting analyses, synthesizing research, writing and reviewing code, building financial models, and automating workflows. With Claude Cowork, non- technical prosumers build agentic workflows across their applications without writing code, accomplishing in minutes what previously required hours of manual effort. Prosumers are some of our earliest adopters and often among our most discerning users. They test out capabilities within hours of the release of a model, push the latest version of Claude into use cases we may not have anticipated, and discover edge cases and failures that sharpen each successive version of a Claude model. The adoption of Claude Code began with individual software developers who noticed the potential of autonomous coding agents before enterprise procurement teams had considered the category; Claude Code is now becoming the default choice inside many enterprise engineering organizations. Prosumers serve as a powerful top-of-funnel engine—we have consistently seen that individuals who experience Claude’s value firsthand become advocates within their organizations, seeding adoption that accelerates from individual use to team-wide and ultimately organization-wide deployment. How Claude Drives Value for Customers Customers realize value from Claude in three primary ways: more productive employees, faster processes, and embedded intelligence in their products. These outcomes are different expressions of the same intelligence, each drawing on the same models and primitives. More Productive Employees. Adoption most often begins here. An individual experiences the impact that a frontier model can have on their own output—for instance, hours of financial analysis or code review completed in minutes—and that conviction spreads from the first user to their team, and from one team to the entire company. This happens for Claude Code in software development; Claude Cowork delivers this for knowledge workers more broadly. Our Claude Enterprise plan provides the governance, security, and administration to support adoption of Claude at organizational scale. Faster Processes. As adoption deepens, Claude stops being something employees consult and starts being something the organization runs on. As organizations encode more of their workflows into Claude—their data, systems, conventions, and prior work—the platform becomes more valuable for them. Claude can draw on that accumulated context to suggest the next workflow worth automating, reducing the effort required for each successive deployment. Embedded Intelligence. At the deepest level, Claude moves from an operational advantage to a commercial one. Product teams build on the Claude Platform to embed frontier models into their own products, including customer-facing agents, AI-native features, and entirely new product lines that were not previously viable without AI capabilities. Claude is both a tool the organization uses and an ingredient in the value it delivers

 
99 to its own customers. Across all three dimensions, a significant share of expansion requires minimal to no new deployment at all. Each new version of a Claude model is designed to improve the performance of existing use cases: employees produce higher-quality work, encoded processes run with greater accuracy and reliability, and embedded products deliver more value to end users. As a result, customers can increase usage, utilize higher subscription tiers, and bring additional workflows onto the platform without a new sales cycle or procurement decision. Despite the pace of adoption, we believe we are in the earliest stages of penetrating the opportunity at the frontier. Most enterprises that use Claude today have deployed it across a small number of teams and use cases relative to the scope of work Claude can address today and the scope of work we believe Claude can address in the future. We believe most knowledge workers globally have not yet used frontier models. As each new version of a Claude model advances in capability, the range of tasks and workflows that become viable on the platform continues to expand. Because we operate the platform and offer applications, model advances reach our customers through several channels simultaneously. 100
