405 Anthropic, PBC Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements 1. Description of Business and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies Anthropic, PBC (the “Company”) is a public benefit corporation (“PBC”) incorporated under Delaware law in January 2021. The Company develops and maintains advanced artificial intelligence (“AI”) models and provides its intelligence service through its platform and applications to customers. The Company’s public benefit purpose is to responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. The Company is headquartered in San Francisco, California. Basis of Presentation The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“GAAP”). The Company consolidates its wholly owned subsidiaries over which it exercises control, as well as variable interest entities (“VIEs”) where the Company is deemed to be the primary beneficiary. All intercompany balances and transactions between consolidated entities have been eliminated in consolidation. 406 Change in Presentation and Reclassification of Prior Periods Certain amounts reported in the Company’s prior period consolidated financial statements have been reclassified to conform to the current period presentation. During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company changed its presentation of operating expenses from a functional classification under which cost of revenue, gross profit (loss), research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative were presented as separate line items, to a classification based on the nature of expenses. As a result of this change in presentation, cost of revenue, gross profit (loss), research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative are no longer presented as separate line items in the consolidated statements of operations. Under the new presentation, expenses are presented by major categories, including compute and infrastructure; personnel; sales, marketing, and partnerships; Bartz settlement; and other operating and administrative. In addition, the Company combined or separately presented certain captions on its consolidated balance sheets and consolidated statements of cash flows. These reclassifications and certain other prior period amounts have been recast for all prior periods presented to conform to the current period presentation. These reclassifications affect presentation only and did not impact total assets, total liabilities, total stockholders’ equity (deficit), total operating loss, net loss, or net cash provided by (used in) operating, investing, or financing activities. Unaudited Interim Consolidated Financial Information The accompanying interim consolidated balance sheet as of September 30, 2026 and the interim consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive loss, redeemable convertible preferred stock and stockholders’ deficit, and cash flows for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 and 2026 and the related notes to such interim consolidated financial statements are unaudited. These unaudited interim consolidated financial statements are presented in accordance with the rules and regulations of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and do not include all disclosures normally required in annual consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP. In management’s opinion, the unaudited interim consolidated financial statements have been prepared on the same basis as the annual consolidated financial statements and reflect all normal and recurring adjustments necessary for the fair statement of the Company’s financial position as of September 30, 2026 and the Company’s consolidated results of operations and cash flows for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 and 2026. The results of operations for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 are not necessarily indicative of the results to be expected for the full year or any other future interim or annual period. Stock Split On September 17, 2026, the Company effected a 10-for-1 stock split of its authorized, issued, and outstanding shares of Class A common stock and Class N common stock. The conversion rate of the Company’s redeemable convertible preferred stock was proportionately adjusted to factor in the stock split. On the same date, the Company also effected a 1-for-1,000 reverse stock split of its authorized and issued shares of Class T common stock. All share and per share information has been retroactively adjusted to reflect the stock split and reverse stock split for all periods presented. Use of Estimates The preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities in the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. Actual results could differ materially from those estimates. Significant items subject to such estimates and assumptions include the determination of the fair value of common stock, valuation of deferred tax assets and the related valuation allowance, the potential outcome of uncertain tax positions that have been recognized in the consolidated financial statements or tax returns, valuation of the simple agreements for future equity (“SAFEs”), valuation of convertible notes, valuation of goodwill, stock-based compensation, the assessment of

 
407 useful lives of long-lived assets and intangible assets, contingencies, the valuation of financial instruments, and incremental borrowing rates for operating and finance leases. Concentrations of Risk Concentration of Credit Risk Financial instruments that potentially subject the Company to concentrations of credit risk consist principally of cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, accounts receivable, and short-term investments. The Company maintains cash with financial institutions of high credit quality and does not believe it is exposed to any unusual credit risk beyond the normal credit risk associated with commercial banking relationships. Deposits held with these financial institutions are in excess of the amount of Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation insured limits provided on such deposits. The Company has not experienced any losses related to these concentrations during the periods presented. The Company’s short-term investments are primarily intended to facilitate liquidity and capital preservation and consist predominantly of highly liquid investment-grade fixed-income securities, diversified among industries and individual issuers. The Company’s investment policy is designed to limit exposure from any particular issuer or institution. Significant Customers The table below sets forth concentrations of credit risk with respect to accounts receivable from major customers that accounted for 10% or more of the Company’s total accounts receivable: As of December 31, As of September 30, 2024 2025 2026 (unaudited) Customer A * 13% * Customer E * * 13% ______________ * Less than 10% of total The table below sets forth concentrations of revenue from customers that accounted for 10% or more of the Company’s total revenue: Year Ended December 31, Nine Months Ended September 30, 2023 2024 2025 2025 2026 (unaudited) Customer A * * 12% 11% * Customer B * * 12% 14% * Customer C 43% * * * * Customer D 11% * * * * ______________ * Less than 10% of total Other Concentrations Prior to 2026, the Company obtained substantially all of its compute infrastructure from three cloud service providers (“CSPs”). During the nine months ended September 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company obtained a substantial majority of its compute infrastructure from a limited number of CSPs and other suppliers under long- term hosting and lease agreements. This created dependencies and potential vulnerabilities, in that a disruption affecting these counterparties could have adversely affected the Company’s operations. While the Company is expanding its relationships with its existing CSPs, it is also expanding its compute capacity through commitments 408 with additional CSPs and through compute procured from other sources, including leased infrastructure operated on its behalf. The Company also provides access to its intelligence service through CSP marketplaces, with CSPs acting as collection agents for the Company in these transactions. During the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024, and 2025, revenue generated from sales through CSP marketplaces to customers represented approximately 11%, 32%, and 47% of total revenue, respectively. During the nine months ended September 30, 2025 and 2026 (unaudited), revenue generated from sales through CSP marketplaces to customers represented approximately 48% and 44% of total revenue, respectively. As of December 31, 2024 and 2025 and September 30, 2026 (unaudited), net accounts receivable from sales through CSP marketplaces to customers represented 42%, 60%, and 52% of the Company’s net accounts receivable, respectively. Certain of the CSPs also hold the Company’s non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock and convertible notes. See Notes 9 and 10 for further information. Cash and Cash Equivalents Cash and cash equivalents consist of cash held in checking and interest-bearing accounts as well as investments in money market funds and highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less from the date of purchase. Restricted Cash The Company’s restricted cash is classified as current or noncurrent based on the contractual or estimated term of the remaining restriction and consists of amounts pledged as collateral for the Company’s lease and other contractual obligations. These amounts are restricted from general corporate use and will be released or applied against the related obligations as the underlying conditions are satisfied. Short-Term Investments The Company’s short-term investments primarily consist of debt securities, including: U.S. Treasury and agency securities, corporate debt securities, and commercial paper. The Company determines the appropriate classification of its short-term investments at the time of purchase and reevaluates such designation at each balance sheet date. The Company has classified and accounted for its short-term investments as available-for- sale securities as the Company may sell these securities at any time for use in its current operations or for other purposes, even prior to maturity. As a result, short-term investments, including securities with stated maturities beyond 12 months, are classified within current assets in the consolidated balance sheets. Available-for-sale securities are recorded at fair value each reporting period and are periodically evaluated for impairment at the individual security level. For unrealized losses in securities that the Company intends to hold and will not-more-likely-than-not be required to sell before recovery, the Company further evaluates whether declines in fair value below amortized cost are due to credit or non-credit related factors. The Company considers credit-related impairments to be changes in value that are driven by a change in the creditor’s ability to meet its payment obligations and records an allowance and recognizes a corresponding loss in other income (expense), net when the impairment is incurred. Unrealized non-credit related losses and unrealized gains are reported as a separate component of accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) in the consolidated balance sheets until realized. Realized gains and losses are determined based on the specific identification method and are reported in other income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of operations.

 
409 Variable Interest Entities The Company evaluates its ownership, contractual, and other interests in entities to determine if it has a variable interest in an entity. These evaluations are complex, involve judgment, and use estimates and assumptions based on available historical and prospective information, among other factors. If the Company determines that an entity for which it holds a contractual or ownership interest is a VIE and that the Company is the primary beneficiary, the Company consolidates such entity in its consolidated financial statements. An enterprise having a controlling financial interest in a VIE must consolidate the VIE if it is considered the primary beneficiary, which is described as having both (1) the power to direct the activities of a VIE that most significantly impact the VIE’s economic performance and (2) the right to receive benefits or the obligation to absorb losses of the VIE that potentially could be significant to the VIE. The Company consolidates certain VIEs formed to finance and deploy compute and infrastructure capacity. Refer to Note 7 for further information. Long-Term Benefit Trust In 2023, the Company established the Long-Term Benefit Trust (“LTBT”). The LTBT is intended to operate as an independent body of financially disinterested trustees with expertise in AI safety, national security, public policy, and social enterprise. In connection with establishing the LTBT, the Company created a class of common stock (the “Class T common stock”) that is held exclusively by the LTBT and gives the LTBT authority to elect and remove certain of the Company’s directors. The LTBT is considered a consolidated VIE as it relies on the Company for financial support. The Company is the primary beneficiary of the VIE as it has the power to direct the activities that most significantly impact the LTBT’s economic performance, provides financial support to the LTBT, and would receive the LTBT’s financial assets (other than the Class T common stock) in the event that the LTBT terminates. The Company consolidated the VIE at inception and will perform on-going reassessments of the VIE based on any reconsideration events to reevaluate whether a change to the consolidation conclusion is required each reporting period. The consolidated balance sheets as of December 31, 2024 and 2025 and September 30, 2026 (unaudited) include assets of the LTBT, which can only be used to settle obligations and liabilities of the LTBT. As of December 31, 2024 and 2025 and September 30, 2026 (unaudited), total assets and liabilities of the LTBT were not material. Fair Value Measurements and Financial Instruments Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. In accordance with Accounting Standards Codification (“ASC”) 820, Fair Value Measurement (“ASC 820”), the Company uses the fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used to measure fair value. The hierarchy, as defined below, gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs. The three levels of the fair value hierarchy are set forth below: Level 1: Observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities. Level 2: Observable inputs other than Level 1 prices such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices in markets that are not active or inputs other than the quoted prices that are observable either directly or indirectly for the full term of the assets or liabilities. Level 3: Unobservable inputs in which there is little or no market data and that are significant to the fair value of the assets or liabilities. The Company’s financial instruments include accounts receivable, short-term investments, prepaid expenses and other current assets, other assets, accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities, convertible notes payable, SAFE liabilities, and certain derivative contracts. The estimated fair value of other financial instruments, including cash and restricted cash, are stated at their carrying value which approximates fair value 410 due to the short time to the expected receipt or payment date. Additionally, the carrying amounts of accounts receivable, prepaid expenses and other current assets, accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities approximate fair value due to their short-term nature. Accounts Receivable and Allowances Accounts receivable represent uncollected payments from customers and payments collected by channel partners from customers on the Company’s behalf which have not yet been remitted to the Company. Accounts receivable are recorded at the invoiced amount net of the allowance for credit losses and do not bear interest. The Company’s accounts receivable balances as of December 31, 2023, 2024, and 2025 and September 30, 2026 (unaudited) were $10 million, $95 million, $909 million, and $7.9 billion, respectively. The Company regularly monitors collections and payments from customers and maintains an allowance for credit losses for estimated losses resulting from the inability of customers or channel partners to make or remit required payments. Management estimates the Company’s allowance for credit losses by considering factors such as historical credit loss experience and current conditions, the length of time accounts receivable are past due, customer payment histories, any specific customer collection issues identified, and current market conditions which may affect customer financial condition. This assessment is performed on an aggregate basis when similar characteristics exist within a customer group and on an individual basis when specific customers with collectability risks are identified. The Company writes off accounts receivable against the allowance when management determines a balance is uncollectible and no longer actively pursues collection of the receivable. Changes in the allowance for credit losses were as follows (in millions): Year Ended December 31, Nine Months Ended September 30, 2024 2025 2026 (unaudited) Balance at beginning of period $ — $ 5 $ 17 Change in allowance for credit losses 5 20 94 Write-off of uncollectible accounts receivable — (8) (2) Balance at end of period $ 5 $ 17 $ 109 Property and Equipment, Net Property and equipment is stated at cost less accumulated depreciation. Depreciation is recorded using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the related asset, ranging from three to five years. Leasehold improvements are amortized over the shorter of estimated useful life or the remaining lease term. The Company estimates the useful lives of property and equipment upon initial recognition and periodically evaluates the useful lives and whether events or changes in circumstances warrant a revision to the useful lives. Maintenance and repair costs that do not extend the useful life of the assets are expensed as incurred. When assets are retired or otherwise disposed of, the cost and accumulated depreciation are removed from the accounts and any resulting gain or loss is reflected in the consolidated statements of operations in the period realized. Software Development Costs Software development costs include costs to develop advanced AI models and related software solutions used to deliver the Company’s services to external users. Software development costs also include costs to develop

 
411 software solely for internal use and applications used to support the Company’s operations. Model development costs are generally expensed as incurred due to the significant development uncertainty inherent in the development process. The Company capitalizes qualifying software development costs when (i) management, with relevant authority, has authorized and committed to fund the software project and (ii) it is probable that the project will be completed and the software will be used to perform its intended function. Capitalization ceases when the software is substantially complete and ready for its intended use, including the completion of all significant testing. Software development costs capitalized were not significant for the periods presented. Evaluation of Long-Lived Assets for Impairment Long-lived assets, such as property and equipment, right-of-use (“ROU”) assets, and finite-lived intangible assets subject to amortization, are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset or asset group (collectively, the “asset group”) may not be recoverable. Recoverability of asset groups to be held and used is measured by comparing the carrying amount to the estimated undiscounted future cash flows expected to be generated. If the carrying amount exceeds the undiscounted cash flows, the asset groups are determined to be impaired, and an impairment charge is recognized as the amount by which the carrying amount exceeds its fair value. Intangible Assets, Net Intangible assets which are subject to amortization are amortized on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives, which range from one to six years. The Company reviews intangible assets which are subject to amortization for impairment under the long-lived asset model. Goodwill Goodwill represents the excess of the purchase price in a business combination over the fair value of net tangible and intangible assets acquired. Goodwill is not subject to amortization but is tested for impairment on an annual basis, performed in the fourth quarter of each year, or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying value of the reporting unit may be in excess of the reporting unit’s fair value. Goodwill is tested for impairment at the reporting unit level by first assessing the qualitative factors to determine whether it is more likely than not that the fair value of the Company’s single reporting unit is less than its carrying amount. Qualitative indicators assessed include consideration of macroeconomic, industry, and market conditions, the Company’s overall financial performance, and personnel or strategy changes. Based on the qualitative assessment, if the Company determines that it is more likely than not that the Company’s single reporting unit’s fair value is less than its carrying amount, a quantitative analysis is performed by comparing the fair value of the Company’s single reporting unit to its carrying value. If the carrying amount of the reporting unit exceeds its fair value, an impairment loss is recognized in an amount equal to that excess, limited to the total amount of goodwill allocated to the reporting unit. The Company did not recognize any goodwill during the years ended December 31, 2023 and 2024. No impairment losses related to goodwill were recognized during the year ended December 31, 2025 or the nine months ended September 30, 2026 (unaudited). Acquisitions The Company accounts for acquisitions of entities or asset groups that qualify as businesses in accordance with ASC 805, Business Combinations (“ASC 805”). The purchase price of the acquisition is allocated to the tangible and intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed based on their estimated fair values at the acquisition date. The excess of the purchase price over those fair values is recorded as goodwill. During the measurement period, which may be up to one year from the acquisition date, the Company may record adjustments to the assets acquired and liabilities assumed with the corresponding offset to goodwill. Upon the conclusion of the 412 measurement period or final determination of the values of assets acquired or liabilities assumed, whichever comes first, any subsequent adjustments are recorded in the consolidated statements of operations. Leases The Company determines if an arrangement is a lease at inception. The Company evaluates the classification of leases at commencement and, as necessary, at modification. The Company, as the lessee, classifies leases with lease terms longer than 12 months as either operating or finance. A lease is classified as a finance lease if it meets any of the finance lease classification criteria in ASC 842 at lease commencement; all other leases are classified as operating leases. The Company’s finance leases are generally those leases that allow the Company to utilize the asset for a major part of its estimated economic life, that have discounted lease payments that are substantially all the estimated fair value of the asset, or that include a purchase option which the Company is reasonably certain to exercise. The Company leases facilities and equipment under operating and finance leases. The Company determines whether an arrangement is or contains a lease at inception and records lease liabilities and right-of-use assets on its consolidated balance sheets at lease commencement. Where the Company’s leases do not provide an implicit rate, the Company determines its incremental borrowing rate based on the information available at commencement date in determining the present value of lease payments. The determination of the incremental borrowing rate is based on an estimate of the Company’s unsecured borrowing rate, adjusted for tenor and collateralized security features. Lease liabilities are recognized at the present value of the future lease payments at the lease commencement date. ROU assets are measured based on the corresponding lease liability adjusted for (i) payments made to the lessor at or before the commencement date, (ii) initial direct costs incurred and (iii) tenant incentives received, incurred or payable under the lease. The Company does not assume renewals or early terminations of its leases unless it is reasonably certain to exercise these options at commencement. Operating lease cost is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term. Finance lease ROU assets are amortized on a straight-line basis over the shorter of the estimated useful life of the underlying asset or, where title does not transfer at the end of the lease term and the Company is not reasonably certain to exercise a purchase option, the lease term, and are recognized within operating expenses based on the nature of the leased asset. The interest component of a finance lease is recognized using the effective interest method over the lease term and is presented separately from the amortization of the related ROU asset. Operating lease ROU assets and operating lease liabilities are presented separately on the consolidated balance sheets. Finance lease ROU assets are included in property and equipment, net. Finance lease liabilities are included in accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities, and in other noncurrent liabilities. The Company’s lease agreements may contain lease and non-lease components. Non-lease components related to the asset being leased are not separated from the lease components and are accounted for as a single lease component for all existing classes of assets. The Company made an accounting policy election for lease agreements with a term of 12 months or less and does not recognize ROU assets and lease liabilities in respect of those agreements. Any payments related to short-term leases are expensed as incurred. Variable lease payments are expensed as incurred and are mainly composed of utilities, common area maintenance, and other operating expenses. Similar to other long-lived assets discussed above, management assesses ROU assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of such assets may not be recoverable. Finance lease ROU assets are assessed for impairment together with the Company’s other property and

 
413 equipment. For leased assets, such circumstances would include the decision to enter into a sublease for which estimated cash flows do not fully cover the costs of the associated lease. Revenue Recognition The Company generates revenue from customers, including enterprises and prosumers, utilizing its intelligence service, which enables customers to submit text, documents, and other materials (“Prompts”), and receive AI- generated results (“Results”) from its proprietary Claude model family. Prompts and Results are measured in the number of tokens consumed. The Company provides the intelligence service through its web, mobile, and desktop interfaces and APIs as well as through CSP marketplaces that distribute the intelligence service to the Company’s customers. The intelligence service is not available for on-premise download or hosting by customers. The Company accounts for revenue under ASC 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers. Revenue is recognized based on the amount of consideration the Company expects to receive when the Company provides its intelligence service to customers. Revenue excludes amounts collected on behalf of third parties, such as sales and indirect taxes, as well as estimated concessions, credits, and refunds. The Company’s intelligence service is provided on a consumption or subscription basis. Revenue is recognized when customers use the Company’s intelligence service, based on the quantity of tokens consumed. Intelligence service provided on a subscription basis is subject to usage limits that reset over short periods, which results in revenue being recognized ratably over the subscription period, which is generally 12 months or less. Payment terms vary by customer and sales channel but are generally less than 60 days. Subscription fees are generally prepaid. Certain enterprise contracts may include minimum spend commitments. When the Company utilizes CSP marketplaces that distribute the intelligence service to customers, the customer receives the same intelligence service as is available through its web, mobile, and desktop interfaces and APIs, and the intelligence service represents a single promise in customer contracts. In these arrangements, the Company is the principal and recognizes revenue on a gross basis because the Company has a direct contractual relationship with customers, is primarily responsible for providing the intelligence service to customers, and establishes pricing. The CSPs in these arrangements do not obtain control of the Company’s intelligence service at any point prior to transfer to the customer. Deferred Revenue Deferred revenue consists of amounts billed or received in advance of the Company satisfying its performance obligations, and is recognized as revenue as services are delivered to customers. Deferred revenue relates primarily to subscriptions that are subject to usage limits that reset over short periods, which results in revenue being recognized ratably over the subscription period, which is generally 12 months or less. Compute and Infrastructure Compute and infrastructure expenses primarily consist of costs attributable to operating the Company’s technology infrastructure, which supports the full range of workloads for the Company’s models, including research, model development, serving customers, and internal usage of Claude. These costs primarily consist of cloud compute fees paid to CSPs under committed and on-demand arrangements, including storage, networking and connectivity, and related support costs, infrastructure costs associated with serving customer workloads through partner channels, colocation facility costs, equipment leases and committed power costs associated with 414 the Company’s data center operations, and third-party application infrastructure software costs directly related to the Company’s compute operations. Personnel Personnel expenses primarily consist of stock-based compensation, including expense related to stock options, restricted stock units (“RSUs”), and restricted stock awards, cash compensation, including base salaries and bonuses, employee benefits, including health and welfare benefits, and employer payroll taxes. Bartz Settlement Bartz settlement consists of the charge the Company recorded in 2025 to settle the Bartz copyright infringement suit. Refer to Note 13 for further information. Sales, Marketing, and Partnerships Sales, marketing, and partnerships expenses primarily consist of channel partner costs and marketing and advertising costs, including media and public relations spend. Advertising costs are expensed as incurred. Advertising expenses were $33 million and $147 million for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2025, respectively. Advertising expenses incurred in 2023 were not material. Other Operating and Administrative Other operating and administrative expenses primarily consist of charitable donations expense related to the Company’s donation matching program, vendor costs related to data quality and performance evaluation services, information technology and cloud software costs, payment processing and platform fees, facility and occupancy costs, non-income taxes, professional services costs, bad debt expense, and depreciation and amortization related to non-data center assets. Stock-Based Compensation The Company’s equity incentive plan provides for the granting of stock options, RSUs, and restricted stock awards to employees, consultants, officers, and directors. The Company measures compensation cost for stock-based awards at grant-date fair value and recognizes it over the requisite service period. The Company accounts for forfeitures when they occur. The fair value of stock-based awards, granted or modified, is determined on the grant date (or modification or acquisition dates, if applicable) using appropriate valuation techniques. Stock-based compensation is included within personnel expenses in the consolidated statements of operations. The Company incurred stock-based compensation expense of $29 million, $192 million, and $1.2 billion for the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024, and 2025, respectively. The Company incurred stock-based compensation expense of $591 million and $3.3 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 and 2026 (unaudited), respectively. The tax benefits recognized in the consolidated statements of operations for stock-based compensation arrangements were not material during the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024, and 2025. During the nine months ended September 30, 2025 and 2026 (unaudited), tax benefits were $2 million and $276 million, respectively. Stock Options Stock-based compensation expense is recognized on a straight-line basis over the period during which an employee is required to provide services in exchange for the award (generally the vesting period of the award). The Company determines the fair value of stock options on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes-Merton option pricing model which is impacted by the estimated fair value of the Company’s common stock, as well as

 
415 changes in assumptions regarding a number of highly complex and subjective variables. These variables are summarized as follows: • Fair value of common stock – Until the Company’s common stock is publicly traded, the Company must estimate the fair value of common stock. The Company’s board of directors (the “Board”) considers numerous objective and subjective factors to determine the fair value of the Company’s common stock including: contemporaneous third-party valuations of the Company’s common stock, price paid by investors for the Company’s common and redeemable convertible preferred stock, actual and forecasted operating and financial performance, market conditions, performance of comparable publicly traded companies, developments and milestones within the Company, the rights, preferences, and privileges of the Company’s common and redeemable convertible preferred stock, and the likelihood and timing of achieving a liquidity event, among other factors. • Expected volatility – Expected volatility is a measure of the amount by which the stock price is expected to fluctuate. Since the Company has no trading history of its common stock, it estimates the expected volatility of its underlying common stock as of the grant date of its stock options by taking the weighted-average historical volatility of a group of comparable publicly traded companies over a period equal to the expected life of the options. • Expected term – Expected term represents the period over which the Company anticipates stock-based awards to be outstanding. The Company estimates the expected term based on the options’ vesting term and contractual terms, such that the expected life is equal to the average of the stock-based award’s weighted-average vesting period and its contractual term. • Risk-free interest rate – The risk-free interest rate used is based on the implied yield in effect at the time of grant of U.S. Treasury securities with maturities similar to the expected term of the stock options. • Expected dividend yield – The expected dividend yield is zero, as the Company has never declared or paid any dividends and has no current plans to do so. Restricted Stock Units The Company measures and recognizes stock-based compensation expense for RSUs based on the estimated fair value of the underlying common stock on the date of grant. The Company’s RSUs vest upon the satisfaction of both service and performance conditions. The service condition for these awards is generally satisfied over a four- year vesting period. The performance condition is satisfied upon the occurrence of either (i) a qualifying change in control of the Company or (ii) a listing of the Company’s equity securities on an established securities market (including through a traditional public offering, direct listing, or business combination with a special purpose acquisition company), in each case, on or before the seventh anniversary of the grant date, as further defined in such RSU agreements. If the performance condition is not satisfied within seven years of the grant date, all unvested RSUs are forfeited. Compensation cost related to these RSUs must be recognized over the requisite service period using the accelerated attribution method, if it is probable that the performance-based vesting condition will be satisfied. The performance-based vesting condition will be deemed probable of being satisfied upon either the consummation of an acquisition or change in control or the Company’s initial public offering. As of December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (unaudited), no stock-based compensation expense had been recognized for the RSUs because management determined that it is not probable that the performance condition will be achieved. 416 Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock The Company records shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock at their respective fair values on the dates of issuance, net of issuance costs. The redeemable convertible preferred stock is recorded outside of permanent equity because it is not mandatorily redeemable and redemption is contingent upon the occurrence of certain deemed liquidation events that are not solely within the Company’s control. The Company has not adjusted the carrying values of the redeemable convertible preferred stock to the liquidation preferences of such shares because it is not probable that a deemed liquidation event would occur that would obligate the Company to pay the liquidation preferences to holders of shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock. Subsequent adjustments of the carrying values to the liquidation preferences will be made only when it becomes probable that such a deemed liquidation event will occur. Foreign Currency The functional currencies of the Company’s foreign subsidiaries are the local currency or the U.S. dollar depending on the nature of the subsidiaries’ activities. Monetary assets and liabilities, and transactions denominated in currencies other than the functional currency are remeasured to the functional currency at the exchange rate in effect at the end of the period and are recorded in the current period consolidated statements of operations. Gains and losses resulting from remeasurement are recorded in foreign exchange gains (losses), net within other income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of operations. Subsidiary assets and liabilities with non-U.S. dollar functional currencies are translated at the month-end rate, retained earnings and other equity items are translated at historical rates, and revenue and expenses are translated at average exchange rates during the year. Cumulative translation adjustments are recorded within accumulated other comprehensive income (loss), a separate component of total stockholders’ deficit in the Company’s consolidated balance sheets. Loss Contingencies The Company is periodically involved in various legal claims, proceedings and other regulatory and administrative proceedings that may arise in the ordinary course of business. Certain of these matters may include speculative claims for substantial or indeterminate amounts of damages. The Company routinely reviews the status of each significant matter and assesses its potential financial exposure. The Company records a liability when it believes that it is both probable that a loss has been incurred and the amount can be reasonably estimated. If the Company determines that a loss is reasonably possible and the loss or range of loss can be reasonably estimated, the Company discloses the possible loss in the consolidated financial statements. Because of inherent uncertainties related to these legal matters, significant judgment is required to determine both the probability and the estimated amount of loss. These estimates have been based on the Company’s assessment of the facts and circumstances at each balance sheet date and are subject to change based on new information and future events. As additional information becomes available, the Company reassesses its potential liability and may revise its estimates. If one or more matters were resolved against the Company for amounts in excess of management’s expectations, the Company’s results of operations and financial condition, including in a particular reporting period in which any such outcome becomes probable and estimable, could be materially adversely affected. Share Repurchase Share repurchases are recorded on the trade date. When shares are immediately retired, the value of repurchased shares is deducted from stockholders’ deficit through common stock with the excess over par value recorded to accumulated deficit.

 
417 Income Taxes The Company uses the asset and liability method to account for income taxes. Current income tax expense or benefit represents the amount of income taxes expected to be payable or refundable for the current year. Under this method, deferred income tax assets and liabilities are determined based on differences between the financial statement reporting and tax bases of assets and liabilities and net operating loss and credit carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates applied to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. Valuation allowances are established when necessary to reduce deferred tax assets to the amounts that are more-likely-than-not expected to be realized based on the weighting of positive and negative evidence. Future realization of deferred tax assets ultimately depends on the existence of sufficient taxable income of the appropriate character (for example, ordinary income or capital gain) within the carryback or carryforward periods available under the applicable tax law. The Company regularly reviews the deferred tax assets for recoverability based on historical taxable income, projected future taxable income, the expected timing of the reversals of existing temporary differences and tax planning strategies. The Company’s judgment regarding future profitability may change due to many factors, including future market conditions and the ability to successfully execute the business plans and/or tax planning strategies. Should there be a change in the ability to recover deferred tax assets, the Company’s income tax provision would increase or decrease in the period in which the assessment is changed. The Company treats Net CFC Tested Income (formerly referred to as Global Intangible Low-Taxed Income or “GILTI”) as a period cost. The Company accounts for uncertain tax positions in accordance with ASC 740-10, Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes. The Company recognizes the tax effects of an uncertain tax position only if such position is more likely than not to be sustained based solely on its technical merits as of the reporting date and only in an amount more likely than not to be sustained upon review by the tax authorities. The Company recognizes accrued interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits in the provision for income taxes in the consolidated statements of operations. Net Loss per Share Basic and diluted net loss per share attributable to common stockholders is computed in conformity with the two-class method required for participating securities. The two-class method requires income available to common stockholders for the period to be allocated between common stock and participating securities based upon their respective rights to receive dividends as if all income for the period had been distributed. The Company considers all series of its redeemable convertible preferred stock to be participating securities as the holders of such stock have the right to participate on a pari passu basis in any distributions to common stockholders. The holders of the redeemable convertible preferred stock would be entitled to dividends in preference to common stockholders, at specified rates, if declared. Any remaining dividend amounts would then be distributed to the holders of common stock, restricted common stock, and the holders of the redeemable convertible preferred stock on a pro-rata basis assuming conversion of all redeemable convertible preferred stock into common stock. These participating securities do not contractually require the holders of such shares to participate in the Company’s losses. As such, net losses for the periods presented were not allocated to the Company’s participating securities. Basic net loss per share is computed by dividing the net loss attributable to common stockholders by the weighted-average number of shares of common stock outstanding during the period, less shares subject to repurchase. The diluted net loss per share is computed by giving effect to all potentially dilutive securities outstanding for the period using the treasury stock method or the if-converted method if the effect is dilutive. For periods in which the Company reports net losses, diluted net loss per share is the same as basic net loss per share, because all potentially dilutive securities are anti-dilutive. 418 Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements In November 2023, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (“FASB”) issued Accounting Standards Update (“ASU”) 2023-07, Segment Reporting (Topic 280): Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures (“ASU 2023-07”), which requires disclosure of incremental segment information on an annual and interim basis, primarily through enhanced disclosures of segment expenses. Level 3 Assets During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company entered into a contract to receive warrant rights to acquire common shares of a privately-held company as consideration under an agreement entered into but not yet commenced. The warrant rights are freestanding financial instruments that meet the definition of a derivative as they contain a net settlement feature. The warrants have not been designated as hedging instruments and will be granted and recognized as lease incentives upon commencement of the related arrangements and recognized as a reduction of the related ROU assets. The Company estimated the fair value of the warrant rights using a probability-weighted expected return method. In applying this method, the Company utilized Level 3 valuation inputs based on information available, including terms and features of the warrant rights and other outstanding classes of the issuer’s equity securities, observable transactions in the issuer’s securities such as its most recent financing round, estimates of equity volatility, and expected time to a liquidity event. The initial fair value of the warrant rights was recognized as a derivative asset classified within other assets on the consolidated balance sheets, with a corresponding deferred liability classified within other noncurrent liabilities. (“Amazon”), which included a commitment to sell 19.3 million shares of the Company’s Series G-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock at $259.1364 per share. (“AMD”) to secure AMD-based compute and infrastructure capacity. Pursuant to the terms of the Hardware Supply Agreement, AMD committed to purchase, at the Company’s election, up to $5.0 billion of the Company’s Class N common stock, if certain conditions are achieved (the “purchased put option”). The purchased put option is recorded at fair value within other assets, noncurrent. Changes in fair value are recognized in other income (expense), net. The estimated fair value of the note purchase agreements and the purchased put option (collectively, the “partner financing arrangements”) was determined by using a probability-weighted expected return method. The fair value of the underlying equity securities was determined by using a hybrid approach comprising a contingent claims analysis (“CCA”) and a common stock equivalent (“CSE”) method. Assumptions included assumed future liquidity and financing events, the terms and features of the partner financing arrangements, weights applied to each scenario, discount rates, applicable risk free rates, the fair value of the underlying equity securities, and a discount for lack of marketability.

The analysis estimates the fair value of the convertible notes based on the probability-weighted expected future investment returns, considering possible outcomes available to the note holder, including conversions to redeemable convertible preferred stock, Class N common stock, and maturity. Assumptions include weight applied to the CCA and CSE methods, assumed volatility, time to a liquidity event, need for and terms of financings or expected financings, and the risk free interest rate. Variable Interest Entities The Company consolidates certain VIEs formed to finance and deploy compute and infrastructure capacity. As of September 30, 2026 (unaudited), assets that are not, except as may be expressly provided in any contract or instrument entered into by these VIEs, generally available to satisfy the obligations of any person other than these VIEs were $2.7 billion, primarily included in property and equipment, net, and operating lease right-of-use assets. The Company guarantees certain consolidated VIE obligations; as a result, these VIEs’ creditors have recourse to the general credit of the Company. As of September 30, 2026 (unaudited), liabilities related to these consolidated VIEs were $2.8 billion, which primarily included $1.3 billion and $178 million of noncurrent and current operating lease liabilities, respectively, and $989 million of finance lease liabilities included in other noncurrent liabilities. In certain instances, these consolidated VIEs have variable interests in the non-consolidated lessor VIEs described below. The Company may satisfy certain VIE rent obligations through the issuance of convertible promissory notes in lieu of cash. These VIEs guarantee the Company’s obligations under the convertible promissory note and grant the lessor a security interest in the leased assets to secure them, up to the amount of notes outstanding to the lessor. As of September 30, 2026 (unaudited), no convertible promissory notes had been issued. Refer to Note 9 for further information. As of December 31, 2025, the assets and liabilities of these consolidated VIEs were not material.

 
431 Certain data center and power developers with which the Company has leases and cost reimbursement arrangements are VIEs. This judgment includes, but is not limited to, consideration of the expected economic life of the leased assets relative to the term of the Company’s leases, estimated fair value of the facilities, and each entity’s ability to generate cash flows during and after the lease term. Decisions pertaining to the remarketing of the assets, including but not limited to, negotiating with future lessees and sales of the assets, were determined to have the most significant impact on the economic performance of the VIEs. Because the Company has determined that it does not have the power to direct the activities that most significantly impact the economic performance of these entities, it is not the primary beneficiary. Convertible Notes, Revolving Credit Agreement and SAFEs Convertible Notes The Company has entered into note purchase agreements which provide for the issuance of one or more convertible notes. To the extent that the note purchase agreements create an obligation to issue notes in the future, these obligations are accounted for as derivative liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets until the related note is issued. Google Google 2023 Note Purchase Agreement In September 2023, the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (“Google 2023 NPA”) with Google LLC (“Google”), for the issuance of convertible promissory notes in an aggregate principal amount of up to $2.0 billion, issuable in three tranches. The Company issued the first tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $500 million in September 2023, the second tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $750 million in September 2024, and the third tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $750 million in September 2025. The notes issued under Google 2023 NPA bore interest at a rate of 10.0% per annum, compounded annually, and payable upon maturity, 48 months after the respective issuance date. The Company also has a commercial agreement with Google for the provision of intelligence service. In connection with the Company’s Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing in 2025, the first and second tranches of notes issued under Google 2023 NPA converted in full into an aggregate of 12.7 million shares of the Company’s Series E-3 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $44.8692 per share and an aggregate of 15.3 million shares of Series E-4 non-voting redeemable convertible

 
435 preferred stock at a conversion price of $50.4779 per share, respectively. The conversion prices reflect the contractual discounts to the Series E-1 original issuance price of $56.0865 per share. As of December 31, 2025, $750 million aggregate principal amount remained outstanding under the third tranche of notes issued under Google 2023 NPA. In January 2026, in connection with the initial closing of the Series G-1 financing, the third tranche of notes issued under Google 2023 NPA converted in full into 3.3 million shares of Series G-4 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $233.2228 per share. The conversion price reflects the contractual discounts to the Series G-1 price of $259.1364 per share. As of September 30, 2026 (unaudited), no amounts remain outstanding under Google 2023 NPA. Google 2024 Note Purchase Agreement In August 2024, the Company entered into an additional note purchase agreement (“Google 2024 NPA”) with Google for the issuance of a convertible promissory note in an aggregate principal amount of approximately $1.3 billion. Such note bore interest at a rate of 8.5% per annum compounded annually, and, unless earlier converted or repaid, was payable upon maturity in August 2030. In connection with the Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing in 2025, the note issued under Google 2024 NPA was converted in full into an aggregate of 24.2 million shares of Series E-5 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $53.2822 per share, reflecting a contractual discount to the Series E-1 original issuance price of $56.0865 per share. As of December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (unaudited), no amounts remain outstanding under Google 2024 NPA. Google 2026 Note Purchase Agreement (Unaudited) In March 2026 (unaudited), the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (“Google 2026 NPA”) under which, subject to certain conditions, up to $30.0 billion of convertible promissory notes or non-voting common stock through December 31, 2030 may be issued. Non-voting common stock would be issued at the 30-day trailing volume-weighted average price and, to the extent issued, the notes will bear interest at 9.0% per annum compounded annually, payable at maturity, and mature six years after issuance, unless earlier repaid or converted pursuant to the terms of the agreement. In May 2026 (unaudited), Google invested $10.0 billion in the Company’s Series H redeemable convertible preferred stock financing, which reduced the amount available for issuance under the Google 2026 NPA to $20.0 billion. As of September 30, 2026, no non-voting common stock or notes had been issued under the Google 2026 NPA. Amazon Amazon 2023 and 2024 Note Purchase Agreements In September 2023, the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (“Amazon 2023 NPA”) with Amazon for the issuance of convertible promissory notes in an aggregate principal amount of up to $4.0 billion issuable in two tranches. The Company issued the first tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $1.2 billion in September 2023, and the second tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $3.4 billion in March 2024, reflecting an issuance premium to the $2.8 billion in proceeds received for the second tranche of notes. In November 2024, the Company entered into an additional note purchase agreement (“Amazon 2024 NPA”) with Amazon for the issuance of convertible promissory notes in an aggregate principal amount of up to $4.0 billion, issuable in three tranches. The Company issued the first tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $1.3 billion in November 2024, the second tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $1.3 billion in May 2025, and the third tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $1.4 billion in November 2025. 436 The notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA bear interest at a rate of 8.0% per annum compounded annually and payable upon maturity, and mature 10 years after the respective issuance date, unless earlier repaid or converted. The first tranche of notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA bears interest at a rate of 8.5% per annum, compounded annually and payable at maturity, and matures in November 2034, unless earlier repaid or converted. The second and third tranche of notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA are each non-interest bearing and mature in May 2035 and November 2035, respectively, unless earlier repaid or converted. The notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA and Amazon 2024 NPA are convertible into non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price equal to the lesser of (i) $20.9280 per share (in the case of notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA), or $50.4779 per share (in the case of notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA), and (ii) the price per share in the Company’s most recent (1) preferred stock equity financing (in the case of the notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA) or (2) qualified equity financing (in the case of the notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA), subject, in each case, to Amazon’s ownership cap, as described below. In connection with certain liquidation transactions, Amazon may, in lieu of converting such notes at the applicable conversion price, elect to receive cash in an amount equal to the outstanding principal amount and accrued but unpaid interest thereon. Pursuant to the terms of Amazon 2024 NPA, the Company may be required to make additional cash payments to Amazon calculated as set forth in Amazon 2024 NPA in connection with certain liquidation transactions. In addition, in connection with an initial public offering, direct listing, or special purpose acquisition company transaction, any outstanding principal amount and accrued but unpaid interest thereon under the applicable Amazon NPA will automatically convert into shares of the Company’s Class N common stock at a conversion price equal to the lower of (i) $2.0928 per share, in the case of Amazon 2023 NPA, or $5.0478 per share, in the case of Amazon 2024 NPA, and (ii) the price per share of the common stock offered to the public in such transaction. Any portion of Amazon’s notes that cannot convert due to Amazon’s ownership cap will automatically convert, subject to Amazon’s ownership cap, into shares of Class N common stock at the close of each fiscal quarter following an initial public offering at a conversion price equal to the lowest of (i) the applicable conversion price set forth above, (ii) the price per share of the common stock offered to the public in connection with such initial public offering, and (iii) the then-current market price of the Company’s common stock based on a 10-day volume-weighted trailing average trading price. The notes issued under an Amazon NPA may also be settled in cash at maturity or, at Amazon’s election, by set-off against amounts Amazon owes the Company under certain commercial agreements with Amazon. Any conversion of the notes issued under an Amazon NPA is subject to Amazon’s aggregate ownership cap, which is waivable at Amazon’s option. If any portion of the notes issued under an Amazon NPA cannot be converted without exceeding the ownership cap, the portion that could not be so converted will be re-issued as a non- interest bearing convertible rollover note, with a maturity date that is 10 years from the issuance date of such rollover note. Upon the occurrence of certain events of default as specified in the applicable Amazon NPA, the Company may be required, depending on the nature of the event of default, to repay in cash the then-outstanding principal amount that has not been converted either (i) in full upon demand of the holder or (ii) in equal installments over a four-year period. In connection with the Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing in 2025, the first and second tranches of notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA were converted into an aggregate of 95.3 million shares of Series E-2 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $20.9280 per share. A portion of the notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA did not convert pursuant to Amazon’s ownership cap, and were re-issued as a non-interest bearing rollover note with an aggregate principal amount of $3.1 billion, maturing in March 2034. The rollover note has substantially identical conversion and repayment terms as set forth above, in each case, subject to Amazon’s ownership cap. In connection with the Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing, the conversion provisions of the notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA were triggered. However, due to Amazon’s ownership cap, none of the notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA converted. As a result, the first tranche was re-issued as a non-interest bearing rollover note with an aggregate

 
437 principal amount of $1.3 billion maturing in January 2035 and the second and third tranches remained outstanding. Such rollover note has substantially identical conversion and repayment terms as set forth above, in each case, and converts subject to Amazon’s ownership cap. Subsequently, in connection with the Company’s Series F-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing in 2025, a portion of the rollover note issued under Amazon 2023 NPA converted into an aggregate of 20.7 million shares of Series F-2 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $20.9280 per share. The remaining balance of such rollover note was re-issued as a non-interest bearing amended and restated rollover note with a principal amount of approximately $2.6 billion, maturing in March 2034. The notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA did not convert in connection with the Series F-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing due to Amazon’s ownership cap. As of December 31, 2025, $2.6 billion aggregate principal amount of the amended and restated rollover note issued under Amazon 2023 NPA remains outstanding and all three tranches of notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA, with the first tranche re-issued as a non-interest bearing rollover note, remain outstanding with an aggregate principal balance of $4.0 billion. In January and February 2026, in connection with the Company’s Series G-1 financing, a portion of the second amended and restated non-interest bearing rollover note issued under Amazon 2023 NPA was converted into an aggregate of 20.6 million shares of the Company’s Series G-3 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a price of $20.9280 per share. The remaining balance of such non-interest bearing rollover note was re-issued as a non-interest bearing amended and restated rollover note with a principal amount of approximately $2.2 billion, maturing in March 2034. As of September 30, 2026 (unaudited), the amended and restated rollover note issued under Amazon 2023 NPA remained outstanding with an aggregate principal amount of approximately $2.2 billion, and all notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA remained outstanding with an aggregate principal balance of $4.0 billion. SAFEs During the year ended December 31, 2023, the Company issued SAFEs with an aggregate purchase amount of $122 million that entitled investors to participate in future equity financings through share-settled redemption of the amount invested. Of this amount, $1 million converted into shares of Series C-1 convertible preferred stock during the year ended December 31, 2023, and $121 million converted into shares of Series D-1 and D-2 convertible preferred stock during the year ended December 31, 2024. Conversion prices were determined based on the purchase amount divided by the per-share price of the applicable series of preferred stock, multiplied by a stipulated discount rate, if applicable. The Company determined that the SAFEs are not legal form debt (i.e., no creditors’ rights). The monetary settlement amount of the SAFEs is based upon a fixed or determinable amount known at inception, and the number of equity shares received upon conversion is variable. In such circumstances, equity classification is not appropriate because such contracts that are settled based upon a fixed amount do not expose the holder to risks and rewards similar to those of an equity-holder, therefore, the SAFEs would have been classified as marked-to- market liabilities pursuant to ASC 480. As of December 31, 2024 and 2025, as well as September 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company had no outstanding SAFEs. Fair Value Option The Company elected to account for the SAFEs and the convertible notes using the fair value option pursuant to ASC 825 and changes in fair value related to the SAFEs and convertible notes are recorded in change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the Company’s consolidated statements of operations (Note 4). The Company elected to account for the convertible notes using the fair value option pursuant to ASC 825 to eliminate the accounting complexity that would otherwise result from separately accounting for the liability and equity components of the convertible notes under the traditional bifurcation model. The estimated fair value of the convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs is determined by using a scenario-based analysis that estimated the fair value of the convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs based on the probability-weighted present value of expected future investment returns, considering possible outcomes available to the SAFE and convertible note holder, including conversions to redeemable convertible preferred stock, Class N common stock and maturity. Issuance costs were expensed as incurred and are reflected in other income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of operations. Changes in fair value of the SAFEs and convertible notes and accrued interest are recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the consolidated statements of operations. There were no changes in fair value attributable to credit risk recognized as of December 31, 2023, 2024, and 2025, as well as September 30, 2026 (unaudited).

 
439 Derivative Liability As of December 31, 2024, the Company had a derivative liability representing the subsequent note tranche rights on Amazon 2024 NPA. The Company applied the terms of the subsequent note tranche rights for a written call option and purchased put option scenarios and calculated a derivative liability. The changes in the fair value of the derivative liability were recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the consolidated statements of operations. Upon the second closing and third closing of the Amazon 2024 NPA during 2025, the related tranche rights were exercised and thus the derivative liability was settled and derecognized in full through the issuance of the convertible notes, with no remaining tranche rights outstanding as of December 31, 2025. Revolving Credit Agreement On May 14, 2025, the Company entered into a credit agreement (the “Credit Agreement”), by and among the Company, the lenders from time to time party thereto (collectively the “Lenders”), and Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc., as Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent for the Lenders. The Credit Agreement provides for a senior secured revolving credit facility in an aggregate principal amount of $2.5 billion, with a $400 million letter of credit sublimit. The obligations under the Credit Agreement mature on May 14, 2030, subject to an earlier springing maturity date that is contingent upon the outstanding amount of convertible notes issued by the Company on the date that is 91 days prior to the maturity of such notes. The proceeds of the credit facility may be used for working capital, general corporate purposes, and other lawful purposes. The Company may request borrowings in U.S. dollars or certain other agreed currencies, subject to the terms of the Credit Agreement. Borrowings under the Credit Agreement bear interest at rates based on either the Alternate Base Rate, Term SOFR or other applicable benchmarks, plus an applicable margin. The Company is required to pay commitment fees on the unused portion of the credit facility and fees in connection with letters of credit. The obligations under the Credit Agreement are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries of the Company and are secured by substantially all of the assets of the Company and the subsidiary guarantors, subject to certain exceptions and exclusions set forth in the Credit Agreement. The Credit Agreement contains customary affirmative and negative covenants, including, but not limited to, restrictions on additional indebtedness, liens, asset sales, investments, mergers, and restricted payments. The Company is also subject to a financial covenant which requires the Company to maintain liquidity of at least $500 million as of the last day of each fiscal quarter. The agreement also includes customary events of default, which, if triggered, could result in the acceleration of amounts due under the credit facility. In September 2025, the Company executed an amendment to the Credit Agreement increasing the aggregate principal amount of revolving credit commitments by $250 million to $2.8 billion. In November 2025, the Company executed a second amendment to the Credit Agreement, providing incremental revolving commitments in an aggregate principal amount of $500 million. Following the second amendment, the aggregate principal amount of revolving commitments totals $3.3 billion. In February 2026 (unaudited), the Company executed a third amendment to the Credit Agreement, increasing the letter of credit sublimit by $600 million to $1.0 billion. In September 2026 (unaudited), the Company amended and restated the Credit Agreement, increasing the letter of credit sublimit to $15.0 billion, and providing incremental revolving commitments of $11.7 billion (as amended and restated, the “A&R Credit Agreement”). Following the amendment and restatement, the aggregate principal amount of revolving commitments totals $15.0 billion. The A&R Credit Agreement also extended the maturity to September 2031, subject to an earlier springing maturity date under certain conditions, and increased the minimum liquidity required under the financial covenant to $5.0 billion, beginning with the fiscal quarter ending December 31, 2026. 440 As of December 31, 2025, the Company had no borrowings drawn under the revolving credit facility, and $4 million of standby letters of credit outstanding under the credit facility. The Company was in compliance with all covenants under the Credit Agreement as of December 31, 2025. The Company recognized $5 million in access fees during the year ended December 31, 2025, which are amortized as interest expense over the term of the credit facility. As of September 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company had no borrowings drawn under the revolving credit facility and $205 million of standby letters of credit were outstanding under the credit facility. The Company was in compliance with all covenants under the A&R Credit Agreement as of September 30, 2026 (unaudited). 10.
