443 Dividend Rights The holders of the outstanding shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock are entitled to receive, when and if declared by the Board, and prior and in preference to dividends on the Company’s common stock, dividends at the per annum rate of 6% of the applicable original issue price per share (“OIP”). Such dividends shall not be cumulative. After payment of such dividends, any additional dividends shall be distributed among the holders of common stock and redeemable convertible preferred stock in proportion to the number of shares of common stock that would be held by each such holder if all shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock were converted to common stock calculated on the record date for determination of holders entitled to such dividends. No dividends have been declared or paid through December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (unaudited). Liquidation Preference In the event of any Liquidation Transaction (defined, generally, as any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the Company or deemed liquidation event), the holders of redeemable convertible preferred stock shall be entitled to receive, prior and in preference to any distribution of any of the assets of the Company to the holders of common stock, by reason of their ownership thereof, an amount per share equal to the OIP for each outstanding share of redeemable convertible preferred stock then held (as adjusted for stock splits, stock dividends, reclassifications and the like), plus any declared but unpaid dividends on such shares. If, upon the occurrence of such event, the assets and funds thus distributed among the holders of redeemable convertible preferred stock shall be insufficient to permit the payment to such holders of the full aforesaid preferential amounts, then the entire assets and funds of the Company legally available for distribution shall be distributed ratably among the holders of redeemable convertible preferred stock in proportion to the preferential amount each such holder is otherwise entitled to receive, and provided that the holders of redeemable convertible preferred stock will be treated on an as-converted basis if, as a result of an actual conversion, such holder would receive, in the aggregate, an amount greater than the amount that would be distributed to such holder if such holder did not convert such series of preferred stock into shares of such series of common stock. Conversion Each share of redeemable convertible preferred stock is convertible into fully paid and non-assessable shares of Class A common stock, in the case of the Series A, Series C-1, Series D-1, Series D-2, Series E-1, Series F-1, Series G-1, and Series H-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock. Each share of non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock is convertible into fully paid and non-assessable shares of Class N common stock (non-voting common stock), in the case of the Series B, Series C-2, Series D-3, Series E-2, Series E-3, Series E-4, Series E-5, Series F-2, Series F-3, Series F-4, Series G-2, Series G-3, Series G-4, Series H-2, Series H-3, and Series H-4 non- voting redeemable convertible preferred stock. • Optional conversion – Each share of redeemable convertible preferred stock is convertible into Class A common stock or Class N common stock, as applicable, at any time after the issuance of shares at the option of the holder. The conversion rate is determined by dividing the applicable original issue price by the conversion price. As of December 31, 2024, the conversion ratio for all series of redeemable convertible preferred stock was 10:1. In connection with the Series E redeemable convertible preferred stock financing during the year ended December 31, 2025, the issuance of Series E-2 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at $20.9280 per share triggered weighted-average antidilution adjustments to the conversion prices of the Series D-1, D-2, and D-3 redeemable convertible preferred stock. As of December 31, 2025, the conversion ratio for all series of redeemable convertible preferred stock was 10:1, except for the Series D-1, Series D-2, and Series D-3 redeemable convertible preferred stock, which were approximately 10.5, 10.4, and 10.5, respectively. As of September 30, 2026 (unaudited), the conversion ratio for all series of redeemable convertible preferred stock was 10:1, except for the Series D-1, Series D-2, and Series D-3, which were approximately 10.6:1, 10.4:1, and 444 10.6:1, respectively. Upon conversion, no adjustments to the conversion price shall be made for any declared but unpaid dividends on the redeemable convertible preferred stock surrendered for conversion or on the common stock delivered upon conversion. • Mandatory conversion – Each share of redeemable convertible preferred stock shall automatically convert to Class A common stock or Class N common stock, as applicable, at the applicable conversion rate upon the earlier of (i) the Company’s sale of its common stock in a firm commitment underwritten public offering pursuant to a registration statement under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, resulting in at least $100 million of aggregate cash gross proceeds to the Company, net of underwriting discounts and commissions, (ii) the Company’s completion of a transaction or series of related transactions (by merger, or consolidation, share exchange or otherwise with a publicly traded “special purpose acquisition company” or its subsidiary), which does not qualify as a liquidation transaction, or (iii) the date, or upon the occurrence of an event, specified by vote or written consent of holders of each of (a) the majority of the then outstanding shares of Series A redeemable convertible preferred stock, Series C-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock, Series D-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock, Series D-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock, Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock, Series F-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock, Series G-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock, and Series H-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock voting together as a single class on an as- converted basis, (b) the holders of a majority of the then outstanding shares of Series C-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock, voting separately as a class, which majority must include the vote or written consent, as applicable, of certain specified stockholders, (c) a majority of the Series D-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock and Series D-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock, voting together as a single class on an as-converted basis, (d) a majority of the Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock, voting separately as a class on an as-converted basis, (e) with respect to the Series F redeemable convertible preferred stock only, a majority of the Series F-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock, voting separately as a class on an as-converted basis, (f) with respect to the Series G redeemable convertible preferred stock only, a majority of the Series G-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock, voting separately as a class on an as-converted basis, and (g) with respect to the Series H redeemable convertible preferred stock only, a majority of the Series H-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock, voting separately as a class on an as-converted basis. Voting The holders of Series A, Series C-1, Series D-1, Series D-2, Series E-1, Series F-1, Series G-1, and Series H-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock shall be entitled to the same voting rights and powers as the holders of the Class A common stock and to notice of any stockholders’ meeting in accordance with the bylaws of the Company, and the holders of Class A common stock and the holders of Series A, Series C-1, Series D-1, Series D- 2, Series E-1, Series F-1, Series G-1, and Series H-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock shall vote together as a single class on all matters. Each holder of Series A, Series C-1, Series D-1, Series D-2, Series E-1, Series F-1, Series G-1, and Series H-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock shall be entitled to the number of votes equal to the number of shares of Class A common stock into which such shares of Series A, Series C-1, Series D-1, Series D-2, Series E-1, Series F-1, Series G-1, and Series H-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock, respectively, could be converted. The holders of Series B, Series C-2, Series D-3, Series E-2, Series E-3, Series E-4, Series E-5, Series F-2, Series F- 3, Series F-4, Series G-2, Series G-3, Series G-4, Series H-2, Series H-3, and Series H-4 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock shall not be entitled to vote and shall have no voting rights, except as required by law or as specifically set forth in the certificate of incorporation, and shall have no right to vote in any election of the Board.

 
445 Redemption The holders of the redeemable convertible preferred stock have no voluntary rights to redeem shares. The redeemable convertible preferred stockholders have liquidation preferences in the event of any Liquidation Transaction (defined, generally, as any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the Company or deemed liquidation event). Although the redeemable convertible preferred stock is not mandatorily or currently redeemable, a deemed liquidation event could constitute a redemption event outside the Company’s control. Therefore, all shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock have been presented outside of permanent equity. The Company recorded shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock issued for cash at their respective issuance price less issuance costs on the dates of issuance. Shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock issued upon conversion of convertible notes were recorded at the fair value of the respective convertible note immediately prior to conversion. The carrying values of the Company’s redeemable convertible preferred stock have not been accreted to their redemption values as the liquidation event is not considered probable of occurring. Subsequent adjustments of the carrying values to redemption values will be made only if and when it becomes probable the convertible preferred stock will become redeemable. Common Stock The Company has one class of capital stock designated “participating common stock” and another class of capital stock designated “Class T common stock.” The class of capital stock designated “participating common stock” is divided into two series, designated “Class A common stock” and “Class N common stock.” The certificate of incorporation, as amended and restated August 27, 2025, authorized the Company to issue up to 8,162.8 million shares of Class A common stock, 5,547.2 million shares of Class N common stock, and 1 share of Class T common stock. The certificate of incorporation, as amended September 17, 2026 (unaudited), authorized the Company to issue up to 10,906.1 million shares of Class A common stock, 7,128.9 million shares of Class N common stock, and one share of Class T common stock. Holders of Class A common stock are entitled to one vote per share. The holders of Class N common stock shall have no right to vote, generally, except as required by law, including no right to vote in any election of the Board, except as required by law. The holders of Class T common stock have no right to vote generally, except as required by law or specifically set forth in the certificate of incorporation. The participating common stock is subordinate to the redeemable convertible preferred stock with respect to dividend rights and rights upon liquidation, winding up, and dissolution of the Company. The Class T common stock is not mandatorily redeemable and does not entitle the holder thereof to receive dividends or any distribution of assets upon the liquidation, winding up, or dissolution of the Company or the occurrence of a Liquidation Transaction (defined, generally, as any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the Company or deemed liquidation event). 446 The total shares of the Company’s common stock reserved for future issuance, on an as-if converted basis are as follows (in thousands): As of December 31, As of September 30, 2024 2025 2026 (unaudited) Series A 485,744 485,744 485,744 Series B 874,304 874,304 874,304 Series C-1 263,972 263,972 263,972 Series C-2 133,617 133,617 133,617 Series D-1 350,128 368,311 370,299 Series D-2 44,438 46,132 46,314 Series D-3 49,993 52,589 52,873 Series E-1 — 636,101 636,101 Series E-2 — 952,819 952,819 Series E-3 — 126,646 126,646 Series E-4 — 153,429 153,429 Series E-5 — 242,436 242,436 Series F-1 — 922,197 922,197 Series F-2 — 207,399 207,399 Series F-3 — — — Series F-4 — — — Series G-1 — — 905,104 Series G-2 — — 839,288 Series G-3 — — 205,629 Series G-4 — — 33,216 Series H-1 — — 776,379 Series H-2 — — 331,103 Series H-3 — — — Series H-4 — — — Shares available under Donation Matching Plan 964,341 964,341 933,698 Stock options and restricted stock units outstanding 1,736,780 2,603,784 2,902,337 Shares available for future issuance 26,547 287,571 502,429 Total shares reserved for issuance 4,929,864 9,321,392 12,897,333 Equity Compensation Plan In January 2021, the Board approved the 2021 Stock Plan (the “Plan”). The service condition for these awards is generally satisfied over a four-year vesting period. The performance condition is satisfied upon the occurrence of an “initial event” which is defined as either (i) a qualifying change in control of the Company or (ii) a listing of the Company’s equity securities on an established securities market (including through a traditional public offering, direct listing, or business combination with a special purpose acquisition company), in each case, on or before the seventh anniversary of the grant date, as further defined in such RSU agreements. If the performance condition is not satisfied within seven years of the grant date, all unvested RSUs are forfeited. As of December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (unaudited), no stock-based compensation expense had been recognized for the RSUs because management determined that it is not probable that the performance condition will be achieved. If management had determined the performance condition was probable of achievement as of December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company would have recognized $671 million and $8.2 billion, respectively, of cumulative stock-based compensation expense as of the respective dates and would have had $5.2 billion and $24.1 billion, respectively, of unrecognized compensation cost that represents the RSUs that have not satisfied the service condition for vesting. As of September 30, 2026 (unaudited), unrecognized compensation cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 2.0 years. Restricted Stock Awards (“RSAs”) In January and February 2021, the Company granted a total of 1,731.3 million RSAs to founders and early employees that vested based on the passage of time (i.e., a service condition). The Company also grants RSAs to certain non-employee service providers. The RSAs are shares of common stock that are issued and outstanding and are subject to repurchase by the Company (for a minimal amount) if the holder’s service terminates before the restricted shares vest. Compensation cost is measured at the grant-date fair value of the underlying common stock and is recognized over the vesting period. During the year ended December 31, 2024, 432.8 million RSAs vested and 36.1 million RSAs were subject to repurchase. During the year ended December 31, 2025, all remaining RSAs subject to repurchase as of the end of the prior year vested and additional RSAs granted and subject to repurchase were not material. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company granted 10.6 million RSAs in connection with acquisitions, substantially all of which remain unvested as of September 30, 2026. As of September 30, 2026 (unaudited), there was approximately $304 million of total unrecognized compensation cost related to unvested RSAs, which is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 2.5 years. Share Repurchases During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company repurchased and immediately retired 27.9 million shares of common stock from certain former and current service providers at a purchase price of $5.61 per share, which was in excess of the then-current fair market value at the time of repurchase. The aggregate fair value of the shares repurchased was $149 million, which was recorded as an increase in accumulated deficit. The excess of the repurchase price over the fair market value of the shares at the date of repurchase was recognized as stock- based compensation expense of $7 million in the consolidated statement of operations. In February 2026 (unaudited), the Company’s Board of Directors approved an offer by a group of third-party buyers to purchase shares of the Company’s Class A common stock at a price of $25.9136 per share from sellers that included current and former employees, non-employee service providers, and donor advised funds. The tender offer closed in April 2026, and an aggregate of 179.9 million shares were sold. Shares sold in the tender offer were sold at fair value, and accordingly, no stock-based compensation expense was recognized in connection with the transaction. Donation Matching Plan In November 2021, the Company adopted its donation matching plan (“Donation Matching Plan”) whereby eligible employees of the Company can pledge to donate to eligible nonprofit organizations, including 501(c)(3) tax exempt organizations, and have the Company match such donation on the terms set forth in the Donation Matching Plan. The Company may elect, at its sole discretion and per the terms of the Donation Matching Plan, to match the donation in shares of Class N common stock or in cash in an equivalent value. As of December 31, 2024 and 2025, 964.3 million shares of common stock were reserved for issuance under the Donation Matching Plan, and no shares are issued or outstanding. As of September 30, 2026 (unaudited), 933.7 million shares of common stock were reserved for issuance under the Donation Matching Plan. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company recognized $2.1 billion within other operating and administrative expense in the consolidated statements of operations for the initial recognition and change in fair value of the donation matching program liability and issued 30.6 million shares of Class N common stock upon settlement of its donation matching obligation in the first quarter of 2026 (unaudited). The Company’s ability to utilize the NOL carryforwards and R&D credit carryforwards in the future may be subject to an annual limitation due to ownership changes that have occurred or that could occur in the future in accordance with Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (“Section 382”), as well as similar state provisions. These ownership changes may limit the amount of NOL and R&D tax credit carryforwards that can be utilized annually to offset future taxable income and future income tax, respectively. In general, an ownership change as defined by Section 382 results from transactions increasing the ownership of certain stockholders or public groups in the stock of a corporation by more than 50% over a three-year period. The Company last completed a Section 382 analysis as of December 31, 2023, and has determined that ownership changes have taken place in October 2021 and September 2023. However, no limitations on the utilization of tax attributes were identified as of that date. A Section 382 study has not been conducted subsequent to December 31, 2023. Ownership changes that may have occurred in 2024 and 2025 may therefore subject tax attributes to a yearly limitation. Legal Matters The Company is involved from time to time in claims, proceedings, and litigation, including the following: In August 2024, various authors filed suit against the Company alleging infringement of copyrighted books in the case of Bartz, et al. v. Anthropic in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California (“Bartz”). The complaint alleged, among other things, copyright infringement related to the use of literary works used in the training of the Company’s large language models. The complaint sought certification as a class action, unspecified amounts of damages, injunctive relief, attorneys’ fees, costs, and interest. The Company reached a settlement in the amount of $1.5 billion and the interest earned thereon, which was approved by the district court in July 2026. The Company paid $300 million during the year ended December 31, 2025 and recorded liabilities of $750 million in accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities and $450 million in other noncurrent liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets as of December 31, 2025, and $450 million in accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities as of September 30, 2026 (unaudited). 458 In October 2023, Concord Music Group et al. filed a complaint against the Company in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee (“Concord I”). The complaint alleges, among other things, that in the process of building and operating the Company models, the Company unlawfully copied and disseminated copyrighted lyrics controlled by the publishers. It also asserts a claim for unlawful removal of copyright management information. The complaint seeks unspecified amounts of damages, injunctive relief, attorneys’ fees, costs, and interest. The case was later transferred to the Northern District of California. Both parties filed motions for summary judgment and the court held a hearing on October 21, 2026. The Company disputes the allegations of wrongdoing and intends to defend itself vigorously in this matter. The Company is also subject to four copyright actions in Canada. In May and July 2025, two putative class actions were filed on behalf of purported classes of Canadian authors - one in British Columbia (“MacKinnon”) on behalf of all Canadian authors, and one in Québec (“Grescoe”) on behalf of all Québec authors - each alleging violations of Canada’s Copyright Act based on the Company’s copying and use of copyrighted books to train its large language models. Grescoe has been stayed pending a final judgment in MacKinnon. In July 2026, La Presse Inc., a Québec news publisher, filed a copyright infringement action against the Company in the Québec Superior Court alleging that the Company reproduced its journalistic works in the data used to train the Company’s models. In October 2026, a group of Canadian news publishers filed a claim against the Company in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice. The plaintiffs allege the Company copied their content from their websites to develop its Claude models. They further allege the Company breached the websites’ terms of service and circumvented technological protection measures. The Company disputes the allegations of wrongdoing and intends to defend itself vigorously in these matters. In June 2025, Reddit, Inc. filed suit against the Company in California state court alleging various claims, including breach of contract and trespass to chattels, stemming from allegations about the Company’s use of Reddit data in building and operating its models. In September 2026, the state court narrowed the case to Reddit’s breach of contract, interference with contract, and unfair competition claims. The Company disputes the allegations of wrongdoing and intends to defend itself vigorously in this matter. Between January and October 2026, several complaints were filed against the Company in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California by various music publishers and their affiliated entities, including Concord Music Group, Universal Music Publishing Group, ABKCO Music, BMG Rights Management (US) LLC, Round Hill Music LP, Sony Music Publishing (US) LLC, Warner Chappell Music, Inc., and others (collectively, the “Music Publisher Matters”). The complaints allege, among other things, that the Company unlawfully copied the plaintiffs’ copyrighted song lyrics and musical compositions, and assert claims for direct and indirect copyright infringement based on both the acquisition and use of copyrighted materials to train the Company’s large language models and the outputs of those models, as well as claims for removal of copyright management information. Certain of the complaints also assert claims for unauthorized downloading and distribution of copyrighted works, circumvention of technological protection measures, and violations of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act, and certain of the complaints also name two Company executives as defendants. The complaints seek unspecified amounts of damages, injunctive relief, attorneys’ fees, costs, and interest. These matters are in preliminary stages. The Company disputes the allegations of wrongdoing and intends to defend itself vigorously in these matters. The Company is subject to several putative class action complaints alleging that it markets and sells subscription plans for Claude through false, misleading, and deceptive advertising practices. These matters are generally in the early stages. The Company disputes the allegations of wrongdoing and intends to defend itself vigorously in these actions. Various authors and publishers have opted out of the class action and settlement reached in Bartz and filed individual suits against the Company, generally alleging claims of direct copyright infringement, contributory copyright infringement, and removal of copyright management information related to the use of literary works used in the training of the Company’s large language models. The Company disputes the allegations of

 
459 wrongdoing in these remaining opt-out actions and intends to defend itself vigorously in all matters. These proceedings remain in various stages. The Company has received notices, demands, and other communications from several authors and individual rights-holders, publishers (including, but not limited to, book, news, and music publishers), platforms and website operators, and trade associations, in the United States and other jurisdictions (collectively, “Rights- Holders”) alleging unauthorized acquisition or use of content, removal of copyright management information, violation of terms of service, and violation of copyrights. Some Rights-Holders have also sought to have their content removed from the Company’s training corpus or sought more information on how their content was used in the development of the Company’s models. Other Rights-Holders have argued that the mere crawling of their sites has harmed them. The Company expects to continue to receive similar notices from Rights-Holders, which may ultimately result in litigation against the Company. The Company disputes the allegations of wrongdoing and intends to defend itself vigorously in these matters. From time to time, the Company is subject to inquiries, investigations, subpoenas and requests for information from federal, state, and foreign governmental authorities, including the U.S. Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general, regarding, among other things, consumer protection, data protection and privacy, and the safety and security of the Company’s products. In addition, from time to time, the Company is subject to claims, litigation, and other proceedings, including potential regulatory proceedings, involving patent and other intellectual property matters, taxes, labor and employment, competition, privacy and data protection, consumer protection, commercial disputes, and services offered by the Company, and other matters. The outcomes of the Company’s legal proceedings and other contingencies are inherently unpredictable, subject to significant uncertainties, and could be material to its operating results and cash flows for a particular period. The Company evaluates, on a regular basis, developments in its legal proceedings and other contingencies that could affect the amount of liability, including amounts in excess of any previous accruals and reasonably possible losses disclosed, and makes adjustments and changes to its accruals and disclosures as appropriate. For the matters the Company discloses that do not include an estimate of the amount of loss or range of losses, such an estimate is not possible or is immaterial, and the Company may be unable to estimate the possible loss or range of losses that could potentially result from the application of non- monetary remedies. Until the final resolution of such matters, if any of the Company’s estimates and assumptions change or prove to have been incorrect, the Company may experience losses in excess of the amounts recorded, which could have a material effect on its business, consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows. Indemnification Agreements The Company enters into standard indemnification agreements in the ordinary course of business. Pursuant to these arrangements, the Company indemnifies, holds harmless, and agrees to reimburse the indemnified parties for losses suffered or incurred by the indemnified party, in connection with any trade secret, copyright, patent, independent testing and evaluation of the Company’s models, or other intellectual property infringement claim by any third party with respect to its technology. These indemnification obligations are not subject to a cap in certain instances. The term of these indemnification agreements is generally perpetual after the execution of the agreement. The maximum potential amount of future payments the Company could be required to make under these agreements is not determinable because it involves claims that may be made against the Company in the future but have not yet been made. The Company has not incurred costs to defend lawsuits or settle claims related to these indemnification agreements. Employee Benefit Plan The Company has a qualified defined contribution plan under Section 401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code covering eligible employees. A portion of employee contributions are matched up to a fixed maximum dollar 460 amount per year per eligible employee. During the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024, and 2025, matching contributions related to the plan were $2 million, $7 million, and $15 million, respectively, and during the nine months ended September 30, 2025 and 2026 (unaudited), matching contributions were $11 million and $35 million, respectively. 14. Segment and Geographical Information The Company’s chief operating decision maker (“CODM”) is the leadership team consisting of the Company’s Chief Executive Officer and President. The Company operates its business in one operating segment and, therefore, has one reportable segment. The CODM utilizes financial information presented on a consolidated basis for purposes of making operating decisions, assessing financial performance, and allocating resources including, but not limited to, the Company’s consolidated net loss. The CODM uses consolidated net loss as the measure of segment profit or loss. The CODM uses consolidated net loss to evaluate overall financial performance, monitor budget-to-actual results, assess the return on the Company’s investments in compute and infrastructure, personnel, and other operating activities to inform decisions regarding the allocation of capital and personnel resources across the Company’s operations. There are no other expense categories regularly provided to the CODM that are not already included in the primary consolidated financial statements, except that stock-based compensation expense is separately provided to the CODM as a discrete component within the Personnel line item. Stock-based compensation expense was $29 million, $192 million, and $1.2 billion for the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024, and 2025, and $591 million and $3.3 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 and 2026 (unaudited), respectively. The CODM does not evaluate operating segments using asset information. Long-lived assets, which consist of property and equipment, net, and operating lease right-of-use assets, by geographic location are based on the physical location of the assets. As of December 31, 2024, December 31, 2025, and September 30, 2026 (unaudited), approximately 94%, 95%, and 98%, respectively, of the Company’s long- lived assets were located in the United States. 15. Business Combinations 2026 Acquisition Activity (Unaudited) On May 18, 2026, the Company acquired Stainless Software, Inc., to advance developer experience and agent connectivity. This acquisition was primarily funded by shares of the Company’s Class A common stock with fair value of $295 million. The total purchase price of $306 million consisted of $12 million cash and cash equivalents, $65 million of intangible assets, $24 million of other net liabilities, and $253 million of goodwill. Goodwill primarily relates to expected synergies and assembled workforce and is not expected to be deductible for U.S. federal income tax purposes. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company completed other acquisition activity for aggregate consideration of $283 million. 2025 Acquisition Activity On December 2, 2025, the Company acquired 100% of the issued and outstanding equity interests of Bun. The acquisition primarily provides additional workforce to support the Company’s developer ecosystem initiatives and has been accounted for as a business combination. The total consideration transferred of approximately $171 million consisted of: $136 million in equity issued, including replacement of equity awards attributable to pre- combination services; a $25 million holdback liability to be settled in shares of the Company’s Class A common stock; and $10 million in cash.

 
461 The fair value of equity issued was determined based on the estimated fair value of the Company’s Class A common stock immediately prior to the acquisition and includes 8.6 million shares of Class A common stock issued to Bun stockholders and a number of replacement options to purchase shares of the Company’s Class A common stock issued to continuing employees that are subject to service-based vesting conditions over a three- year period, of which a portion was attributable to pre-combination services and therefore included within the total consideration noted above. Equity issued excludes 1.6 million shares of Class A common stock held back and not legally issued, which serve as partial security for the sellers’ general representation and warranty obligations. The holdback shares are subject to an 18-month holdback period, after which any remaining shares will be released to the former Bun stockholders, net of any shares necessary to satisfy breaches of the sellers’ general representations and warranties or other post-closing adjustments. The holdback shares were recorded at their acquisition date fair value and classified as a liability within Other noncurrent liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets. The holdback liability will be settled in shares of Class A common stock and is recorded at fair value through its settlement date, with changes in fair value recorded to other income (expense), net on the consolidated statements of operations. The estimate of fair value of the holdback liability used both observable and unobservable inputs, specifically considering the price of the Company’s Class A common stock and the probability of payout at the end of the holdback period. The purchase price was allocated on a preliminary basis to goodwill of $154 million and cash and cash equivalents of $17 million. Goodwill primarily relates to expected synergies and assembled workforce and is not expected to be deductible for U.S. federal income tax purposes. Pro forma results of operations have not been presented because the effects of all acquisitions, individually and in the aggregate, were not material. Acquisition-related costs were expensed as incurred within other operating and administrative expenses on the consolidated statements of operations, and were not material. 16. The lease has a twelve-year initial term contractually commencing in January 2027. In March 2026, the lease was deemed to have commenced for accounting purposes when the landlord made the leased building available for use by the Company to begin tenant improvements. The Company recognized an operating lease right-of-use asset of $200 million and corresponding operating lease liability of $196 million. • In January 2026, the Company modified all stock options outstanding for which the one-year cliff vesting period had not yet been achieved by adjusting the cliff vesting period to be equal to six months. The incremental expense recognized as a result of these stock option modifications was not material. • A portion of the Company’s revenue is derived from contracts with various agencies of the United States Government (“USG”). On February 27, 2026, the President of the United States ordered the USG to stop using the Company’s models and the U.S. Department of War designated the Company as a Supply-Chain Risk to National Security (the “Risk Designation”). The Company may experience material revenue losses or business disruptions attributable to these events. On March 9, 2026, the Company filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California challenging the Risk Designation as unlawful and simultaneously filed a petition for review in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit. The U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California has largely granted summary judgment in the Company’s favor, ruling that the Department of War’s actions were retaliatory acts meant to punish the Company for speech protected under the First Amendment to the United States Constitution and violated the Company’s rights under the Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution, and that the Secretary of War’s Risk Designation, particularly with respect to 10 U.S.C. § 3252, violated the Administrative Procedure Act because they were in excess of statutory authority, contrary to law, and arbitrary and capricious. The defendants have filed a notice of appeal of the preliminary injunction. The D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals, however, in a 2-1 split decision, has denied the Company’s petition for review, ruling that the Department of War’s Risk Designation was proper under Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act (“FASCSA”) Section 4713, and that the Company’s rights under the First Amendment and Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment were not violated. The Company is evaluating its next steps with respect to the D.C. Circuit’s decision. 464 17. Subsequent Events (Unaudited) The Company has evaluated subsequent events for recognition and measurement purposes through November 10, 2026, the date the unaudited interim consolidated financial statements were available to be issued. Equity and Financing Transactions • Subsequent to September 30, 2026, the Company’s board of directors approved grants of approximately 47 million RSUs that vest based on a service-based condition only, generally over four years. The Company is in the process of determining the grant-date fair value of these awards. • In October 2026, the Company issued 28.0 million shares of Class N common stock upon settlement of its donation matching obligation accrued as of September 30, 2026. The liability will be remeasured to fair value through the settlement date in the fourth quarter of 2026. • In October 2026, the Company entered into amendments to the employment agreements of certain executive officers that provide for cash severance, continued health coverage and accelerated vesting of a number of outstanding equity awards upon certain conditions, modifying the executive officers’ outstanding stock options and RSUs. Because the performance-based vesting condition of the RSUs was not probable of being satisfied as of the modification date, the RSUs outstanding are expected to be remeasured at their modification-date fair value. • In October 2026, the Company amended its certificate of incorporation to increase the number of authorized shares of Class N common stock to 7,975.7 million shares, and the Company’s stockholders approved the issuance of up to 846.8 million shares of Class N common stock to a newly formed, wholly owned subsidiary of the Company in furtherance of the Company’s public benefit purpose. • In October 2026, the Company’s board of directors adopted, and its stockholders approved, the 2026 Equity Incentive Plan and the 2026 Employee Stock Purchase Plan, each effective on the day prior to the effectiveness of the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part, with up to 2,950.0 million and 160.0 million shares of Class A common stock, respectively, initially reserved for issuance, subject to annual increases. • On November 9, 2026, the Company’s board of directors modified the service-based vesting condition applicable to approximately 67 million RSUs that would otherwise have satisfied such condition on November 20, 2026, pursuant to their terms, such that the condition will instead be satisfied as of November 19, 2026. Because the performance-based vesting condition of the affected RSUs that have such a condition was not probable of being satisfied as of the modification date, those RSUs are expected to be remeasured at their modification-date fair value. The Company expects the incremental stock- based compensation expense from this modification to be material and is in the process of determining the amount of such expense. • In November 2026, the Company entered into purchase agreements with certain strategic partners, including Google and AMD, to purchase an aggregate of $26.0 billion of the Company’s Class N common stock in a private placement at a price per share equal to the initial public offering price. The purchases are contingent upon, and will occur immediately subsequent to, the closing of the Company’s initial public offering. Google’s $10.0 billion purchase will reduce the amount available under the Google 2026 NPA to $10.0 billion. AMD’s $2.5 billion purchase will reduce its equity commitment under the Hardware Supply Agreement to $2.5 billion upon closing. Compute and Infrastructure Transactions • Subsequent to September 30, 2026, the Company entered into new, and amended existing, lease and commercial arrangements primarily to secure additional compute and infrastructure capacity, with aggregate future minimum payment obligations of approximately $106 billion, some of which are

Description of Business and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies Anthropic, PBC (the “Company”) is a public benefit corporation (“PBC”) incorporated under Delaware law in January 2021. The Company develops and maintains advanced artificial intelligence (“AI”) models and provides its intelligence service through its platform and applications to customers. The Company’s public benefit purpose is to responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. The Company is headquartered in San Francisco, California. Basis of Presentation The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“GAAP”). The Company consolidates its wholly owned subsidiaries over which it exercises control, as well as variable interest entities (“VIEs”) where the Company is deemed to be the primary beneficiary. All intercompany balances and transactions between consolidated entities have been eliminated in consolidation. The consolidated financial statements have been prepared on the same basis as the audited consolidated financial statements as of and for the year ended December 31, 2025, but do not include all disclosures, including certain notes required by GAAP on an annual reporting basis. In the opinion of management, the information contained herein reflects all the adjustments of a normal, recurring nature that are necessary for the fair statement of the Company’s financial position, results of operations, comprehensive loss, cash flows and the changes in equity for the interim periods but are not necessarily indicative of the results expected for the full year or any other period. These unaudited and consolidated financial statements should be read in conjunction with the Company’s audited consolidated financial statements and notes thereto for the year ended December 31, 2025. Changes in Presentation and Reclassification of Prior Periods Certain amounts reported in the Company’s prior period consolidated financial statements have been reclassified to conform to the current period presentation. The Company combined certain captions on its consolidated balance sheets and consolidated statements of cash flows. These reclassifications have been recast for all prior periods presented to conform to the current period presentation. These reclassifications affect presentation only and did not impact total assets, total liabilities, total stockholders’ equity (deficit), total operating loss, net loss, or net cash provided by (used in) operating, investing, or financing activities. Stock Split On September 17, 2026, the Company effected a 10-for-1 stock split of its authorized, issued, and outstanding shares of Class A common stock and Class N common stock. The conversion rate of the Company’s redeemable convertible preferred stock was proportionately adjusted to factor in the stock split. On the same date, the Company also effected a 1-for-1,000 reverse stock split of its authorized and issued shares of Class T common stock. All share and per share information has been retroactively adjusted to reflect the stock split and reverse stock split for all periods presented. Use of Estimates The preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities in the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. Actual results could differ materially from those estimates. Significant items subject to such estimates and assumptions include the determination of the fair value of common stock, valuation of deferred tax assets and the related valuation allowance, the potential outcome of uncertain tax positions that have been recognized in the consolidated financial statements or tax returns, valuation of convertible notes, valuation of goodwill, stock-based compensation, the assessment of useful lives of long-lived assets and intangible assets, contingencies, the valuation of financial instruments, and discount rates for operating and finance leases.

 
475 Concentrations of Risk Significant Customers The Company grants credit to customers in the normal course of business. The table below sets forth concentrations of credit risk with respect to accounts receivables from major customers that accounted for 10% or more of the Company’s total accounts receivable: As of June 30, 2026 December 31, 2025 Customer A 13% 13% Customer C 10% * * Less than 10% of total The table below sets forth concentrations of revenue from customers that accounted for 10% or more of the Company’s total revenue: Three Months Ended June 30, Six Months Ended June 30, 2026 2025 2026 2025 Customer A * 11% * * Customer B * 18% * 18% Customer C 11% * 11% * * Less than 10% of total Other Concentration Cloud compute infrastructure capable of training and serving the Company’s models at scale is available from a limited number of providers. The Company was dependent on certain cloud service providers (“CSPs”) for the substantial majority of its compute infrastructure under long-term hosting and lease agreements. The Company also provides access to its intelligence service through cloud service provider (“CSP”) marketplaces, with CSPs acting as collection agents for the Company in these transactions. Revenue generated from sales through CSP marketplaces to customers represented 47% and 48% of total revenue for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, and 47% and 44% of total revenue for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, respectively. As of June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, net accounts receivable from sales through CSP marketplaces to customers represented 58% and 60% of the Company’s net accounts receivable, respectively. Certain CSPs also hold the Company’s non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock and convertible notes. See Note 7 and Note 8 for further information. Restricted Cash The Company’s restricted cash is classified as noncurrent based on the contractual or estimated term of the remaining restriction and consists of amounts pledged as collateral for the Company’s lease and other contractual obligations. These amounts are restricted from general corporate use and will be released or applied against the related obligations as the underlying conditions are satisfied. Accounts Receivable and Allowances Accounts receivable represent uncollected payments from customers and payments collected by channel partners from customers on the Company’s behalf which have not yet been remitted to the Company. Accounts receivable are recorded at the invoiced amount net of the allowance for credit losses and do not bear interest. The Company monitors collections and payments from customers and maintains an allowance for credit losses for expected losses resulting from the inability of customers or channel partners to make or remit payments. The Company writes off 476 accounts receivable against the allowance when management determines a balance is uncollectible and no longer actively pursues collection of the receivable. Changes in the allowance for credit losses were as follows (in millions): Balance as of December 31, 2025 $ 17 Change in allowance for credit losses 57 Write-off of uncollectible accounts receivable (3) Balance as of June 30, 2026 $ 71 Leases The Company determines if an arrangement is a lease at inception. The Company evaluates the classification of leases at commencement and, as necessary, at modification. The Company categorizes leases with contractual terms longer than twelve months as either operating or finance. Finance leases are generally those leases that allow the Company to substantially utilize or pay for the entire asset over its estimated life. All other leases are categorized as operating leases. The Company leases facilities and equipment under operating and finance leases. The Company determines whether an arrangement is or contains a lease at inception and records lease liabilities and right-of-use assets on its consolidated balance sheets at lease commencement. Where the Company’s leases do not provide an implicit rate; the Company determines its incremental borrowing rate based on the information available at commencement date in determining the present value of lease payments. The determination of the incremental borrowing rate is based on an estimate of the Company’s unsecured borrowing rate, adjusted for tenor and collateralized security features. Lease liabilities are recognized at the present value of the future lease payments at the lease commencement date. ROU assets are measured based on the corresponding lease liability adjusted for (i) payments made to the lessor at or before the commencement date, (ii) initial direct costs incurred and (iii) tenant incentives received, incurred or payable under the lease. The Company does not assume renewals or early terminations of its leases unless it is reasonably certain to exercise these options at commencement. Operating lease cost is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term. Finance lease ROU assets are amortized on a straight-line basis over the shorter of the estimated useful life of the underlying asset or, where title does not transfer at the end of the lease term and the Company is not reasonably certain to exercise a purchase option, the lease term, and are recognized within operating expenses based on the nature of the leased asset. The interest component of a finance lease is recognized using the effective interest method over the lease term and is presented separately from the amortization of the related ROU asset. Operating lease ROU assets and operating lease liabilities are presented separately on the consolidated balance sheets. Finance lease ROU assets are included in property and equipment, net. Finance lease liabilities are included in accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities, and in other noncurrent liabilities. The Company’s lease agreements may contain lease and non-lease components. Non-lease components related to the asset being leased are not separated from the lease components and are accounted for as a single lease component for all existing classes of assets. The Company made an accounting policy election for lease agreements with a term of 12 months or less and does not recognize ROU assets and lease liabilities in respect of those agreements. Any payments related to short-term leases are expensed as incurred. Variable lease payments are expensed as incurred and are mainly composed of utilities, common area maintenance, and other operating expenses. Similar to other long-lived assets discussed above, management assesses operating lease ROU assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of such assets may not be recoverable. Finance lease ROU assets are assessed for impairment together with the Company’s other property and equipment. For leased assets, such circumstances would include the decision to enter into a sublease for which estimated cash flows do not fully cover the costs of the associated lease. The Company measures cash equivalents and short-term investments at fair value. Level 1 instrument valuations are based on quoted market prices of the identical underlying security. Level 2 instrument valuations are obtained from readily available pricing sources for comparable instruments, identical instruments in less active markets, or models using market observable inputs. The estimated fair value of the warrant rights is determined by using a probability-weighted expected return method using valuation inputs based on information available, including terms and features of the warrant rights and other outstanding classes of the issuer’s equity securities, observable transactions in the issuer’s securities, such as its most recent financing round, estimates of equity volatility, and expected time to a liquidity event.

 
481 In March 2026, the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (the “Google 2026 NPA”) with Google LLC (“Google”), which included a commitment to sell 38.6 million shares of the Company’s Series G-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock at $259.1364 per share. In April 2026, the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (the “Amazon 2026 NPA”) with Amazon Web Services Inc. (“Amazon”), which included a commitment to sell 19.3 million shares of the Company's Series G-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock at $259.1364 per share. Refer to Note 7 for further information. These agreements are marked-to-market each period. Changes in fair value are recognized in other income (expense), net on the consolidated statements of operations. Assets under these note purchase agreements are recorded at fair value with other assets, noncurrent on the consolidated balance sheet. The estimated fair value of the note purchase agreements was determined by using a probability-weighted expected return method. The fair value of the Series G-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock was determined by using a hybrid approach comprising a contingent claims analysis (“CCA”) and a common stock equivalent (“CSE”) method. Assumptions included assumptions on future liquidity and financing events, the terms and features of the agreement, weights applied to each scenario, discount rates, applicable risk free rates, the fair value of the Series G-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock, and a discount for lack of marketability. Level 3 liabilities consist of the donation matching program liability (Note 8), convertible notes payable (Note 7), and a holdback liability. There is no current market for these liabilities such that the determination of fair value requires significant judgment or estimation. Changes in fair value measurements categorized within level 3 of the fair value hierarchy are analyzed each period based on changes in estimates or assumptions and recorded as appropriate. The estimated fair value of the donation matching liability represents the current obligation to match employee donations under the Donation Matching Program based on observable and unobservable inputs, specifically considering the price of the Company’s common shares. The estimated fair value of the convertible notes is determined by using a hybrid approach comprising a CCA and a CSE method. The analysis estimates the fair value of the convertible notes based on the probability-weighted present value of expected future investment returns, considering possible outcomes available to the note holder, including conversions to redeemable convertible preferred stock, Class N common stock, and maturity. Assumptions include assumed volatility, time to a liquidity event or financing and the risk free interest rate. Changes in fair value of the convertible notes are recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities in the consolidated statements of operations. The estimated fair value of the holdback liability uses both observable and unobservable inputs, specifically considering the price of the Company’s Class A common stock and the probability of payout at the end of the holdback period. Convertible Notes and Revolving Credit Agreement Convertible Notes The Company has entered into note purchase agreements which provide for the issuance of one or more convertible notes. Google Google 2023 Note Purchase Agreement In September 2023, the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (“Google 2023 NPA”) with Google, for the issuance of convertible promissory notes in an aggregate principal amount of up to $2.0 billion, issuable in three tranches. The Company issued the first tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $500 million in September 2023, the second tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $750 million in September 2024, and the third tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $750 million in September 2025. The notes issued under Google 2023 NPA bore interest at a rate of 10.0% per annum, compounded annually, and payable upon maturity, 48 months after the respective issuance date. The Company also has a commercial agreement with Google for the provision of intelligence service. In connection with the Company’s Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing during the three months ended March 31, 2025, the first and second tranches of notes issued under Google 2023 NPA converted in full into an aggregate of 12.7 million shares of the Company’s Series E-3 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $44.8692 per share and an aggregate of 15.3 million shares of Series E-4 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $50.4779 per share, respectively. The conversion prices reflect contractual discounts to the Series E-1 original issuance price of $56.0865 per share. In January 2026, in connection with the initial closing of the Series G-1 financing, the third tranche of notes issued under Google 2023 NPA converted in full into 3.3 million shares of Series G-4 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $233.2228 per share. The conversion price reflects the contractual discounts to the Series G-1 original issuance price of $259.1364 per share. As of June 30, 2026, no amounts remain outstanding under Google 2023 NPA. Google 2024 Note Purchase Agreement In August 2024, the Company entered into an additional note purchase agreement (“Google 2024 NPA”) with Google for the issuance of a convertible promissory note in an aggregate principal amount of approximately $1.3 billion. Such note bore interest at a rate of 8.5% per annum compounded annually, and, unless earlier converted or repaid, was payable upon maturity in August 2030. In connection with the Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing in the first quarter of 2025, the note issued under Google 2024 NPA was converted in full into an aggregate of 24.2 million shares of Series E-5 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $53.2822 per share, reflecting a contractual discount to the Series E-1 original issuance price of $56.0865 per share. As of June 30, 2026, no amounts remain outstanding under Google 2024 NPA. Google 2026 Note Purchase Agreement In March 2026, the Company entered into the Google 2026 NPA under which, subject to certain conditions, up to $30.0 billion of convertible promissory notes or non-voting common stock through December 31, 2030 may be issued. Non-voting common stock would be issued at the 30-day trailing volume-weighted average price and, to the extent issued, the notes will 486 bear interest at 9.0% per annum compounded annually, payable at maturity, and mature six years after issuance, unless earlier repaid or converted pursuant to the terms of the agreement. In May 2026, Google invested $10.0 billion in the Company’s Series H redeemable convertible preferred stock financing, which reduced the amount available for issuance under the Google 2026 NPA to $20.0 billion. Amazon Amazon 2023 and 2024 Note Purchase Agreements In September 2023, the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (“Amazon 2023 NPA”) with Amazon, for the issuance of convertible promissory notes in an aggregate principal amount of up to $4.0 billion, issuable in two tranches. The Company issued the first tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $1.2 billion in September 2023, and the second tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $3.4 billion in March 2024, reflecting an issuance premium to the $2.8 billion in proceeds received for the second tranche of notes. In November 2024, the Company entered into an additional note purchase agreement (“Amazon 2024 NPA”) with Amazon for the issuance of convertible promissory notes in an aggregate principal amount of up to $4.0 billion, issuable in three tranches. The Company issued the first tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $1.3 billion in November 2024, the second tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $1.3 billion in May 2025, and the third tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $1.4 billion in November 2025. The notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA bear interest at a rate of 8.0% per annum compounded annually and payable upon maturity, and mature ten years after the respective issuance date, unless earlier repaid or converted. The first tranche of notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA bear interest at a rate of 8.5% per annum, compounded annually and payable at maturity, and matures in November 2034, unless earlier repaid or converted. The second and third tranche notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA are each non-interest bearing and mature in May 2035 and November 2035, respectively, unless earlier repaid or converted. The notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA and Amazon 2024 NPA are convertible into non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price equal to the lesser of (i) $20.9280 per share (in the case of notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA) or $50.4779 per share (in the case of notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA), and (ii) the price per share in the Company’s most recent (1) preferred stock equity financing (in the case of the notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA) or (2) qualified equity financing (in the case of the notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA), subject, in each case, to Amazon’s ownership cap, as described below. In connection with certain liquidation transactions, Amazon may, in lieu of converting such notes at the applicable conversion price, elect to receive cash in an amount equal to the outstanding principal amount and accrued but unpaid interest thereon. Pursuant to the terms of Amazon 2024 NPA, the Company may be required to make additional cash payments to Amazon calculated as set forth in Amazon 2024 NPA in connection with certain liquidation transactions. In addition, in connection with an initial public offering, direct listing, or special purpose acquisition company transaction, any outstanding principal amount and accrued but unpaid interest thereon under the applicable Amazon NPA will automatically convert into shares of the Company’s Class N common stock at a conversion price equal to the lower of (i) $2.0928 per share, in the case of Amazon 2023 NPA, or $5.0478 per share, in the case of Amazon 2024 NPA, and (ii) the price per share of the common stock offered to the public in such transaction. Any portion of Amazon’s notes that cannot convert due to Amazon’s ownership cap will automatically convert, subject to Amazon’s ownership cap, into shares of Class N common stock at the close of each fiscal quarter following an initial public offering at a conversion price equal to the lowest of (i) the applicable conversion price set forth above, (ii) the price per share of the common stock offered to the public in connection with such initial public offering, and (iii) the then-current market price of the Company’s common stock based on a ten-day volume-weighted trailing average trading price. The notes issued under an Amazon NPA may also be settled in cash at maturity or, at Amazon’s election, by set- off against amounts Amazon owes the Company under certain commercial agreements with Amazon. Any conversion of the notes issued under an Amazon NPA is subject to Amazon’s aggregate ownership cap, which is waivable at Amazon’s option. If any portion of notes issued under an Amazon NPA cannot be converted without exceeding the ownership cap, the portion that could not be so converted will be re-issued as a non-interest bearing convertible rollover note, with a maturity date that is ten years from the issuance date of such rollover note. Upon the occurrence of certain events of default as specified in the applicable Amazon NPA, the Company may be required, depending on the nature of the event of

 
487 default, to repay in cash the then-outstanding principal amount that has not been converted either (i) in full upon demand of the holder or (ii) in equal installments over a four-year period. In connection with the Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing during the three months ended March 31, 2025, the first and second tranche of notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA were converted into an aggregate of 95.3 million shares of Series E-2 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $20.9280 per share. A portion of the notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA did not convert pursuant to Amazon’s ownership cap, and were re-issued as a non-interest bearing rollover note in an aggregate principal amount of $3.1 billion, maturing in March 2034. The rollover note has substantially identical conversion and repayment terms as set forth above, in each case, subject to Amazon’s ownership cap. In connection with the Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing, the conversion provisions of the notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA were triggered. However, due to Amazon’s ownership cap, none of the notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA converted. As a result, the first tranche was re-issued as a non-interest bearing rollover note with an aggregate principal amount of $1.3 billion, maturing in January 2035 and the second and third tranche remained outstanding. Such rollover note has substantially identical conversion and repayment terms as set forth above, in each case, subject to Amazon’s ownership cap. Subsequently, in connection with the Company’s Series F-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing during the three months ended September 30, 2025, a portion of the rollover note under Amazon 2023 NPA converted into an aggregate of 20.7 million shares of Series F-2 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $20.9280 per share. The remaining balance of such rollover note was re-issued as a non-interest bearing amended and restated rollover note with a principal amount of approximately $2.6 billion, maturing in March 2034. The notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA did not convert in connection with Series F-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing due to Amazon’s ownership cap. In the first quarter of 2026, in connection with the Company’s Series G-1 financing, a portion of the second amended and restated non-interest bearing rollover note issued under Amazon 2023 NPA was converted into an aggregate of 20.6 million shares of the Company’s Series G-3 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $20.9280 per share. The remaining balance of such non-interest bearing rollover note was re-issued as a non-interest bearing amended and restated rollover note with a principal amount of approximately $2.2 billion, maturing in March 2034. As of June 30, 2026, the non-interest bearing amended and restated rollover note remains outstanding. The notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA did not convert in connection with the Series G-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing due to Amazon’s ownership cap. As of June 30, 2026, all notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA remain outstanding with an aggregate principal balance of $4.0 billion. Amazon 2026 Note Purchase Agreement In April 2026, the Company entered into the Amazon 2026 NPA under which the Company may issue, subject to certain conditions, up to $20.0 billion of non-voting common stock or convertible promissory notes. Non-voting common stock would be issued at the thirty-day trailing volume-weighted average price and, to the extent issued, the notes will bear interest at 8.0% per annum, compounded annually and payable at maturity, and mature ten years after issuance, unless earlier repaid or converted pursuant to the terms of the agreement. In May 2026, Amazon invested $5.0 billion in the Company’s Series H redeemable convertible preferred stock financing, which reduced the amount available for issuance under the Amazon 2026 NPA to $15.0 billion. As of June 30, 2026, no non- voting common stock or notes had been issued under the Amazon 2026 NPA. Fair Value Option The Company elected to account for the convertible notes using the fair value option pursuant to Accounting Standards Codification (“ASC”) 825 to eliminate the accounting complexity that would otherwise result from separately accounting for the liability and equity components of the convertible notes under the traditional bifurcation model. Fair value changes related to convertible notes are recorded in change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities in the Company’s consolidated statements of operations (Note 4). The Company recognized losses on the change in fair value of convertible notes of $59.6 billion and $5.1 billion during the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The Company recognized losses on the change in fair value of convertible notes of $72.4 billion and $9.9 billion during the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. There were no changes in fair value attributable to credit risk as of June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025. Derivative Liability In connection with Amazon 2024 NPA in November 2024, the Company recognized a derivative liability representing the subsequent note tranche rights provided by Amazon 2024 NPA ("Amazon 2024 NPA derivative liability"). The Company applied the terms of the subsequent note tranche rights for a written call option and purchased put option scenarios to calculate the fair value of the Amazon 2024 NPA derivative liability. The changes in the fair value of the Amazon 2024 NPA derivative liability were recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities in the consolidated statements of operations. The Company recognized losses on the changes in fair value of Amazon 2024 NPA derivative liabilities of $99 million during the three months ended June 30, 2025. There was no Amazon 2024 NPA derivative liability as of June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025. Revolving Credit Agreement On May 14, 2025, the Company entered into a credit agreement (the “Credit Agreement”), by and among the Company, the lenders from time to time party thereto (collectively the “Lenders”), and Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc., as Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent for the Lenders. The Credit Agreement provides for a senior secured revolving credit facility in an aggregate principal amount of $2.5 billion, with a $400 million letter of credit sublimit. The obligations under the Credit Agreement mature on May 14, 2030, subject to an earlier springing maturity date that is contingent upon the outstanding amount of convertible notes issued by the Company on the date that is 91 days prior to the maturity of such notes. The proceeds of the credit facility may be used for working capital, general corporate purposes, and other lawful purposes. The Company may request borrowings in U.S. dollars or certain other agreed currencies, subject to the terms of the Credit Agreement. Borrowings under the Credit Agreement bear interest at rates based on either the Alternate Base Rate, Term SOFR or other applicable benchmarks, plus an applicable margin. The Company is required to pay commitment fees on the unused portion of the facility and fees in connection with letters of credit. The obligations under the Credit Agreement are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries of the Company and are secured by substantially all of the assets of the Company and the subsidiary guarantors, subject to certain exceptions and exclusions set forth in the Credit Agreement. The Credit Agreement contains customary affirmative and negative covenants, including, but not limited to, restrictions on additional indebtedness, liens, asset sales, investments, mergers, and restricted payments. The Company is also subject to a financial covenant which requires the Company to maintain liquidity of at least $500 million as of the last day of each fiscal quarter. The agreement also includes customary events of default, which, if triggered, could result in the acceleration of amounts due under the credit facility. In September 2025, the Company executed an amendment to the Credit Agreement increasing the aggregate principal amount of revolving credit commitments by $250 million to $2.8 billion. In November 2025 , the Company executed the second amendment to the Credit Agreement, providing incremental revolving commitments of $500 million. Following the second amendment, the aggregate principal amount of revolving commitments total $3.3 billion.

As of June 30, 2026, $78 million of standby letters of credit were outstanding under the credit facility. Common Stock The Company has one class of capital stock designated “participating common stock” and another class of capital stock designated “Class T common stock”. The class of capital stock designated “participating common stock” is divided into two series, designated “Class A common stock” and “Class N common stock”. The certificate of incorporation, as amended and restated May 27, 2026, authorized the Company to issue up to 10,991.0 million shares of Class A common stock, 7,044.0 million shares of Class N common stock, and 1 share of Class T common stock. Holders of Class A common stock are entitled to one vote per share. The holders of Class N common stock shall have no right to vote, generally, except as required by law, 492 including no right to vote in any election of the Board, except as required by law. The holders of Class T common stock have no right to vote generally, except as required by law or specifically set forth in the certificate of incorporation. The participating common stock is subordinate to the redeemable convertible preferred stock with respect to dividend rights and rights upon liquidation, winding up, and dissolution of the Company. The Class T common stock is not mandatorily redeemable and does not entitle the holder thereof to receive dividends or any distribution of assets upon the liquidation, winding up, or dissolution of the Company or the occurrence of a Liquidation Transaction (defined, generally, as any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the Company or deemed liquidation event).
